conflicts.issue: EMC Corporation Workforce Demographics Disclosure on Incentives Agreement (Item 27)
conflicts.summary: While all Council members supported the $1 million EMC Corporation data-center incentives agreement, Howard Clement III sought a formal motion amendment requiring workforce demographic data in closed session, which failed for lack of a second before staff agreed informally to supply the figures.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the EMC incentive agreement as drafted while arranging for staff to provide demographic data separately in closed session.
side_a_arguments: EMC's $70 million investment and 112 city jobs bring critical tax revenue and employment during 8.5% county unemployment.
Attaching a formal amendment is unnecessary because staff agreed to share demographic data in executive session without delaying the incentive.
conflicts.side_b_position: Formally amend the approval motion to require the Workforce Development Director to furnish EMC workforce demographic information in executive session.
side_b_arguments: Council has a nearly quarter-century precedent of reviewing workforce demographics on major incentive deals.
A formal requirement ensures accountability on diversity commitments.
conflicts.resolution: Amendment failed for lack of a second; staff agreed to provide demographic data in executive session and the main motion passed 7-0.

conflicts.issue: Postponement of Mozella Elma McLaughlin Neighborhood Revitalization Fund Contract for Mediation with Notebook Store
conflicts.summary: Council divided 5-2 over whether to postpone action on Mozella Elma McLaughlin's Neighborhood Revitalization Fund contract until October 5 so staff could address pro forma tax/debt-coverage questions and attempt to resolve issues raised by Bruce Bridges' Notebook Store.
conflicts.side_a_position: Postpone decision until October 5 to clarify pro forma debt-coverage figures and seek a joint win-win resolution between McLaughlin and Bridges.
side_a_arguments: Pro forma did not show federal or state income tax expenses when computing net operating income and debt coverage.
Staff needed to respond to Bruce Bridges' letter and encourage the two parties to reach an agreement.
conflicts.side_b_position: Do not tie the two projects together or delay McLaughlin's project.
side_b_arguments: The two projects are mutually exclusive and independent, and the Notebook Store was already accommodated in McLaughlin's pro forma.
Staff had already reviewed the proposal twice and recommended approval; delaying puts Ms. McLaughlin's project at risk.
conflicts.resolution: Motion to postpone to October 5 passed 5-2 (Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown; Nays: Farad Ali, Diane Catotti).

conflicts.issue: Neighborhood Revitalization Fund Contract with Mozella Elma McLaughlin (Item 33)
conflicts.summary: Council split 5-2 on Item 33 following the public hearing on the Neighborhood Revitalization Fund contract with Mozella Elma McLaughlin amid unresolved tensions with Bruce Bridges' Notebook Store and RFP process concerns.
conflicts.side_a_position: Advance/approve the motion on Item 33 while encouraging staff to mediate a win-win arrangement with Dr. Bridges' Notebook Store.
side_a_arguments: Supportive of revitalization efforts in Northeast Central Durham involving McLaughlin, the Notebook Store, and the Clock.
Staff encouraged to continue seeking a win-win resolution between McLaughlin and Bridges.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose the motion on Item 33.
side_b_arguments: Diane Catotti and Eugene Brown recorded dissenting No votes after debate over the RFP process and conflicting business interests.
conflicts.resolution: Motion passed 5-2 (Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Farad Ali; Nays: Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti); the contract later returned for further mediation and Council review in September and October.

conflicts.issue: Timing and Rule Suspension for 2009-2010 Employee Benefits Recommendation (Item 30)
conflicts.summary: Council divided 6-1 over whether to accept the City Manager's priority request to consider suspending rules for a vote on Item 30 (2009-2010 benefits recommendations) at the June 4 work session rather than automatically deferring it to the June 15 regular meeting.
conflicts.side_a_position: Accept manager's priority agenda and evaluate Item 30 after discussion
side_a_arguments: The manager noted that waiting until June 15 would compress the timeline to inform employees after the item had already been held up a cycle.
Council members who were not in the Insurance Subcommittee wanted to hear the presentation first before deciding whether to vote today or carry the item over to June 15.
conflicts.side_b_position: Automatically defer Item 30 to the June 15 regular Council meeting
side_b_arguments: Believed the community is impacted by benefits decisions and preferred voting at a regular full Council meeting on June 15 rather than suspending rules at a work session.
conflicts.resolution: Clement's substitute motion failed on a voice vote, and the main motion accepting the City Manager's priority items passed 6-1 with Howard Clement III voting Nay.

conflicts.issue: Southpoint Professional Center Phase II Major Special Use Permit and Flood-Fringe Development
conflicts.summary: Council divided 5-2 over whether to grant a Major Special Use Permit and companion site plan/floodplain permit for a 30,000-square-foot office building in the NC 54/I-40 flood fringe within the Jordan Lake watershed.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the Major Special Use Permit and companion site plan/floodplain development permit with staff conditions and sand-filter stormwater upgrades.
side_a_arguments: Planning staff confirmed both water quality and floodplain requirements were satisfied with no net adverse impact.
The proposed sand filter system exceeds minimum ordinance standards and equities favored approval.
Wall-repair commitments are incorporated into the final order attached to the site plan.
conflicts.side_b_position: Deny the Major Special Use Permit and require the applicant to return with a rezoning application.
side_b_arguments: Allowing incremental encroachment in flood fringes sets a harmful precedent along Jordan Lake where the city faces $300 million in water quality retrofit obligations.
Repeated negligible impacts accumulate into major environmental and water quality damage.
A rezoning is the more appropriate structural and environmental review mechanism.
conflicts.resolution: Both the Major Special Use Permit and the companion site plan/floodplain development permit passed 5-2 with Diane Catotti and Mike Woodard voting No.

conflicts.issue: Phased Development / Impact Fee Increase vs. Development Review Process Delay
conflicts.summary: Council divided 4-3 over passing Section 2's phased development/impact fee schedule alongside technical ordinance corrections versus setting aside or delaying the fee increase until development-review reforms satisfied business groups.
conflicts.side_a_position: Adopt the full ordinance including the phased fee schedule to fund parks, open space, and road infrastructure.
side_a_arguments: Parks, open spaces, and roads should not be held hostage to the development review reform process.

The fee increase had already been delayed a full year and split into two phases (July 2008 and July 2009) to soften the impact, while infrastructure cost studies justified collecting the full amount earlier.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose adopting the fee resolution as presented rather than decoupling or postponing Section 2.
side_b_arguments: Critics and business/NAIOP stakeholders argued the city's development review system remained inconsistent and had made backward steps alongside partial improvements.
conflicts.resolution: Council adopted the full item including Section 2's fee resolution by a 4-3 vote.

conflicts.issue: First-Phase Development / Impact Fee Increase Timing and Development Review Reform
conflicts.summary: Council split 4-3 over whether to enact the first phase of development/impact fee increases immediately after staff consultations with homebuilders or wait two to three weeks until development-review reforms could be demonstrated to the public.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the first phase of fee increases now as a reasonable compromise aligned with neighboring jurisdictions.
side_a_arguments: Staff engaged in extensive dialogue with the development community and structured a two-phase compromise.
Fee comparisons showed most Durham fees remained lower than Raleigh and Cary (with Cary also increasing fees in July 2008), representing a normal cost of doing business.
conflicts.side_b_position: Delay imposing the fee increase until substantial improvements in the development review process are completed and shown to the public.
side_b_arguments: Mayor Bill Bell argued it was not legally critical to adopt the fees that night rather than two or three weeks later.
Imposing higher fees before publicly demonstrating meaningful development-review improvements created poor public relations and risked unresolved business-community concerns.
conflicts.resolution: Council passed the first-phase fee motion 4-3, with Howard Clement III, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Bill Bell voting No.

conflicts.issue: Timeline for Deferring Utility Extension Agreement (Item 12) and Annexation (Item 33g) Amid Drought Review
conflicts.summary: Following concerns about whether approving annexation and utility extension agreements would obligate Durham to supply water during the drought, Council split 3-4 over whether to defer Items 12 and 33g until late January 2008 or only until December 17, 2007.
conflicts.side_a_position: Defer Items 12 and 33g until January 24, 2008 (second meeting in January)
side_a_arguments: Pressing staff to complete legal and water-obligation review by December 17 places an unnecessary burden on staff over the holidays.
A longer deferral gives staff and Council adequate time to thoroughly research drought and utility obligations.
conflicts.side_b_position: Defer Items 12 and 33g only until December 17, 2007
side_b_arguments: Further delay past December 17 imposes additional financial costs on the applicant, who specifically offered December 17 to try to preserve a December 31 effective date for tax assessment.
Staff and the City Attorney indicated December 17 was achievable and the item could be deferred again then if review remained incomplete.
conflicts.resolution: The January 24 deferral substitute-to-the-substitute motion failed 3-4, after which Council adopted the December 17 deferral and voted 7-0 to continue the Item 33g public hearing to December 17.

conflicts.issue: Historic Landmark Designations Tax Deferral vs. Preservation Value (Items 28-33 / 40)
conflicts.summary: Council debated whether to pause or scrutinize 2009 Historic Landmark Designations on a case-by-case economic basis amid concern over foregone property tax revenue versus preservation incentives, ending in a 6-0-1 vote with Farad Ali abstaining.
conflicts.side_a_position: Preserve and honor completed historic landmark applications while evaluating individual designations rather than scrapping the program.
side_a_arguments: Investors and owners relied on program criteria, surrendered demolition and alteration rights, and completed the full review process.
The program is a strong historic preservation and economic development tool in a city that has lost many historic commercial buildings.
conflicts.side_b_position: Abstain from voting while questioning the fiscal return on investment and case-by-case criteria of landmark tax deferrals.
side_b_arguments: Landmark designations reduce city tax revenue and require rigorous case-by-case economic impact scrutiny rather than automatic approval.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 6-0 with Farad Ali abstaining.

conflicts.issue: Transparency and Community Support for $350,000 St. Joseph's Historic Foundation Contract (Item 16)
conflicts.summary: Council Member Eugene Brown questioned missing background details and past neighborhood concerns regarding the $350,000 Neighborhood Revitalization Fund contract with St. Joseph's Historic Foundation, while Mayor Bill Bell abstained due to UDI CDC's involvement.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the $350,000 catalyst contract with milestone safeguards
side_a_arguments: Project ranked best among nine competitive proposals as a Fayetteville Street economic development catalyst.
Contract disbursements are tied to percentage-of-completion deliverables and close staff project management.
conflicts.side_b_position: Demand clearer staff memos and abstain where organizational ties exist
side_b_arguments: Eugene Brown noted that former board members and charrette organizers raised concerns and criticized the memo for omitting a $14,000 expansion program.
Mayor Bill Bell abstained because UDI CDC is part of the recipient group.
conflicts.resolution: Approved 6-0 with Mayor Bill Bell abstaining.

conflicts.issue: Contract Amendment No. 3, Contract ST-227 (2006 Street Improvements, Item 19)
conflicts.summary: Diane Catotti dissented on Item 19 (Contract Amendment No. 3 for 2006 Street Improvements) when the Consent Agenda was voted, carrying forward her objection from the work session.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve Contract Amendment No. 3 for Contract ST-227 (2006 Street Improvements).
side_a_arguments: Included on the Consent Agenda for approval by the six-member majority.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose Contract Amendment No. 3 for Contract ST-227.
side_b_arguments: Signaled intent to vote No consistent with position stated at the work session.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 6-1 with Diane Catotti voting No.

conflicts.issue: Beer and Wine Privilege License Approvals in Fragile Neighborhoods (Item 11)
conflicts.summary: Council Member Howard Clement III opposed issuing beer and wine privilege licenses despite four establishments being pulled for ABC review, arguing too many alcohol vendors operate in fragile neighborhoods.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the remaining privilege license list while staff and the City Attorney review the four flagged businesses with the ABC board for possible quasi-judicial hearings.
side_a_arguments: Four problematic applicants (Harlem Mini-Mart, El Palenque LLC, Room About 54, and Stop and Go Food Mart) were already pulled for review with local ABC officials.
Staff committed to returning with recommendations within two work-session cycles.
conflicts.side_b_position: Vote against privilege license issuance to protest ongoing vendor concentration in fragile neighborhoods.
side_b_arguments: Too many beer and wine vendors remain located in fragile neighborhoods.
A stronger mechanism is needed to remove bad influences from vulnerable communities.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 6-1 with Howard Clement III voting No.

conflicts.issue: Initial Zoning and Stormwater Runoff Concerns in Falls Lake Watershed (Lake Creek / Sierra)
conflicts.summary: Council debated whether to approve staff's recommended low-density initial zoning or downzone the property after citizen testimony tied the developer/engineer to prior Clean Water Act erosion violations at Ravenstone draining into Falls Lake.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve staff's recommended initial zoning capping impervious surface at 24% under low-density watershed rules.
side_a_arguments: The property owner had not requested a downzoning.
Although the protected watershed tier could permit up to 70% impervious surface, the proposal voluntarily limits development to low density (24% or less impervious surface).
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose approval / favor downsizing due to steep-slope erosion and Falls Lake water quality concerns.
side_b_arguments: Documented sediment and nutrient runoff from the same developer's nearby Ravenstone 1 and 2 projects had remained unresolved for over 18 months.
Phosphorus and nitrogen runoff via Lake Creek contributes to algae blooms in Falls Lake.
conflicts.resolution: Staff's recommendation passed 6-1 with Mayor Bill Bell voting No.

conflicts.issue: Council Position on Proposed National Bio and Agro-Defense Facility (NBAF) and Abstention Authority (Item 39)
conflicts.summary: Council divided over whether to adopt a formal resolution opposing the proposed NBAF alongside accepting the Environmental Affairs Board's report and forwarding unanswered questions, as well as whether Howard Clement III could abstain.
conflicts.side_a_position: Accept the EAB report, forward its unanswered questions, and adopt a Council resolution opposing the proposed NBAF.
side_a_arguments: The EAB report identified substantial unanswered questions and outstanding environmental and safety concerns.
Passing the opposition resolution reflects the unresolved concerns highlighted in items one and two of the motion.
conflicts.side_b_position: Accept the EAB report and forward questions, but do not vote to oppose the facility without complete facts (with Eugene Brown voting No and Howard Clement III attempting to abstain).
side_b_arguments: Council had been placed in a bind by being asked to approve or disapprove the facility without having all the facts.
The Environmental Affairs Board itself recommended deferring action until additional information was obtained.
Eugene Brown requested severing the motion so he could support accepting the report and sending questions while declining to oppose the facility.
conflicts.resolution: The floor vote tallied 5-1 (Eugene Brown No, Howard Clement III attempting to abstain), and at 03:31:36 City Attorney Patrick Baker ruled Clement could not abstain without a conflict of interest and must be recorded as an affirmative vote, resulting in a 6-1 adoption.

conflicts.issue: Gateway Terrace Rezoning and Protest Petitioner Land-Purchase Demand
conflicts.summary: During the Gateway Terrace rezoning hearing, a neighboring protest petitioner urged Council to withhold approval unless the developer purchased an adjacent ~1-acre residential parcel for roughly $350,000, prompting Council members to question whether private real estate disputes belong in zoning decisions.
conflicts.side_a_position: Make a zoning policy decision on the merits without forcing the applicant to buy adjacent private real estate, while referring broader policy questions to JCCPC.
side_a_arguments: The applicant met ordinance standards, agreed to committed elements including a 100-foot buffer along Watkins Road, and had no project use for the extra acre.
Requiring a land purchase would force a brand-new rezoning application and a 9-to-12-month delay.

Council Member Farad Ali questioned whether Council was being asked to intervene in a private business transaction before deciding zoning policy, and Diane Catotti suggested placing the broader issue on a JCCPC agenda.
conflicts.side_b_position: Hold rezoning support pending a land-purchase settlement (~$350,000) to incorporate the adjacent parcel and remove a 25-foot residential buffer.
side_b_arguments: Buying the end parcel represents roughly 1.5–1.7% of the mid-to-upper-teens million budget and would yield additional usable square footage.
A settlement would address neighborhood concerns over potential tenants such as Hooters.
conflicts.resolution: Council voted 7-0 to approve the Gateway Terrace rezoning.

conflicts.issue: Walltown Park Recreation Center CMAR Construction Services Agreement (Item 22)
conflicts.summary: Council approved the CMAR construction services agreement for Walltown Park Recreation Center structural steel detailing, fabrication, and erection by a 6-1 vote, with Council Member Eugene Brown dissenting.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the CMAR construction services agreement to advance the Walltown Park Recreation Center structural steel work while providing a Thursday work-session status report to the community.
side_a_arguments: The Walltown Community Association appreciated the funding and did not oppose negotiating structural steel work so the project could move forward expediently.
The City Manager committed to meeting with Walltown Community Association President Audrey Mitchell and reporting back at the Thursday work session on outstanding community questions.
conflicts.side_b_position: Vote against the CMAR construction services agreement.
side_b_arguments: Council Member Eugene Brown requested that the record note his vote against the measure without elaborating on-mic in the transcript digest.
conflicts.resolution: Item 22 passed 6-1, and the City Manager committed to presenting a status update at the Thursday work session.

conflicts.issue: Relaxation of Townhouse Design Guidelines (Vinyl Siding and Garages) on 33-Acre PDR 6.8 Rezoning
conflicts.summary: Council voted 5-1 to approve a fifth rezoning modifying townhouse design guidelines on a 33-acre parcel, with Mayor Bill Bell dissenting against dropping garage requirements and brick/wood exterior standards.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the revised townhouse rezoning guidelines
side_a_arguments: Allowed the applicant to proceed under modified development standards.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose relaxing previously agreed design guidelines
side_b_arguments: Mayor Bell stated he was disappointed in the request to eliminate garages and switch to vinyl siding on a project he had previously supported.
Public opponent Bob Yensch argued the fifth rezoning weakened design quality solely for the developer's financial benefit and was inconsistent with the comprehensive plan.
conflicts.resolution: Approved 5-1 with Mayor Bill Bell voting Nay and Howard Clement III absent.

conflicts.issue: Historic Preservation Covenants vs. Redevelopment Process for 727 North Mangum Street (Item 20)
conflicts.summary: Preservation advocates urged requiring preservation covenants to prevent demolition of a significant Five Points structure before selling 727 North Mangum Street to UDI Community Development Corporation, while Council and staff maintained the current action only initiated the upset-bid process.
conflicts.side_a_position: Advance the upset-bid sale process to UDI CDC now, with community review and a public hearing occurring later before any $186,000 incentive contract is approved.
side_a_arguments: Approval only begins the upset-bid process (requiring a 10% / $30,000 minimum upset bid) and does not finalize a site plan or incentive grant.
UDI CDC's proposal already states it will restore the building if a structural engineer determines it is structurally sound.
Any future $186,000 economic incentive requires three contingencies, community review, and a subsequent Council public hearing.
conflicts.side_b_position: Require binding preservation covenants with the sale so blight is addressed through renovation rather than demolition.
side_b_arguments: Fighting blight is best achieved by rehabilitating significant existing structures rather than tearing them down.
Surrounding empty lots can accommodate new construction without losing historic fabric.
conflicts.resolution: With Mayor Bill Bell excused, Council voted 6-0 to approve the administration's recommendation initiating the upset-bid sale.

conflicts.issue: Flag-Lot Layout Policy in Zoning Map Change Z07-44 (Item 26)
conflicts.summary: Council divided 5-2 over approving zoning map change Z07-44 after Council Member Mike Woodard criticized the applicant's intended flag-lot layout off Hickory Nut Drive.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the straight rezoning request based on comprehensive plan consistency and UDO standards.
side_a_arguments: Planning staff recommended approval as consistent with the comprehensive plan and noted no subdivision plan was yet before Council.
Staff explained flag-lotting is an existing alternate lotting provision under the UDO for limited frontage situations.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose the rezoning because it facilitates an undesirable flag-lot configuration.
side_b_arguments: Council Member Mike Woodard argued a flag lot with a house facing away from the street along the flagpole portion is bad policy and made the rezoning request untenable.
Without converting the 30-foot corridor to an approved public or private street, legal frontage remained constrained to Hickory Nut Drive.
conflicts.resolution: Item 26 passed 5-2, with Eugene Brown explicitly recorded voting No and the second Nay voter's name garbled in the automated transcript following Mike Woodard's opposition.

conflicts.issue: Water/Sewer Extension Subsidies Without Annexation and Strip Paving Default Policy (Item 14)
conflicts.summary: During the work session, Diane Catotti objected to staff proposals for city cost-sharing on water/sewer extensions without forced annexation and opposed letting residents opt for curb-and-gutter instead of strip paving under Item 14.
conflicts.side_a_position: Maintain flexible case-by-case annexation evaluation with capped homeowner assessments and allow citizens to choose between strip paving and curb-and-gutter when both are feasible.
side_a_arguments: Case-by-case annexation review avoids obligating the city to costly street, stormwater, and service delivery liabilities on unsuitable parcels.
Giving residents an option between strip paving and curb-and-gutter accommodates neighborhood preferences.
conflicts.side_b_position: Require full actual-cost payment (pre-1998 policy) when properties are not annexed and mandate strip paving whenever feasible.
side_b_arguments: In constrained economic times, the city should not subsidize water and sewer extensions for properties it is not annexing.

Strip paving is less expensive and less environmentally detrimental than curb-and-gutter and should be the mandatory policy whenever feasible, effective immediately or January 1 rather than February 1.
conflicts.resolution: Staff agreed to compile total-value cost examples for water/sewer extensions and revisit the strip-paving feasibility policy before regular Council action.

conflicts.issue: Inclusion of Handgun Ammunition ('Bullet') Purchase Restriction in 2009 Legislative Agenda (Item 25)
conflicts.summary: Council members debated whether to include a proposal restricting handgun ammunition sales in Durham's 2009 state legislative package despite lacking a legislative sponsor, draft bill language, or backing from statewide gun-control advocates.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support including the ammunition purchase restriction in the legislative agenda to close a gap in gun violence prevention.
side_a_arguments: Gun violence in Durham is an epidemic crisis requiring local leadership even if state passage is difficult.
People prohibited from legally buying handguns due to criminal records or mental illness can still walk into stores and buy bullets legally.
Urged Council and the Crime Cabinet (meeting in March) to stand behind tying ammunition eligibility to legal firearm purchase eligibility.
conflicts.side_b_position: Question inclusion based on legislative protocol, missing bill sponsorship, and competing budget priorities.
side_b_arguments: Neither the local legislative delegation nor North Carolinians Against Gun Violence (which is prioritizing safe storage, gun-show loopholes, and anti-bullying bills) supports the proposal, and there is no sponsor or drafted legislation.
State-level gun legislation should not distract Council from focusing 'like a laser beam' on the city's $3–4 million current-year budget shortfall.
conflicts.resolution: Deferred for vote at the February 2, 2009 Regular Meeting, with the City Attorney directed to draft simpler language tying ammunition purchases to legal firearm purchase eligibility (speaker attribution in the digest was largely unnamed except a reference to 'what Farad was saying' and Mayor Bell's view that it is a state issue).

conflicts.issue: Whether to Hold a Public Hearing on Planned Adam & Eve Retail Store at Fayetteville Road and NC 54
conflicts.summary: A Council member requested a public hearing in response to over 1,000 residents objecting to the planned Adam & Eve retail store at Fayetteville Road and NC 54, while Mayor Bill Bell and Planning Director Steve Medlin cautioned that the use was permitted by right under Commercial Neighborhood (CN) zoning and could not be overturned by Council.
conflicts.side_a_position: Hold a public hearing so concerned residents can be heard and have the zoning rules explained publicly.
side_a_arguments: Over a thousand area residents have expressed outrage about the planned store in their neighborhood.
Council owes residents a forum to explain the circumstances surrounding the project.
conflicts.side_b_position: Do not hold a formal public hearing that could mislead residents into expecting Council can block or overturn a permitted retail use.
side_b_arguments: The property is zoned Commercial Neighborhood (CN) and the two buildings total under 15,000 square feet, within the 20,000-square-foot limit.
Staff inspected existing stores and determined the retail sale of goods does not meet the UDO or statutory definition of an adult establishment.
Holding a public hearing would raise false expectations when Council lacks legal authority to overturn the use.
conflicts.resolution: Informational discussion concluded with no formal motion or public hearing scheduled.

conflicts.summary: Council split 3-3 for the third time between Marie Baker and David Sokal for a single vacancy on the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission, failing to reach the four-vote majority required to appoint.
conflicts.side_a_position: Appoint Marie Baker to the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission.
side_a_arguments: Three council members cast ballots for Marie Baker.
conflicts.side_b_position: Appoint David Sokal to the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission.
side_b_arguments: Three council members cast ballots for David Sokal.
conflicts.resolution: No appointment made (3-3 tie; individual member ballots were not read aloud in the transcript).

conflicts.side_a_position: Appoint David Sokal to the DOST Commission.
side_a_arguments: Three council members voted for David Sokal.
conflicts.side_b_position: Appoint Marie Baker to the DOST Commission.
side_b_arguments: Three council members voted for Marie Baker.

conflicts.summary: Council split its seven ballots among three candidates for a Housing Appeals Board seat—Mr. Hopkins (3), Mr. Dudley (2), and Mr. Patterson (2)—leaving no candidate with the required four-vote majority.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 19, 2009 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, the Council approved priority scheduling (7-0) and suspended the rules to unanimously pass (7-0) Durham Athletic Park Change Order #4 (Item 12) so subcontractors could be paid, Durham Holiday Parade sponsorship (Item 13), and ARRA street and sidewalk improvement contracts (Items 16 and 17), while emphasizing MWBE participation under Governor's Executive Order #13. During citizens' matters, a resident detailed a $150 cash booting incident and presented a four-city comparison showing Durham's non-consensual towing ordinance lacked fee caps, credit card mandates, and police reporting rules, prompting Council to indicate the Towing Committee should meet. Representatives of Emmanuel AME Church also requested city financial assistance after incurring over $200,000 in stormwater pipe costs and $6,000 in added loan interest. Council closed by confirming two unanimous 7-0 advisory board appointments and setting the next regular meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Priority Items, and Clerk Report on Item 39 Protest Petition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the session to order and recognized the City Manager, who requested rule suspensions on Durham Athletic Park Change Order #4 (Item 12), Holiday Parade sponsorship (Item 13), and ARRA street/sidewalk contracts (Items 16-18), referral back of police in-car cameras (Item 15), and reclassification of Item 24 as consent. After Howard Clement III raised questions about alleged stimulus fraud, Council approved the priority items and the Clerk noted an invalid protest petition on Hope Valley Farms (Item 39).

agenda_items.title: Consent Review and Immediate Votes on Items 12, 13, 16, and 17
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Mike Woodard commended staff for achieving a 12.5% fund balance in the FY09-10 carryover budget report (Item 6), while Habitat for Humanity HOME loans (Item 8) and beer/wine privilege licenses (Item 10) were pulled. Council suspended the rules and voted unanimously (7-0) to approve Durham Athletic Park Change Order #4 (Item 12), Holiday Parade sponsorship (Item 13), ARRA Street Improvements ST-247 (Item 16), and ARRA Sidewalk Construction SW-25 (Item 17), while reviewing MWBE participation on stimulus contracts.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matter: Non-Consensual Towing and Booting Ordinance Reform
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A citizen recounted being charged $150 cash for a parking-lot boot and compared Durham's towing rules ($125 cap plus $25/day storage and $55 no-key fees) against Chapel Hill, Raleigh, Asheville, and Charlotte ($100-$120 caps, 12-24 hour storage grace periods, 50% boot/drop fees, credit/debit acceptance, and immediate police reporting). Staff explained existing ordinance updates targeted rotation tows and noted the Towing Committee would need to convene to address private-lot towing.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matter: Emmanuel AME Church Stormwater Pipe Cost Assistance Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reverend Miles and Brother Emmanuel Brunson of Emmanuel AME Church requested reasonable city financial assistance after paying 100% of stormwater-related work exceeding $200,000, including roughly 350 feet of 42-inch pipe triggered by a neighbor's ponding complaint and $6,000 in added loan interest.

agenda_items.title: Rezoning Schedule Frequency, Board Appointments, and Setting the Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members expressed concern over bundling numerous connected, time-sensitive rezoning hearings onto a single upcoming night and discussed holding rezoning hearings twice monthly when volume warrants. The Clerk reported unanimous 7-0 ballot appointments for Joy Morgan (Human Relations Commission) and Dennis Garrett (Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission), and Council unanimously set the next regular meeting agenda.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 16, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council presented a proclamation honoring the Pauli Murray Project and celebrated national recognitions for Durham's 32nd-ranked Government Green Fleet and its 21st consecutive GFOA Distinguished Budget Presentation Award. Council unanimously approved (7-0) the Consent Agenda (excluding pulled Items 6 and 16), the September 2009 Bid Report (Item 2, 7-0), and street closings on Rowan Street (Item 20, 7-0) and Sycamore Street (Item 21, 7-0). Police Chief Jose Lopez presented the 2009 Third Quarter Crime Report highlighting daytime residential burglaries and smash-and-grab arrests, and Council unanimously approved pulled Items 6 (Clean Energy Durham ARRA energy-efficiency outreach, 7-0) and 16 (Public Works on-call master agreements, 7-0) after Howard Clement III voiced concerns over contractor workforce demographics. All votes at the meeting were unanimous (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pauli Murray Proclamation, and National Fleet/Budget Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order with all seven members present and presented a proclamation honoring civil rights pioneer, lawyer, and historian Pauli Murray and the Pauli Murray Project. Council also recognized Durham ranking 32nd out of 38,000 public fleets for Government Green Fleet and earning its 21st consecutive GFOA Distinguished Budget Presentation Award, while Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden requested a Weed and Seed status update and a memorial resolution for Patricia Diane Elliott-Riley-Amity.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Items 6 and 16)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved Consent Agenda items including minutes, Taser X26 devices (Item 3), street acceptances (Item 5), water/sewer bond reimbursement resolution (Item 8), General Services bundle phase 2 CMR amendment (Item 9), HUD cooperative grant (Item 10), 2010 Council schedule (Item 11), Hollow Rock master plan (Item 12), bicycle/pedestrian commission interlocal agreement (Item 15), and recycling grant (Item 17), while pulling Items 6 and 16.

agenda_items.title: Item 2: Bid Report (September 2009) and Workforce Demographics Inquiry
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Howard Clement III reiterated concerns about contractor workforce demographics on city bids, and City Attorney Patrick Baker repeated legal limitations previously discussed at work session. Council approved the September 2009 Bid Report.

agenda_items.title: Item 19: 2009 Third Quarter Police Department Crime Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Jose Lopez reported that 2009 property crime increases were driven by daytime residential burglaries (80%) and commercial smash-and-grab break-ins, though auto thefts declined, suspect Anthony Suggs was arrested, and property crime clearance rates exceeded FBI national averages for peer cities. Council commended National Night Out recognition and inquired about mapping where offenders reside.

agenda_items.title: Items 20 and 21: Street Closings (Rowan Street and Sycamore Street)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported no adverse impacts for permanent street closings of 60.03 linear feet of Rowan Street (Item 20) and 203.38 linear feet of Sycamore Street requested by Freeman Ledbetter (Item 21). With no public speakers, Council closed both public hearings and approved each closing.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Items 6 (Clean Energy Durham ARRA Contract) and 16 (Public Works On-Call Agreements)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public comment by Victoria Peterson on Item 6, staff explained Clean Energy Durham's ARRA energy-efficiency outreach contract would involve a neighborhood selection group and $24,000 in workforce-development contractor training; Council approved Item 6 (7-0). Howard Clement III then noted he pulled Item 16 (Public Works on-call master agreements) due to longstanding workforce demographic concerns with a repeat contractor before Council approved Item 16 (7-0) and closed with a call by Farad Ali to support NCCU's Rose Bowl Parade fundraising.

votes.discussion_detail: Permanent street closing of 60.03 linear feet of Rowan Street after public hearing.

votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Permanent street closing of 203.38 linear feet of Sycamore Street requested by Freeman Ledbetter.

votes.notes: Passed 7-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 5, 2009 City Council Work Session—opened by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden while Mayor Bill Bell was arriving and subsequently chaired by Mayor Bell—Council unanimously approved priority items referring stormwater code revisions (Item 4) back to staff and suspended the rules to approve the sale of 521 Eastway Avenue (Item 7). Staff briefed Council on Durham Performing Arts Center financial performance, the citizen-based 'We Care' employee recognition feature, Clean Energy Durham's $314,000 ARRA grant (Item 6), and the Hollow Rock master plan (Item 12, reiterating no city development or management obligation). Policy disagreements emerged during review of water/sewer extension cost-sharing and strip paving (Item 14), where Diane Catotti challenged subsidizing non-annexed properties and urged making strip paving the default over curb and gutter, before Council reviewed Rolling Hills/Southside redevelopment plans (Item 18) and set the next meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Priority Items, Blue Cross Inquiry, and Election Turnout Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden opened the work session until Mayor Bill Bell arrived, and Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (referring Item 4 back to Public Works, suspending rules for Item 7, and scheduling Rolling Hills, DPAC, and We Care updates). Howard Clement III followed up on Blue Cross Blue Shield claim denial records and Council remarked on the roughly 8.8% municipal general election turnout.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Rule-Suspension Approval of Item 7 (521 Eastway Avenue Sale)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent and public hearing items (Items 3-21) and suspended the rules to unanimously approve Item 7, the proposed sale of property at 521 Eastway Avenue.

agenda_items.title: DPAC Financial Update, 'We Care' Recognition Video, and Clean Energy Durham (Item 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reginald Johnson presented a Durham Performing Arts Center press release and initial-period figures, followed by a preview of the citizen-based 'We Care' employee recognition video. Council then questioned Clean Energy Durham's capacity to manage a $314,000 ARRA grant (Item 6), with Sustainability Manager Tobin Freid citing the executive director's 20 years of grant experience and Northeast Central Durham workshops.

agenda_items.title: Hollow Rock Master Plan (Item 12), Water/Sewer Extensions, and Strip Paving Policy (Item 14)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council emphasized that adopting the Hollow Rock master plan (Item 12) commits Durham to zero development or management costs, leaving management to Durham and Orange counties. Diane Catotti challenged city cost-sharing on water/sewer extensions for non-annexed properties and argued on Item 14 that less expensive, environmentally preferable strip paving should be the city's default policy whenever feasible rather than giving citizens the curb-and-gutter option.

agenda_items.title: EOEA Bid Review, Item 18 Rolling Hills/Southside Presentation, and Setting the Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff confirmed Equal Opportunity/Equity Assurance sign-off on bid awards, and presenters outlined Rolling Hills/Southside connectivity plans and accelerated community charrettes at Hayti Heritage Center (including daytime hours for night-shift workers) ahead of the budget cycle. Council set the next agenda with Consent Items 1, 3, 5, 6, 8-12, and 15-17, GBA Items 2 and 19, and Public Hearings 20 and 21.

votes.notes: Presided over by Cora Cole-McFadden before Mayor Bell's arrival; passed by voice vote without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion accepting the City Manager's priority items (referring Item 4 back to Public Works, suspending rules for Item 7, and scheduling Item 18, DPAC, and We Care).

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules for Item 7 (Sale of Property at 521 Eastway Avenue)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to suspend the rules for immediate vote on the proposed sale of 521 Eastway Avenue.

votes.item_title: Approve Item 7: Proposed Sale of Property at 521 Eastway Avenue
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approval of the proposed sale of city-owned property at 521 Eastway Avenue.

disagreements.issue: Water/Sewer Extension Subsidies Without Annexation and Strip Paving Default Policy (Item 14)
disagreements.summary: During the work session, Diane Catotti objected to staff proposals for city cost-sharing on water/sewer extensions without forced annexation and opposed letting residents opt for curb-and-gutter instead of strip paving under Item 14.
disagreements.side_a_position: Maintain flexible case-by-case annexation evaluation with capped homeowner assessments and allow citizens to choose between strip paving and curb-and-gutter when both are feasible.
side_a_arguments: Case-by-case annexation review avoids obligating the city to costly street, stormwater, and service delivery liabilities on unsuitable parcels.
Giving residents an option between strip paving and curb-and-gutter accommodates neighborhood preferences.
disagreements.side_b_position: Require full actual-cost payment (pre-1998 policy) when properties are not annexed and mandate strip paving whenever feasible.
side_b_arguments: In constrained economic times, the city should not subsidize water and sewer extensions for properties it is not annexing.

Strip paving is less expensive and less environmentally detrimental than curb-and-gutter and should be the mandatory policy whenever feasible, effective immediately or January 1 rather than February 1.
disagreements.resolution: Staff agreed to compile total-value cost examples for water/sewer extensions and revisit the strip-paving feasibility policy before regular Council action.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 2, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council proclaimed November 2009 Epilepsy Awareness Month, recognized the second graduating class of the city's in-house backhoe training program, and unanimously approved the Consent Agenda (7-0). Council held a public hearing on voluntary annexations for Primrose School and SecureCare Properties (Item 26) and unanimously approved both the Crutchfield/Duke Street right-of-way closing (Item 34, 7-0) and the 10-Year Solid Waste Management Plan update (Item 35, 7-0). A notable split occurred on the 2009 Historic Landmark Designations (Items 28-33 and 40) after debate over the tax-revenue cost versus preservation value of historic tax deferrals: Council passed the motion 6-0 with one abstention—Ayes from Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, and Diane Catotti, and an Abstention from Farad Ali.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Epilepsy Awareness Proclamation, and Backhoe Training Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order with all seven Council members present, proclaimed November 2009 Epilepsy Awareness Month with the Durham Epilepsy Support Team, and Public Works Director Katie Kalb recognized street and water/sewer maintenance staff graduating from the second 48-hour in-house backhoe training class alongside IMPACT cleanup efforts in Old Five Points.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to approve the City Manager's priority items (adding material to Item 14 on deferred facilities maintenance and advancing Supplemental Item 40 ahead of the historic landmark hearings) and voted 7-0 to approve the Consent Agenda (Items 2-6, 12-15, 17-23, 39, and public-hearing referrals 26-35).

agenda_items.title: Item 26: Voluntary Annexation Petitions (Primrose School and SecureCare Properties)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented two voluntary annexation petitions effective December 31, 2009—Primrose School at 4527 Hope Road and SecureCare Properties at 5014 Durham-Chapel Hill Boulevard—reporting positive net fiscal gains at build-out. Primrose School representatives spoke in support of expanding to a second Durham location before the hearing closed and a motion was put to a vote.

agenda_items.title: Items 28-33 and 40: 2009 Historic Landmark Designations Debate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Preservationists and property representatives (including Cynthia De Miranda) urged Council not to table completed landmark applications such as Liberty Warehouse, stressing the program's preservation value and property-rights restrictions. disagreements.issue: Historic Landmark Designations Tax Deferral vs. Preservation Value (Items 28-33 / 40)
disagreements.summary: Council debated whether to pause or scrutinize 2009 Historic Landmark Designations on a case-by-case economic basis amid concern over foregone property tax revenue versus preservation incentives, ending in a 6-0-1 vote with Farad Ali abstaining.
disagreements.side_a_position: Preserve and honor completed historic landmark applications while evaluating individual designations rather than scrapping the program.
side_a_arguments: Investors and owners relied on program criteria, surrendered demolition and alteration rights, and completed the full review process.
The program is a strong historic preservation and economic development tool in a city that has lost many historic commercial buildings.
disagreements.side_b_position: Abstain from voting while questioning the fiscal return on investment and case-by-case criteria of landmark tax deferrals.

disagreements.resolution: Passed 6-0 with Farad Ali abstaining.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 19, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council presented a National Massage Therapy Awareness Week proclamation and unanimously approved the Consent Agenda (7-0, excluding pulled Item 14). On Item 27, Council approved a $1 million seven-year economic development incentive agreement with EMC Corporation for a $70 million, 112-city-job data center (7-0) after Howard Clement III's amendment to require corporate workforce demographic data failed for lack of a second and Mayor Bell arranged for staff to supply the demographics to Council in closed session. Council also unanimously passed (7-0) UDO historic landmark criteria revisions (Item 28), initial zoning for 412.88 annexed acres on Page Road (Item 29), the 2009 Comprehensive Plan Evaluation and Assessment Report (Item 30), and a lease extension for Hickstown Elementary School Auditorium (Item 14), alongside three advisory board ballot appointments (Russell Strowell 4 votes, Hope Murdoch 6 votes, David Salkal 5 votes; individual member ballots were not read aloud).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Proclamations, and Community Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order with all seven members present, proclaimed National Massage Therapy Awareness Week, and heard updates on moving a community event into partnership on NCCU's campus and a $3.2 million 2005 bond park project scheduled for August 2010 completion.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Item 14 and General Business Ballot Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the Consent Agenda (including annexation hearing settings, minutes, street and water/sewer contracts, Gang Resistance Education and Training grant, and highway safety grants) while holding ballot appointments (3B, 4B) until tallying and pulling Item 14.

agenda_items.title: Item 27: EMC Corporation Economic Development Incentives Agreement ($70M Data Center)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic and Workforce Development Director Kevin Dick presented a $1 million seven-year incentive package offsetting electricity rates for EMC Corporation's $70 million data center creating 112 city jobs (292 countywide), projecting $385,000 in average annual net new revenue during years 1-7 and a 7.7:1 20-year return. Howard Clement III moved an amendment requiring staff to provide corporate workforce demographics in closed session; after no member seconded the amendment, staff agreed to share the data in closed session and Council approved the agreement 7-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 (amendment died for lack of second)

agenda_items.title: Item 28: UDO Text Amendment on Historic Landmark Criteria
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Lisa Miller presented UDO revisions incorporating National Register criteria directly into the ordinance, emphasizing local Durham significance, and requiring designated properties to be distinct from the general historic fabric. With no public speakers, Council approved the text amendment.

agenda_items.title: Item 29: Initial Zoning Map Change (Page II Initial, 412.88 Acres)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Steve Medlin presented initial zoning (Industrial Light, Commercial Center, and Residential Rural with a development plan) for 412.88 recently annexed acres in the suburban tier, recommended unanimously by the Planning Commission. With no public speakers, Council approved the initial zoning.

agenda_items.title: Item 30: Comprehensive Plan Amendment (2009 Evaluation and Assessment Report)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Joe Carley presented the 2009 Evaluation and Assessment Report (A090005), noting a 100% response rate across 542 policies, Future Land Use Map rectification with three county plan amendments, one policy deletion, and seven policy language amendments. With no public speakers, Council approved the EAR.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Item 14 (Hickstown Elementary Lease Extension) and Board Ballot Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved Item 14, extending the lease and purchase option on the Hickstown Elementary School Auditorium at the property owner's request to satisfy HUD refinancing requirements (7-0). The Clerk then reported ballot appointments for the Capital Program Advisory Committee (Russell Strowell, 4 votes), Recreation Advisory Commission (Hope Murdoch, 6 votes), and Durham Open Space and Trails Commission (David Salkal, 5 votes).

votes.notes: Passed 7-0.

disagreements.issue: EMC Corporation Workforce Demographics Disclosure on Incentives Agreement (Item 27)
disagreements.summary: While all Council members supported the $1 million EMC Corporation data-center incentives agreement, Howard Clement III sought a formal motion amendment requiring workforce demographic data in closed session, which failed for lack of a second before staff agreed informally to supply the figures.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the EMC incentive agreement as drafted while arranging for staff to provide demographic data separately in closed session.
side_a_arguments: EMC's $70 million investment and 112 city jobs bring critical tax revenue and employment during 8.5% county unemployment.
Attaching a formal amendment is unnecessary because staff agreed to share demographic data in executive session without delaying the incentive.
disagreements.side_b_position: Formally amend the approval motion to require the Workforce Development Director to furnish EMC workforce demographic information in executive session.
side_b_arguments: Council has a nearly quarter-century precedent of reviewing workforce demographics on major incentive deals.
A formal requirement ensures accountability on diversity commitments.
disagreements.resolution: Amendment failed for lack of a second; staff agreed to provide demographic data in executive session and the main motion passed 7-0.

Council heard presentations from Durham's Partnership for Children on birth-to-five literacy and park strategies and from Water Management on the Water and Sewer Capital Improvement Program ($130 million of $135 million in prior bond funds committed or completed, potential future revenue bonds, and staying in normal irrigation status rather than Stage 1 drought restrictions). On the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission appointment (Item 34), a 3-3 split ballot occurred for the third time between Marie Baker (3 votes) and David Sokal (3 votes), leaving the vacancy unfilled because neither reached the required four votes (individual council member ballots were not read aloud in the transcript). Council unanimously set the next regular agenda and entered closed session for legal consultations (including Haskell Properties et al. v. City of Durham) and appointee performance evaluations with no salary increases.

agenda_items.title: City Manager and City Attorney Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager pulled Item 13 (condemnation of 8114 and 8117 Massie Chapel Road) for presentation, scheduled timed presentations for Items 23-26, requested rule suspension to vote on Item 33 (600 Eastway Avenue / Eastway Village), added Item 34 (DOST appointment), and deferred Item 35 (employment-related medical services) to October 22. The City Attorney requested two closed sessions under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) regarding an administrative procedure and Haskell Properties et al. v. City of Durham.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Sale of 600 Eastway Avenue and Eastway Village Closing Cost Assistance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff requested immediate action on the sale of city-owned property at 600 Eastway Avenue and an increase in closing cost assistance for the remaining seven properties in Eastway Village. Council voted to suspend the rules and then approved the item as outlined.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Condemnation of 8114 and 8117 Massie Chapel Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff briefed Council on two parcels (8114 and 8117 Massie Chapel Road, parcels 144333 and 144336) owned by the same party with an access area and explained the easement required. The item was subsequently placed on the consent agenda for the next regular meeting.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presenters noted that over 20,000 children ages 0-5 live in Durham County and nearly half reside in low-income families. agenda_items.discussion_summary: A community speaker expressed frustration with procedural red tape hindering grassroots applicants seeking Community Development funding, while thanking Director Mike Burrows for maintaining an open door.

agenda_items.title: Water and Sewer CIP Projects and Water Conditions Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained how $20 million in GO bonds for critical water and sewer projects are repaid via enterprise water and sewer fees rather than property taxes, with future debt likely issued as revenue bonds. Staff reported Durham County remained abnormally dry, noted that June 1 alternate-day irrigation kept peak summer demand below 36 MGD, recommended holding off on Stage 1 restrictions, updated Council on Jordan Lake allocation modeling with Triangle J, and reported ~$130 million of $135 million in prior bond funds committed or completed.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Rolling Hills/Southside Revitalization Initiative
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the September 24, 2009 Special City Council Meeting to order for staff and developer McCormick Baron Salazar to present next steps on the expanded Rolling Hills / South of 147 (Southside) revitalization planning effort. Community Development staff outlined a $745,000 community planning budget ($65,000 Fannie Mae grant plus $680,000 in housing bond program income, adding $355,000 to the prior $325,000), a critical-path land survey, traffic impact analysis, and May 2010 rezoning deadline for a NC Housing Finance Agency tax-credit application. Council questioned McCormick Baron Salazar on its inability to raise the originally anticipated $325,000 planning match, rental-first phasing (100% rental in phases 1-2 before introducing for-sale housing), and Steering Committee governance, while the developer committed to repaying ~$300,000-$325,000 of the city's planning investment from Phase 1 and 2 closing budgets if projects advance. Council unanimously approved the immediate $65,000 Fannie Mae planning grant expenditure and deferred the additional $355,000 housing bond authorization and pre-development amendment to the October 5 regular meeting.

agenda_items.title: Southside / Rolling Hills Planning Scope, Budget, and Critical Path
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield, Community Development Director Mike Burrows, Assistant Director Larry Jarvis, and Carl Schlocker presented the expanded Southside neighborhood planning scope and $745,000 budget. Staff highlighted immediate needs for a land survey (30-40 days) and a traffic impact analysis to support rezoning by May 2010 ahead of a state Housing Finance Agency application.

agenda_items.title: McCormick Baron Salazar Financing, Repayment Commitment, and Pre-Development Terms
agenda_items.discussion_summary: McCormick Baron Salazar detailed tax-credit equity challenges, recent stimulus awards on other national projects, and a commitment to return $300,000-$325,000 to Durham from Phase 1 and 2 closing development budgets if the project moves forward. Council members probed why the developer had not raised its $325,000 match, how rental versus for-sale percentages would evolve across phases, and how Council and the Steering Committee would oversee the process.

agenda_items.title: Authorization of $65,000 Fannie Mae Planning Grant Expenditure
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council acted on the immediate request to authorize spending $65,000 in Fannie Mae grant funds for surveying and planning costs under the existing McCormick Baron Salazar pre-development agreement, leaving the $355,000 housing bond authorization and contract amendment for October 5.

votes.item_title: Authorize Expenditure of $65,000 Fannie Mae Planning Grant Funds for Rolling Hills/Southside Surveying and Planning
votes.notes: Voice vote; additional $355,000 housing bond request slated for October 5 regular meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: Authorized spending $65,000 in Fannie Mae grant funds under the existing McCormick Baron Salazar agreement for immediate land surveying and planning costs.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presided over the September 21, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting, opening with DPR Play More Day proclamations and memorial resolutions honoring former City Manager Israel Harding Hughes, Jr. and retired Fire Chief Nathaniel Lewis Thompson. Council unanimously (7-0) approved the City Manager's priority items (moving Item 17 on general obligation bond refunding to the General Business Agenda and referring Item 22 on recreation center construction management back to staff) and granted Councilman Farad Ali an upcoming excused absence (7-0). On the Neighborhood Revitalization Fund contract involving Mozella Elma McLaughlin and Bruce Bridges' Notebook Store, Council split 5-2 to postpone the decision until October 5 so staff could address Mayor Bell's pro forma tax/debt-coverage questions and seek a joint resolution between McLaughlin and Bridges, with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, and Eugene Brown voting Aye and Farad Ali and Diane Catotti voting Nay. Council also approved Item 13 (prior-year grant accounting cleanup for HOME, CDBG, and Emergency Shelter Grants) following public questioning by Victoria Peterson.

agenda_items.title: DPR Play More Day Proclamation and Memorial Resolutions for Israel Harding Hughes, Jr. and Nathaniel Lewis Thompson
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council proclaimed September 25, 2009 as DPR Play More Day and presented memorial resolutions honoring former Durham City Manager Israel Harding Hughes, Jr. (1963-1977) and retired Fire Chief Nathaniel Lewis Thompson (38 years, 9 months of service), accepted by their families.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Item 17 GO Bond Refunding & Item 22 Rec Center CMR) and Ali Excused Absence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested moving Item 17 (refunding GO bond series 1998, 1999, 2000B, 2002, and 2004) to the General Business Agenda for formal adoption and referring Item 22 (Recreation Centers construction manager at risk amendment) back to General Services. Councilman Farad Ali also requested an excused absence to attend the Congressional Black Caucus Education press conference.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Revitalization Fund Contract (Mozella Elma McLaughlin / Notebook Store)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated the Neighborhood Revitalization Fund proposal involving Mozella Elma McLaughlin and Bruce Bridges' Notebook Store. Mayor Bell questioned why the pro forma omitted federal and state income taxes in calculating net operating income and debt coverage, while Councilman Clement moved to postpone until October 5 to obtain staff answers and foster mediation between McLaughlin and Bridges; Councilman Ali objected that tying the two projects together unfairly risked Ms. McLaughlin's project.

agenda_items.title: Prior Years Grant Funding Cleanup (HOME, CDBG, and Emergency Shelter Grant)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson questioned why three grant programs were bundled and asked how much unspent money remained from grants dating back to 1999-2000. Mayor Bell and staff explained Item 13 was solely a technical accounting budget ordinance cleanup unrelated to her separate information request.

votes.discussion_detail: Moved Item 17 (GO bond refunding) to GBA and referred Item 22 (Rec Centers CMR amendment) back to administration.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved excused absence for Farad Ali to attend Congressional Black Caucus event.

votes.item_title: Postpone Neighborhood Revitalization Fund Contract (Mozella Elma McLaughlin) to October 5, 2009
votes.notes: Split vote 5-2; Farad Ali and Diane Catotti explicitly recorded as voting No.
votes.discussion_detail: Postponed decision one cycle until October 5 to allow staff to answer Mayor Bell's pro forma tax and debt-coverage questions, respond to Bruce Bridges' letter, and encourage the two parties to work out an arrangement.

votes.item_title: Item 13: Prior Years Grant Funding Cleanup (HOME, CDBG, Emergency Shelter Grant)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved accounting budget authorization adjustments for prior-year federal housing/community development grants.

disagreements.issue: Postponement of Mozella Elma McLaughlin Neighborhood Revitalization Fund Contract for Mediation with Notebook Store
disagreements.summary: Council divided 5-2 over whether to postpone action on Mozella Elma McLaughlin's Neighborhood Revitalization Fund contract until October 5 so staff could address pro forma tax/debt-coverage questions and attempt to resolve issues raised by Bruce Bridges' Notebook Store.
disagreements.side_a_position: Postpone decision until October 5 to clarify pro forma debt-coverage figures and seek a joint win-win resolution between McLaughlin and Bridges.
side_a_arguments: Pro forma did not show federal or state income tax expenses when computing net operating income and debt coverage.
Staff needed to respond to Bruce Bridges' letter and encourage the two parties to reach an agreement.
disagreements.side_b_position: Do not tie the two projects together or delay McLaughlin's project.
side_b_arguments: The two projects are mutually exclusive and independent, and the Notebook Store was already accommodated in McLaughlin's pro forma.
Staff had already reviewed the proposal twice and recommended approval; delaying puts Ms. McLaughlin's project at risk.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to postpone to October 5 passed 5-2 (Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown; Nays: Farad Ali, Diane Catotti).

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden opened and chaired the September 10, 2009 City Council Work Session (with Mayor Bill Bell participating later in the session). Council unanimously approved priority items, entered closed-session schedules for lawsuits (Marvin Martin, Evans, McFadden, and Carrington cases), suspended rules to appoint NCLM and National League of Cities voting delegates, and unanimously adopted Item 24, a resolution opposing electricity rate increases for senior staff to present at the NC Utilities Commission hearing that evening. Council also received a Water Shortage Response Plan update and reviewed consent items including Downtown Renovation Phase II, T-Mobile tower licensing, and Primrose School water extensions. Under Citizens Matters (Item 38), Morehead Hill residents protested Healthy Start Academy's plan to demolish two 1930s Jackson Street bungalows; after Planning Director Steve Medlin explained the city lacked legal authority to deny a demolition permit once the Historic Preservation Commission's one-year delay expired, Council unanimously approved directing staff to summon Healthy Start Academy's president and board to explain their intentions and requested advance notice of any demolition permit application.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presided over the September 8, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting with all seven council members present, and every formal vote passed unanimously (7-0). Council adopted the consent agenda (excluding pulled Items 8, 17, and 44) and heard Police Chief Jose Lopez present the redesigned Second Quarter 2009 Crime Report, noting a 16% drop in robberies alongside rising residential daytime and commercial smash-and-grab burglaries. In public hearings, Council approved a development/stormwater item 7-0 and voted 7-0 on motions by Councilwoman Diane Catotti to continue Plan Amendment A080001 and Zoning Map Change Z07-47 (Eno Drive at West Point on the Eno) for six months until March 2010 so NC State Parks could continue land-preservation negotiations. Council then voted 7-0 on each of pulled Items 8 (ARRA contract amendment with Durham Management Solutions), 17 (2008 Byrne Justice Assistance Grant amendment), and 44 (CDBG contract with Edgemont Neighborhood LLC for 702 Wall Street) after addressing procurement, crime-funding, and local-hiring questions from resident Victoria Peterson.

agenda_items.title: Childhood Cancer Awareness Month Proclamation and Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell proclaimed Childhood Cancer Awareness Month and noted ceremonial items without public guests would shift to the end of meetings. Council approved the consent agenda covering annexations, Duke Energy contamination agreement, domestic violence court support, compensation/classification updates, Safe Routes to School, and ARRA grants, while pulling Items 8, 17, and 44.

agenda_items.title: 2009 Second Quarter Police Crime Summary Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Jose Lopez presented redesigned monthly and quarterly crime reporting tracking violent crime, property crime, staffing, clearance rates, and Priority 1 response times. Robberies declined 16% year-to-date while residential daytime and convenience store smash-and-grab burglaries rose, prompting covert and overt saturation patrols in Northgate Park; Councilman Clement praised Operation Bullseye results.

agenda_items.title: Development Public Hearing (Stormwater Concerns Addressed)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Councilwoman Diane Catotti confirmed with Planning and Public Works stormwater/engineering staff that no adverse stormwater impacts remained from earlier reviews, after which Council closed the public hearing and approved the item.

agenda_items.title: Plan Amendment A080001 and Zoning Map Change Z07-47 (Eno Drive at West Point on the Eno)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Joe Carley reported staff and Planning Commission (8-5) approval recommendations, while Friends of West Point Park representative Dan McNeill asked for a delay because NC State Parks was actively negotiating with the property owner to preserve the parcel as parkland. Councilwoman Catotti moved six-month continuations for both cases to the second cycle in March 2010.

agenda_items.title: ARRA Second Amendment with Durham Management Solutions, Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Responding to Victoria Peterson's question about whether an RFP had been issued, OEWD staff Nick McCoy confirmed the original contract had gone through an RFP with a one-year renewal option, and staff agreed to provide workforce placement benchmarks.

agenda_items.title: 2008 Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (JAG) Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson criticized serious violent crime and urged greater community input on federal law enforcement grant allocations. Mayor Bell noted staff is open to ideas via the City Manager.

agenda_items.title: CDBG Subrecipient Contract with Edgemont Neighborhood LLC (702 Wall Street)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson questioned city policies on selecting housing renovation contractors and whether Durham residents were hired locally. Community Development staff explained awards follow annual or intermittent RFPs requiring at least a 2:1 (preferably 3:1 or 4:1) private dollar match and demonstrated capacity.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved all consent items except Items 8, 17, and 44.

votes.item_title: Approve Public Hearing Item Following Stormwater Verification
votes.discussion_detail: Approved following staff confirmation that stormwater/engineering raised no adverse impacts.

votes.discussion_detail: Continued public hearing for six months to the second cycle in March 2010 to allow NC State Parks parkland preservation negotiations.

votes.discussion_detail: Continued companion zoning map change to the second cycle in March 2010.

votes.item_title: Item 8: ARRA Second Amendment with Durham Management Solutions, Inc.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved one-year contract renewal amendment after confirming prior RFP.

votes.item_title: Item 17: 2008 Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (JAG) Amendment
votes.discussion_detail: Approved JAG grant ordinance amendment.

votes.item_title: Item 44: CDBG Subrecipient Contract with Edgemont Neighborhood LLC (702 Wall Street)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved CDBG subrecipient contract after staff explained RFP match and capacity standards.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presided over the August 20, 2009 City Council Work Session with all seven council members present, and all votes were unanimous. Council reported continuing closed-session employee performance evaluations to September 10, requested memorial resolutions (including for Durham's first Black Fire Chief, Nathaniel Thompson), approved priority agenda referrals, and authorized a brief legal closed session. Staff introduced the city's 'Culture of Service' employee initiative, and Council suspended the rules to unanimously approve Item 12 (sale of 614 Eastway Avenue). Council also pressed Public Works Director Katie Kalb for a firm schedule and funding source by late September for long-delayed Harvard Avenue paving, heard Citizens Matters complaints from annexed residents denied city trash and recycling collection, noted Melanie Taylor's appointment to the Recreation Advisory Commission (6 votes), and set the next regular meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Report, Memorial Requests, and Priority Agenda Adjustments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reported continuing employee evaluations until September 10 (motion by Ali), requested memorial resolutions including for retired Fire Chief Nathaniel Thompson, and approved City Manager referrals (Items 25, 29, 38), supplemental Item 44 (Edgemont Neighborhood LLC / 1102 Wall St), and a City Attorney closed session. The Clerk noted a valid protest petition on Item 37 (Eno Drive at West Point on the Eno).

agenda_items.title: Culture of Service Initiative Introduction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vicki Atkinson from Budget and Management Services introduced the 'Culture of Service' initiative launched by the City Manager, engaging graduates of city leadership development programs to reinforce public service values across departments.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Sale of Property at 614 Eastway Avenue
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted unanimously to suspend the rules and approve the proposed sale of city-owned property at 614 Eastway Avenue.

agenda_items.title: Harvard Avenue Paving Design, Funding, and 10-Year Assessment Process
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Councilmembers Clement and Brown pressed staff on delays dating back to 1996 petitions for paving Harvard Avenue, which Council had ordered in the public interest despite lacking a sufficient neighborhood petition. Staff noted property-owner assessments are amortized over 10 years, and Public Works Director Katie Kalb committed to returning at the September 24 work session with a firm schedule and identified funding.

agenda_items.title: District 1 Policing Praise, Annexed Community Recycling Denial, and Youth Van Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Residents praised District 1 police officers and National Night Out, while residents of an annexed community (including Bill Ludwell at 827 Saratoga Drive) protested paying city taxes while being denied city trash/recycling collection and forced to pay private haulers. Council directed the City Manager to review outdated collection rules, and heard a funding/van request from a youth organization (YBDA).

agenda_items.title: Recreation Advisory Commission Appointment and Regular Agenda Setting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk reported Melanie Taylor received 6 votes for the Recreation Advisory Commission. Council unanimously set the consent agenda (Items 1-11, 13-24, 26-27, 44), GBA presentation (Item 30), and GBA public hearings (Items 31-37).

votes.notes: Voice vote; all 7 members present at roll call.

votes.notes: Voice vote.

votes.notes: Voice vote.
