meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presided over the August 17, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting with all seven council members present. Following proclamations for MDA Firefighter Appreciation Month, Meals on Wheels Day, Durham Striders, Youth Council, and national accreditations for Durham's Emergency Communications Center and Budget Director Bertha Johnson, Council unanimously (7-0) approved the City Manager's priority items. On Item 33, the public hearing for the Neighborhood Revitalization Fund contract with Mozella Elma McLaughlin (following remarks urging a win-win resolution with Dr. Bruce Bridges' Notebook Store), Council split 5-2 on the motion after closing the public hearing, with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, and Farad Ali voting Aye and Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti voting Nay. Council confirmed Item 35 (zoning map change for a new DPS middle school on Trayburn) was referred back to staff without a public hearing so Durham Public Schools could pursue County site-plan and transportation permits, and unanimously (7-0) approved pulled consent items including Rolling Hills acquisition authority (Item 9), a U.S. EDA grant ordinance (Item 11), and Items 12, 17, 18, 19, and 27.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations and Recognitions (MDA, Meals on Wheels, Durham Striders, DECC, Bertha Johnson)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council issued proclamations for MDA Firefighter Appreciation Month, August 26 Meals on Wheels Day, and Substance Abuse Committee efforts, and recognized the Durham Striders (Dr. Brenda Armstrong), the Youth Council, Budget Director Bertha Johnson (elected NC Local Government Budget Association president), and the Durham Emergency Communication Center's triple accreditation including CALEA.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Item 33 McLaughlin NRF & Item 35 New Middle School)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager recommended opening Item 33 for public comment without final action until September 21 and referring Item 35 (New Middle School / Trayburn zoning map change) back to Planning at Durham Public Schools' request.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Neighborhood Revitalization Fund Contract with Mozella Elma McLaughlin
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During public hearing wrap-up, Councilman Clement emphasized support for the Notebook Store (Dr. Bruce Bridges), McLaughlin's grocery, and 'the Clock' in Northeast Central Durham and urged staff to help broker a win-win resolution between McLaughlin and Bridges. After closing the public hearing, Council voted 5-2 on the motion on Item 33, with Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti voting No.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change - New Middle School (Trayburn / Durham Public Schools)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After initially opening the public hearing by mistake, Mayor Bell and Planning Director Steve Medlin clarified that Council's adoption of the Manager's priority items had already referred the DPS middle school zoning case back to staff so DPS could submit a site plan and transportation special use permit to the Board of County Commissioners.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Referred back to staff (via Priority Items)

agenda_items.title: Rolling Hills Acquisition/Relocation Budget Authority Increase
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson asked whether a Rolling Hills/Southside committee would be formed and raised questions about federal grant scope. Staff noted ongoing work with Community Development and Workforce Development to ensure local business participation.

agenda_items.title: U.S. Department of Commerce EDA Federal Grant Project Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson asked how Durham would ensure local residents are hired on RDU-area projects funded by the EDA grant, and a council member urged workforce diversity review for Kimley-Horn.

agenda_items.title: Remaining Pulled Consent Items (12, 17, 18, 19, and 27)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council bundled and approved the remaining five consent items previously pulled for comment by Victoria Peterson.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager Priority Items (Item 33 & Item 35 Referral)
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted manager priority recommendations on Item 33 (public hearing/continuation) and Item 35 (refer DPS middle school zoning back to staff).

votes.item_title: Item 33: Motion Following Public Hearing on Neighborhood Revitalization Fund Contract with Mozella Elma McLaughlin
votes.notes: Split vote 5-2; Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti voted Nay, with the other five seated members present voting Aye.
votes.discussion_detail: Closed public hearing and voted on Item 33 (Mozella Elma McLaughlin NRF contract), passing 5-2 after Diane Catotti voted No and Eugene Brown added his No vote.

votes.item_title: Item 9: Increase in Budget Authority for Rolling Hills Acquisition/Relocation
votes.discussion_detail: Approved Rolling Hills budget authority increase following public comment.

votes.item_title: Item 11: U.S. Department of Commerce EDA Federal Grant Project Ordinance
votes.discussion_detail: Approved EDA federal grant ordinance after discussion of local Durham hiring and workforce diversity.

votes.item_title: Approve Remaining Pulled Consent Items (Items 12, 17, 18, 19, and 27)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved pulled consent Items 12, 17, 18, 19, and 27 in a single motion.

meetings.title: Special Council Meeting - Master Plan/Parks & Rec Facilities
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the August 13, 2009 Special City Council Meeting to order (with Diane Catotti excused absent and Farad Ali arriving en route from Charlotte) to establish strategic policies for updating the Parks and Recreation Master Plan and shaping the six-year Capital Improvement Plan. Following a unanimous procedural vote on Diane Catotti's excused absence, City Manager Tom Bonfield and Parks and Recreation Director Rhonda Parker presented results from six council member surveys and the Recreation Advisory Commission showing consensus on core center amenities, equitable travel distances, prioritizing underserved residents, and operating programs in non-city facilities. Council members criticized the lack of early PAC and Northeast Central Durham Leadership Council engagement in the prior budget decision to close E.D. Mickle Center and move programs to Holton Career and Resource Center. Discussion also addressed deferred maintenance costs, potential joint use of Burton School/DPS gymnasiums and partnerships with Raleigh/Trust for Public Land, whether future regional centers (including north and south facilities beyond Holton and Walltown) require pools, and budget/bond and impact-fee constraints; the Manager committed to returning with draft multi-year guiding directives for formal adoption.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call and Excused Absence for Council Member Diane Catotti
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Roll call showed five members present initially, Farad Ali en route from Charlotte, and Diane Catotti requesting an excused absence. Council approved the opening motion unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Parks & Recreation Master Plan Context, Council Survey Consensus, and Citizen Survey Data
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Bonfield and Director Rhonda Parker reviewed the 6-year CIP context and consensus from six council surveys and the Recreation Advisory Commission: centers should offer core amenities (gym, classrooms, kitchen, fitness, teen/senior space, computer lab), equalize travel distances, prioritize residents lacking private options, serve beyond single neighborhoods, and utilize non-city facilities. Staff also reviewed 2005 Citizens Voice Survey and state SCORP rankings.

agenda_items.title: Closure of E.D. Mickle Center, Transfer to Holton, and Community Engagement Concerns
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members questioned the budget-cycle decision to close E.D. Mickle rather than renovate it and shift programs to Holton Career and Resource Center. Members criticized staff for engaging the PAC and Northeast Central Durham Leadership Council only after the closure decision had been made rather than up front.

agenda_items.title: Regional Recreation Center Siting, School/Interlocal Partnerships, Pools, and CIP Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council examined plans for two additional regional centers (north and south, alongside Holton and Walltown), deferred maintenance shortfalls ($207,000 identified vs. $140,000 budgeted at a sample center), potential school gym partnerships (such as Burton School near T.A. Grady) and Raleigh/Trust for Public Land collaboration, whether new centers must include pools, and bond/budget constraints amid lower impact fees. City Manager Bonfield agreed to return with synthesized multi-year policy guidelines for formal Council action.

votes.item_title: Approve Excused Absence for Council Member Diane Catotti
votes.notes: Voice vote; 5 members present at call to order (Ali en route, Catotti excused).
votes.discussion_detail: Approved excused absence request for Diane Catotti at start of special meeting while Farad Ali was en route from Charlotte.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden opened the August 6, 2009 City Council work session prior to Mayor Bill Bell's arrival, following an earlier morning closed session on direct-report performance evaluations that Council voted to continue to August 20. Council suspended the rules to unanimously approve Item 24 (a 2010 NC Governor's Highway Safety Program traffic safety equipment grant) and Item 28 (a resolution regarding water quality protection for Falls Lake ahead of anticipated General Assembly action). During the afternoon session, Council reviewed community development second-mortgage homeownership incentives, discussed potential rezoning and minor special use permit rules for group homes in the Vail Street area, heard a presentation from Summer Youth Construction Training Program participants, and questioned the delayed memo timeline on the $5 million West Village Phase 2 streetscape and power-line undergrounding agreement. All votes recorded during the session were unanimous by voice vote, and Council set the consent and General Business agendas for its August 17 regular meeting.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Items 24, 28, 31, and 41)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager presented four priority items: suspending rules to vote on Item 24 (2010 NC Governor's Highway Safety Program grant) and Item 28 (Falls Lake water quality protection resolution ahead of state legislative action), scheduling Item 31 (Capital Program Advisory Committee quarterly report) for 2:30 p.m., and carrying over Item 41 (Housing Appeals Board appointment) from the August 3 council meeting.

agenda_items.title: Continuation of Direct-Report Performance Evaluation Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden reported that Council met in closed session earlier that morning (delayed while members attended the new Lowe's opening at Martin Luther King Jr. Drive and Fayetteville Street) for performance evaluations of Council direct reports. Council voted to continue those evaluation meetings to 10:00 a.m. on Thursday, August 20 in the Council Conference Room.

agenda_items.title: 2010 NC Governor's Highway Safety Program Traffic Safety Equipment Grant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During the agenda review, Council suspended the rules as requested by the City Manager to take immediate action on a 2010 North Carolina Governor's Highway Safety Program grant for traffic safety equipment.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Regarding Water Quality Protection for Falls Lake
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council suspended the rules and voted on a resolution concerning water quality protection for Falls Lake, which had been pulled from the August 3 agenda, because the North Carolina General Assembly was anticipated to act on related legislation later that week.

agenda_items.title: FY 2009 Fourth Quarter Mortgage Loan Portfolio Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development staff highlighted the city's second-mortgage homeownership program offering up to $30,000 in low-interest financing to increase homeownership in neighborhoods with low ownership rates.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Resolution (Comparison with Chapel Hill and Carrboro Language)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members requested placing Item 37 on the General Business Agenda for the August 17 meeting and asked the City Attorney to compare the draft resolution submitted by Mr. Weaver with resolutions adopted by Chapel Hill and Carrboro so Council could vote on specific language.

agenda_items.title: Vail Street Zoning and Group Home Investigation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported on the split-zoned Vail Street area (Office/Institutional and Industrial Light), evaluating potential rezoning to residential to stabilize the neighborhood and coordinating with state regulators to verify whether local facilities are legally permitted family care or group homes. Staff also noted potential zoning changes such as requiring a minor special use permit for group homes, with a follow-up report scheduled for the second work session in September.

agenda_items.title: Summer Youth Construction Training Program Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Youth participants and partners from Eco Construction, the Durham Affordable Housing Coalition, Step Up Durham, and the Mayor's Youth Program thanked Council for supporting the second year of the Summer Youth Construction Training Program and asked how to sustain and expand funding.

agenda_items.title: Second Amendment to West Village Phase 2 Agreement (Blue Devil Partners)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council revisited Item 10 regarding a streetscaping agreement with Blue Devil Partners originally budgeted at $4 million and needing a new agreement increasing the budget to $5 million to cover undergrounding of overhead power lines. Council members questioned why the Office of Economic and Workforce Development had not delivered a separate memo or agenda item earlier between January and August.

agenda_items.title: Set Agenda for August 17, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed and approved the August 17 agenda, placing Items 1-9, 11-27, 30, and 41 on the Consent Agenda; Items 10, 29, and 37 on the General Business Agenda; and Items 32-35 on General Business Public Hearings.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Items (Items 24, 28, 31, and 41)
votes.notes: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presided at the start of the session prior to Mayor Bill Bell's arrival; passed by voice vote with no dissent.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the manager's four priority items, including suspending rules on Items 24 and 28, scheduling Item 31 for 2:30 p.m., and carrying over Item 41.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At its August 3, 2009 regular meeting, the Durham City Council issued proclamations recognizing August 2009 as Grow Solar North Carolina and Durham Month and highlighting National Night Out public safety and human services partnerships. Council voted 7-0 to grant Ward 2 Council Member Howard Clement III an excused absence for the August 6 morning Lowe's opening in Ward 2, where over 2,000 applicants sought 274 jobs, and later voted 7-0 to approve a commercial/retail rezoning along U.S. 70 after developer Joe Jernigan committed to 3.5-inch caliper buffer trees and stormwater pond vegetation measures to deter geese. In a split multi-candidate ballot vote for an appointment to the Housing Appeals Board, Mr. Hopkins received 3 votes, Mr. Dudley received 2 votes, and Mr. Patterson received 2 votes (individual council member selections were not announced); because 4 votes were required, the appointment was deferred to the August 6 work session.

agenda_items.title: Grow Solar North Carolina and Durham Month & National Night Out Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented a proclamation declaring August 2009 as Grow Solar North Carolina and Durham Month to support solar incentives and renewable-energy workforce training. Council also recognized National Night Out and Durham Police Department collaborations with Durham Crisis Response Center, the Red Cross, Crime Stoppers, the Food Bank, and Project Safe Neighborhoods.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence Request for Council Member Howard Clement III (August 6, 2009)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Howard Clement III requested an excused absence for the August 6 morning session to attend the 10:00 a.m. grand opening of the new Lowe's store at Martin Luther King Jr. Drive and Fayetteville Street in Ward 2, noting that more than 2,000 people had applied for 274 jobs at the store. Council approved the excused absence.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Items (Minutes, Contracts, Street Closings, and Grants)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Mayor read the consent agenda titles covering board applications, automated refuse collection vehicles, May/June bid reports, street closings and acceptances, records retention schedules, a Habitat for Humanity subrecipient amendment, a DBAP operating agreement amendment, an ARRA Brownfields grant for the Fayetteville Street corridor, volunteer fire contracts, and Third Fork Creek Trail design amendments.

agenda_items.title: U.S. 70 Commercial/Retail Rezoning Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed stormwater pond vegetation best management practices and string-line deterrents for Canada geese along pedestrian trails, lighting mitigation via wide buffers and berms, and city vs. state street jurisdiction along U.S. 70. Applicant representative Joe Jernigan agreed to an additional committed element increasing buffer tree caliper from 2.5 inches to 3.5 inches.

agenda_items.title: Housing Appeals Board Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk announced the ballot tally for the Housing Appeals Board appointment: Mr. Hopkins received 3 votes, Mr. Dudley received 2 votes, and Mr. Patterson received 2 votes. Because 4 votes were required for an appointment, Council agreed to defer the vote to the August 6 work session.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Council Member Howard Clement III (August 6, 2009)
votes.notes: All seven seated members were present at roll call and voted in favor.
votes.discussion_detail: Granted an excused absence to Ward 2 Council Member Howard Clement III to attend the Ward 2 Lowe's opening at 10:00 a.m. on August 6, 2009.

votes.item_title: U.S. 70 Commercial/Retail Rezoning Proposal
votes.notes: Passed unanimously 7-0 following close of the public hearing.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the U.S. 70 commercial/retail rezoning proposal with committed elements including 3.5-inch diameter buffer trees, lighting mitigation, and stormwater pond vegetation commitments.

votes.item_title: Housing Appeals Board Appointment Ballot
votes.notes: Individual council member ballot choices were not announced in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Ballot voting produced 3 votes for Mr. Hopkins, 2 votes for Mr. Dudley, and 2 votes for Mr. Patterson; with 4 votes required, Council deferred the appointment to the August 6 work session.

disagreements.issue: Housing Appeals Board Appointment (Three-Way Ballot Split)
disagreements.summary: Council split its seven ballots among three candidates for a Housing Appeals Board seat—Mr. Hopkins (3), Mr. Dudley (2), and Mr. Patterson (2)—leaving no candidate with the required four-vote majority.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support Mr. Hopkins (3 votes)
side_a_arguments: Received a plurality of 3 ballots from Council.
disagreements.side_b_position: Support Mr. Dudley (2 votes) or Mr. Patterson (2 votes)
side_b_arguments: Four council members split evenly between Mr. Dudley and Mr. Patterson.
disagreements.resolution: Deferred to the August 6, 2009 City Council work session after no candidate reached the four-vote threshold.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the July 23, 2009 work session, Council reported a unanimous 7-0 vote from closed session to continue the City Manager's performance evaluation to August 6 and unanimously accepted the City Manager's priority items, including referring Items 46 (Fountainfield/Fountainworks contract) and 50 (Rowan Street assessment rolls) back to administration and carrying forward Brightleaf Commons items 64 and 65. Solid Waste Management Director Don Long updated Council on the rollout of the new curbside recycling program, reporting 61,700 carts delivered, roughly 2,000 missed deliveries, and One Call wait-time backlogs expected to clear by August 6. Council also discussed potential lead-paint abatement amendments to the minimum housing code with the City Attorney, heard citizen comments on Duke Energy tree trimming and traffic safety signals, noted a $724,497 U.S. Department of Justice grant awarded to the Police Department, and unanimously approved the agenda for the August 3 regular meeting.

agenda_items.title: Continuation of City Manager Evaluation Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell announced for the record that Council met in closed session for the personnel evaluation of the City Manager and voted unanimously (motion by Howard Clement III, seconded by Farad Ali) to continue the evaluation to 10:00 a.m. on August 6 in the Council Committee Room.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Items 46, 47, 48, 50, 64, and 65)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested referring Item 46 (Fountainfield/Fountainworks contract) and Item 50 (Rowan Street assessment rolls) back to administration, scheduling the recycling update and Southwest Central Durham Quality of Life presentation at the start of the meeting and the Make It Durham presentation at 2:00 p.m., and adding supplemental Brightleaf Commons public hearings (Items 64 and 65).

agenda_items.title: New Curbside Recycling Program Rollout Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Solid Waste Management Director Don Long reported that 61,700 recycling carts had been delivered in the first two weeks of the new program, while approximately 2,000 deliveries were missed and caused One Call wait-time backlogs. Staff anticipated resolving delivery and routing issues by the start of the second full collection cycle on August 6.

agenda_items.title: Minimum Housing Code and Lead Paint Abatement Authority
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following comments from Rev. Whitley, Mr. Hester, and Mr. Quittler, Council asked the City Attorney to research state enabling legislation and determine whether Durham has authority to amend its minimum housing code to require lead paint abatement, as well as to review sample ordinances from other cities.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments on Tree Trimming, Bus Incident, Traffic Signals, and DOJ Grant Announcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizens addressed Duke Energy's tree-trimming practices, a bus incident and related insurance documentation, job creation for Brownfields graduates via lead abatement, and intersection left-turn accidents needing a traffic signal. Staff also announced the Police Department had just received a $724,497 competitive U.S. Department of Justice law enforcement assistance grant.

agenda_items.title: Set Agenda for August 3, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council confirmed there was no further closed session needed and unanimously approved the August 3 agenda: Items 1-6, 8-21, 22 (Hersey Street sanitary sewer), and 23-45 on Consent; Item 7 on GBA; and Items 50 (subset B)-57 plus 64-65 on GBA Public Hearings.

votes.discussion_detail: Continued the City Manager personnel evaluation closed session to 10:00 a.m. on August 6, 2009 in the Council Committee Room.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote with all seven members present.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote with all seven members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Set the consent, GBA, and GBA public hearing items for the August 3 regular Council meeting.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Council dedicated the opening of its June 15, 2009 regular meeting to Durham youth—recognizing Durham Nativity School graduates and Youth Commission members—and read a resolution memorializing historian Dr. John Hope Franklin. The City Manager presented priority items including the revised FY 2009-2010 budget and FY 2010-2015 Capital Improvement Plan (Item 14), referrals back to administration for Lyon Park upgrades (Item 28) and recyclable materials processing (Item 43), and supplemental items on Health Care Reform Principles and groundwater monitoring wells; later in the meeting the Manager noted the budget passed and reported one of 31 employees slated for reduction in force had arranged to retire. Council unanimously approved 7-0 a grant allocation across Northeast Central Durham, Southwest Central Durham, and Southside/West End, the FY 2010 Downtown Durham, Inc. economic development contract (Item 23), and 18 ARRA Surface Transportation Program projects totaling roughly $5 million (Item 39) while emphasizing local hiring, job tracking, and Alston Avenue environmental justice mitigation.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Durham Youth and Resolution Memorializing Dr. John Hope Franklin
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Promise Woody sang the National Anthem, and Council recognized graduates of Durham Nativity School and 40 to 50 members of the Youth Commission. Council Member Howard Clement III also read into the record a resolution honoring historian Dr. John Hope Franklin, noting his mentorship of Clement at Howard University.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (FY 2009-2010 Budget, Lyon Park, Recycling Processing, Health Care Reform, Monitoring Wells)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager presented revised motion language for Item 14 (FY 2009-2010 Budget and FY 2010-2015 CIP), requested referring Item 28 (Lyon Park upgrades) and Item 43 (recyclable materials processing, expected back July 23 after curbside recycling launches July 13) to administration, and added supplemental Items 60 (Health Care Reform Principles) and 61 (monitoring wells license agreement). Later remarks confirmed the budget's passage and an update that one of 31 RIF-impacted employees arranged to retire.

agenda_items.title: Grant Award Allocation to Northeast Central Durham, Southwest Central Durham, and Southside Project Areas
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff clarified that the grant award funds would be allocated across three target project areas: Northeast Central Durham, Southwest Central Durham, and Southside/West End.

agenda_items.title: FY 2010 Contract Between the City of Durham and Downtown Durham, Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A public speaker urged Council to consider other organizations performing downtown economic development work before voting. Following discussion, Council approved the FY 2010 contract with Downtown Durham, Inc.

agenda_items.title: ARRA Municipal Agreements and Grant Project Ordinances for STP-DA Surface Transportation Projects
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented 18 separate ARRA-funded transportation projects (~$5 million) facing strict NCDOT September 1, 2009 submission and January 1, 2010 award deadlines. Council members pressed staff on resolving the NCDOT environmental justice mitigation for the Alston Avenue widening, maximizing local contractor and Equal Opportunity participation, and tracking jobs created and sustained.

agenda_items.title: Recycling Processing Speakers, RIF Placement Update, and Tennis Court CIP Inquiry
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council noted Item 43 speakers after the item was referred back to administration, heard the City Manager report that one of 31 employees scheduled for reduction in force had arranged to retire, and answered a Durham Orange Community Tennis Association inquiry clarifying that Rock Quarry court resurfacing would use reallocated funds while Southern Boundaries remained unfunded.

votes.item_title: Grant Award Allocation to Northeast Central Durham, Southwest Central Durham, and Southside Project Areas
votes.notes: Passed unanimously 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved grant award distribution across Northeast Central Durham, Southwest Central Durham, and Southside/West End project areas.

votes.item_title: Item 23: FY 2010 Contract with Downtown Durham, Inc. for Downtown Economic Development Services
votes.notes: Passed unanimously 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the FY 2010 economic development services contract with Downtown Durham, Inc. after resetting the electronic voting display.

votes.item_title: Item 39: ARRA Municipal Agreements and Grant Project Ordinances for 18 STP-DA Projects
votes.notes: Passed unanimously 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved 18 separate project agreements and grant project ordinances under the ARRA Surface Transportation Program ahead of NCDOT's September 1 deadline.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Following a three-hour morning Insurance Subcommittee meeting, Council debated whether to suspend the rules and vote immediately on Item 30 (2009-2010 employee benefits recommendation) at its June 4, 2009 work session. Howard Clement III made a substitute motion to automatically defer Item 30 to the June 15 regular meeting, which failed on a voice vote, and Council then approved accepting the City Manager's priority items in a 6-1 split vote—Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Farad Ali voted Aye, while Howard Clement III voted Nay because he opposed acting on Item 30 outside a regular council meeting. Council also unanimously approved adding a City Attorney resolution reaffirming domestic partner benefits and a City Clerk proposal revising board and commission attendance rules for June 15 action. During public comments and discussion, Council heard concerns over workforce development training contracts, housing code enforcement delays, and tennis court lighting bid schedules before setting the June 15 meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items & Debate Over Item 30 (2009-2010 Benefits Recommendation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager asked Council to suspend rules to vote on Eastway Avenue property sales (Item 19) and 2009-2010 employee benefits recommendations (Item 30), while referring Walltown Aquatic Center (Item 49), Lewis & Clark and Mozella L. McLaughlin NRF items (51-52), and Central Durham Gateways (Item 55) back to administration. Howard Clement III objected to voting on Item 30 at a work session and moved to defer it to June 15; after his substitute motion failed, the main priority-items motion passed 6-1 with Clement opposed.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Reaffirming Council Support for Domestic Partner Benefits
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Attorney submitted a priority resolution reaffirming the City Council's support for domestic partner benefits to be considered that afternoon.

agenda_items.title: Revisions to Board, Committee, and Commission Appointment and Attendance Rules
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk requested adding recommendations from the May 21 Procedures Committee revising citizen board and commission attendance rules for formal action at the June 15 meeting. Council later discussed the 50% (six-absence) threshold and how quorum should be defined.

agenda_items.title: Tennis Lighting Bids, Workforce Development Contracts, and Housing Code Enforcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated Council on expedited tennis court lighting bids due June 16 and potential August action. Council also heard a clean-energy/green-jobs pledge request, a dispute over Workforce Development Board Executive Committee approvals and Ms. Peterson's $300,000 Individual Training Account request (requesting a written staff response), and a tenant's complaint regarding unresolved housing code enforcement since December 2007.

agenda_items.title: Set Agenda for June 15, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council set the June 15 agenda, assigning Items 1-18, 22-29, 31-42, 44-45, 47-48, and 59 to Consent; Items 14, 20, 21, 43, and 46 to GBA; and Items 50, 54, and 55 to GBA Public Hearings.

votes.item_title: Substitute Motion to Automatically Defer Item 30 (2009-2010 Benefits) to June 15, 2009
votes.notes: Mayor Bell initially offered a pro forma second for discussion, and at the vote declared the motion failed for lack of a second / support.
votes.discussion_detail: Howard Clement III moved to pull Item 30 from the manager's priority request and automatically carry it over to the June 15 regular meeting; other members preferred pulling Item 30 for discussion first before deciding whether to vote or defer.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Items (Including Rule Suspension Request for Items 19 and 30)
votes.notes: Howard Clement III stated on the record at 00:04:33 that he would vote against the manager's recommendation on Item 30.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved accepting the City Manager's priority items after defeating Clement's substitute motion, while allowing Council to pull Item 30 during the meeting to decide whether to suspend rules or defer.

votes.item_title: City Attorney Priority Item: Resolution Reaffirming Domestic Partner Benefits
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Added the City Attorney's priority resolution reaffirming Council support for domestic partner benefits.

votes.item_title: City Clerk Priority Item: Add Board/Commission Attendance Rule Revisions for June 15 Action
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Added the Procedures Committee's board and commission attendance rule revisions to the agenda for discussion today and action on June 15, 2009.

votes.item_title: Set Agenda for June 15, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the consent, GBA, and GBA public hearing agenda assignments for the June 15 regular Council meeting.

disagreements.issue: Timing and Rule Suspension for 2009-2010 Employee Benefits Recommendation (Item 30)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 6-1 over whether to accept the City Manager's priority request to consider suspending rules for a vote on Item 30 (2009-2010 benefits recommendations) at the June 4 work session rather than automatically deferring it to the June 15 regular meeting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Accept manager's priority agenda and evaluate Item 30 after discussion
side_a_arguments: The manager noted that waiting until June 15 would compress the timeline to inform employees after the item had already been held up a cycle.
Council members who were not in the Insurance Subcommittee wanted to hear the presentation first before deciding whether to vote today or carry the item over to June 15.
disagreements.side_b_position: Automatically defer Item 30 to the June 15 regular Council meeting
side_b_arguments: Believed the community is impacted by benefits decisions and preferred voting at a regular full Council meeting on June 15 rather than suspending rules at a work session.
disagreements.resolution: Clement's substitute motion failed on a voice vote, and the main motion accepting the City Manager's priority items passed 6-1 with Howard Clement III voting Nay.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: With Council Member Howard Clement III absent, the six present members of the Durham City Council held the public hearing on the proposed FY 2009-2010 budget and FY 2010-2015 Capital Improvement Plan (Item 34), which began with a projected $24 million to $40 million deficit, and referred the 2009-2010 employee benefits recommendation (Item 20) back to Human Resources. Council unanimously approved the Consent Agenda (5-0), continued the Brightleaf Commons plan amendment public hearing to August 3 (5-0), received Human Relations Commission applications (5-0), and approved Alexander Village Phase II plan amendment A0800006 (6-0) and rezoning Z08-36 (6-0) with a $1,000-per-student school proffer. On a 33-acre townhouse rezoning proposal seeking to relax design guidelines to allow vinyl siding and omit garages, Council voted 5-1 to approve: Cora Cole-McFadden, Farad Ali, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Mike Woodard voted Aye, while Mayor Bill Bell voted Nay in disappointment over the weakened standards.

agenda_items.title: National Homeownership Month & Referral of 2009-2010 Benefits Recommendation (Item 20)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell proclaimed June 2009 as National Homeownership Month and recognized Boy Scout Troop 137 from St. Joseph's. As a priority item, Council unanimously approved the City Manager's request to refer Item 20 (2009-2010 employee benefits recommendation) back to the Human Resources Department.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Boards, Audits, DPAC, Public Safety, and Public Works)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the Consent Agenda covering board appointments, municipal candidate filing fee ordinances, an ARRA NSP-2 public hearing, April 2009 bid reports and equipment purchases, ward boundary reaffirmation, the April 2009 zoning enforcement audit, memorial resolutions for John Hope Franklin and Ernie Barnes, DPAC non-naming rights, Holton Center sublease, police polygraph funds, and NCSU floating wetland islands.

agenda_items.title: Brightleaf Commons Plan Amendment Continuance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Applicant attorney Craig Eustice (K&L Gates) requested continuing the Brightleaf Commons comprehensive plan amendment public hearing to August 3, 2009 so it could be heard concurrently with the companion rezoning. Planning staff had no objection, and Council opened and continued the public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Human Relations Commission Receive and Accept Applications
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk distributed a letter from the Human Relations Director addressing applicant Ryan Urquhart's attendance record as requested at the work session. Council voted to receive and accept the applications.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on Proposed FY 2009-2010 Budget and FY 2010-2015 Capital Improvement Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson introduced the FY 2009-2010 budget and FY 2010-2015 CIP public hearing, noting that staff began the process facing a projected $24 million to $40 million budget deficit at the annual Council retreat.

agenda_items.title: 33-Acre Townhouse Rezoning Proposal (PDR 6.8 Design Guidelines Revision)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Bob Yensch opposed the fifth rezoning of the 33-acre parcel, arguing that eliminating garages and allowing vinyl siding instead of brick/wood weakened design guidelines solely for developer benefit. Mayor Bill Bell echoed disappointment over dropping garages and brick/wood standards, while the remaining five council members present voted to approve.

agenda_items.title: Alexander Village Phase II Comprehensive Plan Amendment (Case A0800006)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Case A0800006 to change the future land use designation of a 1.95-acre segment of a 5.71-acre vacant parcel north of T.W. Alexander Drive near the Wake County line from medium-density residential to commercial. Planning Commission (14-0) and staff recommended approval.

agenda_items.title: Alexander Village Phase II Zoning Map Change (Case Z08-36)

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At its May 18, 2009 regular meeting, the Durham City Council recognized National Public Works Week and unanimously approved priority items referring a Cole Mill Road cell tower license agreement (Item 12) back to administration and moving the proposed FY 2009-2010 budget and FY 2010-2015 Capital Improvement Plan presentation (Item 38) to the start of the General Business Agenda (7-0). Council also approved the Consent Agenda 7-0, covering an ARRA employment and training grant, a Builders of Hope CHDO grant, Duke Energy land sales, and multiple water and transportation engineering contracts. In public hearings, Council voted 7-0 to confirm Wynn Road and Rowan Street assessment rolls while continuing objected Rowan Street properties (Item 29), voted 7-0 to grant a quasi-judicial major special use permit for floodway-fringe elevation-by-design renovations at Stewart Heights Apartments (Item 30), and voted 7-0 to adopt initial translational zoning for newly annexed Alexander Village acreage (Item 31).

agenda_items.title: National Public Works Week Proclamation & Council Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell proclaimed National Public Works Week to Public Works Director Kathryn Kalb and staff. Council members also celebrated heavy-equipment training graduates, a record $27,000+ Duck Race fundraiser for the Interfaith Food Shuttle, Police Department promotions, and the Bimbe Festival.

agenda_items.title: City Manager & City Clerk Priority Items (Items 5, 12, and 38)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved 7-0 the City Manager's priority items referring Item 12 (T-Mobile cell tower license at 1701 Cole Mill Road) back to administration and moving Item 38 (FY 2009-2010 Budget and FY 2010-2015 CIP presentation) to the start of GBA. Council also approved 7-0 the City Clerk's priority ballot update removing Frederick Davis Jr. from Item 5 (Planning Commission) following his county appointment.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Grants, Real Estate, Engineering, and Annual Reports)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the Consent Agenda covering board appointments, rear-loading refuse trucks, the Builders of Hope CHDO grant, an ARRA employment and training grant ordinance, Drew Street sales to Duke Energy, friendly condemnation at Home Place Townhomes, South Alston Avenue acquisition for the Cary interconnection water main, Lanier Parking Amendment #1, DPAC interest income, planning/appearance annual reports, NC 54/I-40 corridor study, and Black & Veatch water treatment engineering.

agenda_items.title: Presentation of Proposed FY 2009-2010 Budget and FY 2010-2015 Capital Improvement Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the Consent Agenda vote, Council moved to the presentation of the proposed FY 2009-2010 budget and FY 2010-2015 Capital Improvement Plan.

agenda_items.title: Confirmation of Assessment Rolls (Wynn Road and Rowan Street)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works Director Kathryn Kalb recommended confirming assessment rolls for curb, gutter, paving, water/sewer laterals, and water mains on Wynn Road and Rowan Street, while continuing the public hearing and referring objected Rowan Street properties (Marie Webb, William and Brenda G. Curtis, and Mr. Hunter as clarified with Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden) to a future work session.

agenda_items.title: Major Special Use Permit: Stewart Heights Apartment Building TT (Case M080004)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In a quasi-judicial hearing, Planning staff and the applicant (Stewart Circle LLC) presented plans to elevate-by-design an existing 1950s low-income tax-credit apartment building off Atlantic Street located within the FEMA floodway fringe (raising the finished floor to 288.2 feet, two feet above future conditions BFE, with French drains and no fill). No opponents spoke, and Council approved the permit with staff's consistency condition.

agenda_items.title: Initial Zoning Map Change: Alexander Village Initial Zoning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented direct translational city zoning for a 2.9-acre tract on T.W. Alexander Drive east of Page Road annexed effective March 31, 2009. With no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and approved the zoning.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Items (Items 12 and 38)
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Referred Item 12 (Cole Mill Road cell tower license) back to administration and moved Item 38 (budget presentation) to the start of GBA.

votes.item_title: Accept City Clerk's Priority Item (Item 5 Planning Commission Ballot Update)
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Removed Frederick Davis Jr. from the Item 5 Durham Planning Commission ballot due to his May 11 appointment by the County Commissioners.

votes.item_title: Item 29: Confirmation of Assessment Rolls (Wynn Road and Rowan Street, Excluding Continued Objections)
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Confirmed assessment rolls except for objected Rowan Street properties (Webb, Curtis, and Hunter), which were continued to a future work session.

votes.item_title: Item 30: Major Special Use Permit — Stewart Heights Apartment Building TT (Case M080004)
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the quasi-judicial major special use permit for floodway-fringe elevation-by-design renovations with staff's consistency condition.

votes.item_title: Item 31: Initial Zoning Map Change — Alexander Village Initial Zoning
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted direct translational initial zoning for the 2.9-acre Alexander Village tract annexed March 31, 2009.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden in Mayor Bill Bell's absence, the May 7, 2009 work session saw Council unanimously accept City Manager priority items—including suspending the rules to vote immediately on an ARRA Justice Assistance Grant (Item 33), the sale of 605 Eastway Avenue (Item 34), House Bill 624 on Rougemont incorporation (Item 35), and East Durham Outfalls Phase 3 (Item 36). Council suspended the rules and approved Item 34 (605 Eastway Avenue) and a companion supplemental item by unanimous voice votes, questioned parking garage exit delays on Lanier Parking Amendment #1 (Item 14), and reviewed an ARRA stimulus status update noting three city ARRA approvals to date and pending second-round wastewater decisions. Residents also addressed long-delayed street paving petitions (including Red Oak/Chalmers Street) and streetlights, staff provided a 90-day bankruptcy consent-order update on Lund Street apartment demolition enforcement, and Council set the May 18 meeting agenda including proposed FY 2009-2010 water and sewer rates on GBA.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Items 26, 33, 34, 35, 36, and 37)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously accepted the manager's priority items scheduling the Downtown Durham Inc. presentation at 2:00 p.m., requesting rule suspensions on Items 33 (ARRA JAG grant), 34 (sale of 605 Eastway Ave), 35 (HB 624 Rougemont incorporation, added at Mike Woodard's request to update 2007 letters), and 36 (East Durham Outfalls Phase 3), and adding Item 37 (ARRA FAA grant to RDU).

agenda_items.title: Proposed Sale of Property at 605 Eastway Avenue (and Preceding Supplemental Item)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council suspended the rules and voted unanimously by voice vote to approve a Community Development supplemental item and Item 34, the proposed sale of city-owned property at 605 Eastway Avenue.

agenda_items.title: House Bill 624: Incorporation of Rougemont
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council took up supplemental Item 35 regarding North Carolina House Bill 624 on the proposed incorporation of Rougemont, updating Durham's 2007 correspondence.

agenda_items.title: Amendment #1 to Parking Systems Management Agreement (Lanier Parking)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services staff (Harmon Crutchfield) answered questions regarding Center Parking Garage across from the Carolina Theatre, where construction work and post-event exit backups had prompted citizen complaints.

agenda_items.title: RDU FAA ARRA Grant, Street Paving Petitions, and ARRA Stimulus Tracking Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained urgency for certification on the RDU FAA ARRA grant, citizens pressed for clear paving timelines on petitions dating back to 1995 (including the 900 block of Red Oak/Chalmers Street) and streetlights, and Assistant to the Manager Carmisha Wallace reported on ARRA grant tracking (three city items approved so far, EPA fleet grant withdrawn with Triangle J COG, and June 3 expected results for round-two wastewater projects).

agenda_items.title: Set May 18 Agenda & Lund Street Apartment Code Enforcement Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the May 18 agenda (Consent 1-4 and 6-24; GBA Item 5 and Item 28 water/sewer rates; GBA Public Hearings 29-31). The City Attorney also reported a 90-day consent-order agreement awaiting bankruptcy judge signature under which the city has funds and a contractor ready to demolish the non-compliant apartment complex on day 91 in July if repairs are not completed.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager's Priority Items (Including Rule Suspension on Item 35, HB 624)
votes.notes: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presided with Mayor Bill Bell absent; passed by voice vote with no dissent.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the manager's priority items and added the request to suspend rules on House Bill 624 (Rougemont incorporation).

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules and Approve Supplemental Item (Preceding Item 34)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended rules and approved the supplemental item presented immediately prior to Item 34.

votes.item_title: Item 34: Proposed Sale of Property at 605 Eastway Avenue (Rules Suspended)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended rules and approved the Community Development sale of 605 Eastway Avenue.

votes.item_title: Set Agenda for May 18, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the consent, GBA, and GBA public hearing agenda assignments for May 18, 2009.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 4, 2009 regular meeting, Council presented proclamations for the 2010 U.S. Census, Drinking Water Week student poster winners, and Police Week, while Howard Clement III requested a memorial resolution for Durham artist Ernie Barnes and an update on the Lund Street apartments. In public hearings, Council voted 7-0 to close and refer back the Sumter Street (Item 35) and Maxwell Street (Item 36) closings pending site plan approval, voted 7-0 to close 80 linear feet of Conyers Avenue (Item 37), and voted 7-0 to establish a $9.00/month third residential stormwater billing tier (Item 40). Council also approved the March 23 Audit Services Oversight Committee report 7-0 (Item 10) after Clement's inquiry. On pulled Consent Item 16—a $350,000 Neighborhood Revitalization Fund contract with St. Joseph's Historic Foundation—Council approved the contract 6-0 with one abstention after Eugene Brown questioned community concerns and missing memo details: Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Farad Ali voted Aye, while Mayor Bill Bell abstained because UDI CDC was part of the recipient group.

agenda_items.title: 2010 Census, Water Conservation Poster Contest, and Police Week Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented proclamations for the 2010 U.S. Census (highlighting address canvassing and $300 billion in federal funding formulas), Drinking Water Week alongside state and local student poster winners from Morehead Montessori, Lakewood Elementary, Durham Academy, and Voyager Academy, and Police Week (May 10-16) to Chief Jose Lopez. Council Member Howard Clement III also requested a memorial resolution for Durham artist Ernie Barnes and a Thursday work-session update on the Lund Street apartment complex.

agenda_items.title: Street Closings: 295 Linear Feet of Sumter Street and 1,067 Linear Feet of Maxwell Street
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Steve Medlin) recommended closing the public hearings and referring both the Sumter Street and Maxwell Street closing requests back to administration until a site plan is submitted, reviewed, and approved so Council can evaluate the public interest. No members of the public spoke, and Council approved both referrals 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Street Closing: 80 Linear Feet of Conyers Avenue
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff recommended permanently closing 80 linear feet of Conyers Avenue right-of-way to allow property recombination for future development after vetting showed no adverse impacts. No public speakers appeared, and Council approved the closing 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Establish Third Residential Tier for Stormwater Utility Billing Rates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works Director Kathryn Kalb recommended creating a third residential stormwater billing tier increasing top-tier monthly charges from $4.50 to $9.00 to fund stormwater and NPDES permit operations. Greater Durham Chamber of Commerce representative John White asked whether the stormwater utility was in deficit; staff confirmed there was no deficit and all fees stay within the stormwater utility.

agenda_items.title: Audit Services Oversight Committee Report (March 23, 2009)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Howard Clement III pulled Item 10 to clarify what was approved at the March 23 Audit Services Oversight Committee meeting. Staff confirmed two audits were presented: the non-city agency selection process audit and the 2005/2007 bond performance audit, after which Clement moved approval.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Revitalization Fund Contract ($350,000) with St. Joseph's Historic Foundation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Eugene Brown pulled Item 16, raising concerns from former board members and charrette organizers and criticizing the staff memo for omitting mention of a $14,000 expansion program. Staff explained that the Fayetteville Street catalyst project ranked atop nine competitive proposals and includes milestone/percentage-of-completion payment controls; Mayor Bill Bell abstained because UDI CDC was part of the recipient group.

votes.item_title: Item 35: Close Public Hearing and Refer Back Street Closing of 295 Linear Feet of Sumter Street
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Closed the public hearing and referred the Sumter Street closing request back to administration pending submission and approval of a site plan.

votes.item_title: Item 36: Close Public Hearing and Refer Back Street Closing of 1,067 Linear Feet of Maxwell Street
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Closed the public hearing and referred the companion Maxwell Street closing request back to administration pending site plan approval.

votes.item_title: Item 37: Street Closing of 80 Linear Feet of Conyers Avenue
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved permanently closing 80 linear feet of Conyers Avenue right-of-way for property recombination.

votes.item_title: Item 40: Establish Third Residential Tier for Stormwater Utility Billing Rates
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Established a third residential stormwater billing tier raising the top residential tier from $4.50/month to $9.00/month.

votes.item_title: Item 10: Audit Services Oversight Committee Report (March 23, 2009)
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the Audit Services Oversight Committee report covering the non-city agency selection process audit and the 2005/2007 bond performance audit.

votes.item_title: Item 16: Neighborhood Revitalization Fund Contract ($350,000) with St. Joseph's Historic Foundation
votes.notes: Mayor Bill Bell formally abstained on the record because UDI CDC is part of the recipient group.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the $350,000 Neighborhood Revitalization Fund contract with St. Joseph's Historic Foundation with percentage-of-completion milestone deliverables.

disagreements.issue: Transparency and Community Support for $350,000 St. Joseph's Historic Foundation Contract (Item 16)
disagreements.summary: Council Member Eugene Brown questioned missing background details and past neighborhood concerns regarding the $350,000 Neighborhood Revitalization Fund contract with St. Joseph's Historic Foundation, while Mayor Bill Bell abstained due to UDI CDC's involvement.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the $350,000 catalyst contract with milestone safeguards
side_a_arguments: Project ranked best among nine competitive proposals as a Fayetteville Street economic development catalyst.
Contract disbursements are tied to percentage-of-completion deliverables and close staff project management.
disagreements.side_b_position: Demand clearer staff memos and abstain where organizational ties exist
side_b_arguments: Eugene Brown noted that former board members and charrette organizers raised concerns and criticized the memo for omitting a $14,000 expansion program.
Mayor Bill Bell abstained because UDI CDC is part of the recipient group.
disagreements.resolution: Approved 6-0 with Mayor Bill Bell abstaining.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At its April 20, 2009 regular meeting, Council issued proclamations for Fair Housing Month, youth injury prevention, Emergency Communications Employee of the Year, and Junior Fire Marshal Malik Magette, and adopted a memorial resolution honoring Hayti printing executive and civic leader Nathaniel Bradshaw White Sr. Council approved the Consent Agenda 7-0 (excluding Item 4), covering a Habitat for Humanity property acquisition contract, Durham Station professional services, transit pass-through agreements, annual stormwater billing conversion, anti-gang planning grants, and a People's Channel PEG contract. All General Business public hearings passed 7-0: a major special use permit and companion site/floodplain permit for Crestwood Suites renovations (Items 18-19) and direct translational initial zoning for newly annexed Page/Champage Office Park and Alcorn/Olsen Harris properties (Items 20-21). On pulled Consent Item 4 (setting a public hearing for a third residential stormwater tier), Council heard a county resident's complaint about double utility surcharges, clarified that the stormwater fee does not apply outside city limits, and approved setting the hearing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Fair Housing Month, Emergency Communications, Junior Fire Marshal, and Nathaniel B. White Sr. Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented proclamations recognizing April 2009 as Fair Housing Month, youth substance-abuse and injury prevention, the Durham Emergency Communications Employee of the Year, and Junior Fire Marshal Malik Magette. Council Member Howard Clement III presented a memorial resolution honoring Nathaniel Bradshaw White Sr., long-time Service Printing Company leader in Hayti, to his son Nathaniel White Jr.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 4 and GBA Public Hearings)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved all unpulled consent items 7-0, including the Social Security Number certification audit, a Habitat for Humanity contract for four properties, a Durham Station SME amendment, a Bethpage water extension, a salt dome contract (SW-23), DCHC MPO transit agreements, converting residential stormwater billing to annual billing, anti-gang planning subrecipient contracts, and the People's Channel PEG access agreement.

agenda_items.title: Major Special Use Permit & Site Plan / Floodplain Permit: Crestwood Suites Renovations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a quasi-judicial hearing with no conflicts of interest disclosed, Council voted 7-0 (moved by Mike Woodard) to approve the major special use permit for Crestwood Suites renovations subject to substantial consistency with Attachment 7 plans. Council then voted 7-0 to approve the companion site plan and floodplain development permit (Item 19).

agenda_items.title: Initial Zoning Map Change: Page/Champage Office Park
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Steve Medlin) presented direct translational city zoning (ILD, PDR 4.73, and RSMD) for a newly annexed property whose annexation took effect March 31, 2009. No members of the public spoke, and Council approved the zoning 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Initial Zoning Map Change: Alcorn/Olsen Harris Properties
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented direct translational RS-20 rural residential city zoning for newly annexed property effective March 31, 2009. With no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and approved the zoning 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Set Public Hearing on Establishing a Third Tier for Stormwater Residential Billing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Stanley Branch pulled Item 4 to object to double utility rates charged to his mother, a county resident outside city limits. Mayor Bill Bell and the City Manager clarified that the outside-city surcharge applies to water and sewer—offering a water conservation specialist visit—while the proposed stormwater tier public hearing applies only within city limits; Council then approved setting the hearing.

votes.item_title: Item 18: Major Special Use Permit — Crestwood Suites Renovations
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the quasi-judicial major special use permit for Crestwood Suites renovations subject to Attachment 7 plan consistency.

votes.item_title: Item 19: Major Site Plan and Floodplain Development Permit — Crestwood Suites Renovations

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 6, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council presented an Earth Month proclamation, recognized local youth mentorship participants, requested a memorial resolution for historian Dr. John Hope Franklin, and noted protest petition validity for upcoming zoning cases (valid on Item 34, invalid on Item 43). The Council unanimously approved the Consent Agenda (excluding pulled Item 16) 7-0, conducted public hearings on a University Drive sidewalk petition (Item 31) and an elections/charter item preceding Item 45 (passing 7-0), and later approved pulled Consent Item 16 (employment and training incumbent-worker grant ordinance amendment) 7-0 after staff confirmed the funds train existing workers at Durham businesses. On Item 45, the proposed economic development job-creation incentive agreement with Burt's Bees, Inc. for downtown Durham, speakers and Council members discussed local unemployment, first-source recruitment through the Durham JobLink Career Center, workforce demographics, and South Deck parking impacts; although the formal vote call fell within an omitted transcript gap, Mayor Bell thanked company representatives and welcomed Burt's Bees downtown. Before adjourning at 11:02 PM, the City Manager also confirmed staff had begun preparatory steps toward the proposed July solid waste and recycling program changes, with a status report requested by Howard Clement III.

agenda_items.title: Earth Month Proclamation, Youth Recognition, and Dr. John Hope Franklin Resolution Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented an Earth Month proclamation highlighting Keep Durham Beautiful and Parks and Recreation's waste-free event, and recognized Julie King as well as youth mentoring participants and parents ahead of their June trip to Winston-Salem. meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 19, 2009 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council approved priority items from the City Manager and City Attorney, including an urgent supplemental item (Item 46) with Durham County Attorney Chuck Kitchen to clear deed restrictions on a Peabody Street parcel for the County Health and Human Services campus financing. Under suspended rules, the Council unanimously approved Item 19 (the annual insurance program, 7-0), Item 21 (an interlocal reimbursement agreement to seek modification of the Jordan Lake rules, 7-0), and Item 46 (quitclaim deed authorization for the County Health and Human Services parcel, 7-0). Staff also presented two proposed year-round water conservation ordinances—requiring rain/moisture sensors, separate meters for new in-ground irrigation systems starting July 1, 2009, and enforceable water-waste and leak-repair standards—while coordinating common regional drought terminology with Raleigh, Chapel Hill, Cary, Apex, and OWASA. Council closed the session by setting the April 6 regular meeting agenda and voting unanimously to enter closed session on pending litigation.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Congressional Update, and Manager/Attorney Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:08 PM with all seven members present, and a Council member reported on a Washington visit with Senator Hagan and Representatives Price, Miller, and Butterfield. The City Manager flagged priority items for immediate action (Items 13, 19, 21, 42) and April 6 public hearings (Items 43, 44, and an economic development incentive item), while the City Attorney requested a closed session on three lawsuits and added emergency Item 46 regarding the County Health and Human Services campus.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review and Immediate Action on Items 19 and 21
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed Consent Items 13 through 27, pulling Item 20 (multi-site park renovation capital project ordinance amendment) for discussion. agenda_items.title: Year-Round Water Conservation, Irrigation Efficiency, and Water Waste Ordinances
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle section, staff presented two proposed year-round water efficiency ordinances developed in regional consensus with Raleigh, Chapel Hill, Cary, Apex, and OWASA: one requiring rain/moisture sensors (retrofits within 180 days) and separate meters for new in-ground irrigation systems effective July 1, 2009, and a second prohibiting water waste and mandating timely leak repairs with escalating notices, two fine tiers, and service termination. Council Member Eugene Brown questioned whether runoff language would prohibit residents from washing cars on downward-sloping driveways.

agenda_items.title: Setting the April 6 Regular Meeting Agenda and Entering Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk read the slate for the April 6, 2009 regular meeting (Consent Items 1–12, 14–18, 20, and 22–27; General Business public hearings Items 31–37 and 45), which Council approved by voice vote. Council then voted unanimously to enter closed session in the committee room for attorney-client consultation under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3).

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 16, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, first- and second-grade students from Carter Community School opened with a performance of 'It Takes a Village,' and Council approved the Consent Agenda (excluding pulled Items 17 and 34) 7-0 along with unanimous 7-0 votes on an East Geer Street water main assessment correction (Item 22) and three voluntary annexations (Item 23). Following public criticism over urban tree canopy loss, impervious surface limits, and watershed land-banking ratios, the Council unanimously adopted pulled Item 34 (the Stormwater Development Performance Standards Ordinance) 7-0 after staff clarified that peak-flow controls remain mandatory and that exemptions were narrowed to Downtown, Urban Transit, and Compact Neighborhood tiers. On pulled Item 17 (FY2010 Budget Development Guidelines), Mayor Bell added a sustainability and energy-efficiency directive, and the Council approved Item 17 overall 7-0 in a partial split: one Council member (garbled in the transcript ASR as 'council and the' and not unambiguously named) voted No specifically on the page-three bullet barring funding for new non-city agencies, while all seven members voted Yes on the remainder of the guidelines (6-1 on that single provision). Council also unanimously approved a closed session on economic development under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4).

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden welcomed Carter Community School Principal Gail Taylor, teachers, parents, and first- and second-grade students to perform 'It Takes a Village to Raise a Child.' Council Member Mike Woodard congratulated downtown creative firms Flywheel Design and Splinter Group on winning eight ADDY Awards each and thanked volunteers for Brookline Trail work, while Council approved 7-0 the City Manager's request for a post-meeting closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) on industrial location/expansion.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Excluding Items 17 and 34)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the Consent Agenda items, including advisory board appointments, RDU/DATA items, Research Triangle Park site plan D06-977 (Item 13), Self-Help contract amendment (Item 15), general obligation bond reimbursement resolution (Item 16), Fugitive Apprehension Task Force agreement (Item 18), and Water and Sewer Contract WS-81-2009 (Item 19). With Items 17 and 34 pulled for separate discussion, the Consent Agenda passed 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearings: East Geer Street Water Main Assessment (Item 22), Voluntary Annexations (Item 23), and Treyburn Middle School Rezoning (Item 24)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council held public hearings and voted 7-0 on Item 22 (correcting a water main assessment roll error for Walter R. Smith on East Geer Street) and 7-0 on Item 23 (voluntary annexations for Alexander Village 2, Bethpage 2, and Colton Harris properties, showing a net fiscal gain). Planning staff then began presenting Item 24 (New Middle School Treyburn zoning map change Z08-034) before the middle portion of the transcript was truncated.

agenda_items.title: Stormwater Development Performance Standards Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained a revised amendment limiting the greatest imperviousness leniency to the Downtown Development, Urban Transit, and Compact Neighborhood tiers rather than citywide by density. Speakers Mr. Wilson and Tina Motley-Pearson objected to off-site land banking ratios (one acre built for half an acre preserved), higher urban runoff, reduced urban tree canopy, and protecting critical watershed land already largely protected, while another speaker urged prioritizing green space already designated in watershed plans such as across from E.K. Powe; staff responded that redevelopment reduces existing loads and peak-flow controls remain required, and Council approved Item 34 unanimously.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell requested adding a guideline requiring budget submissions to address sustainability and energy efficiency goals, which the City Manager agreed to incorporate. One Council member (name garbled in ASR as 'council and the') moved to vote No specifically on the page-three bullet barring funding for new non-city agencies while voting Yes on the rest of Item 17; the item passed 7-0 overall with that single No recorded on the non-city agencies bullet.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to the City Manager's earlier priority request.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 5, 2009 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council reviewed early policy items including a request for staff to examine Raleigh's upcoming rental registration program, upcoming federal stimulus highway project selections at TAC, and a debate over DATA transit board governance prompted by the Merrick-Moore / Focus School memorandum. Council Member Howard Clement III argued that citizens and schools aggrieved by transit board route decisions should have a codified right to appeal to City Council in an ordinance rather than relying on informal Council budget pressure, and asked the City Manager to return with a report. The Council approved the City Manager's priority items (deferring immediate action on Item 17 and requesting rule suspension on Item 33, the sale of 601 Eastway Avenue). Later in the session, staff presented a detailed cost and compliance briefing on the Stormwater Development Performance Standards Ordinance (Item 34)—illustrating on-site bioretention (~$45,000) and off-site donor parcel requirements using the DPAC site—heard Citizens' Matters from Vanessa Alston and Willie Jackson, and received an update on NCDOT's requirement to use a single contract to demolish and replace the NC 147 pedestrian bridge.

agenda_items.title: Rental Registration Inquiry, University Comparisons, and Stimulus Highway Projects
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell opened the work session at 1:05 PM with all seven members present. A Council member asked staff to review Raleigh's rental registration program launching in late April to see if Durham should revisit the policy; another member asked why Duke could not match a program offered by Yale; and Council noted the upcoming Wednesday Transportation Advisory Committee meeting to approve the first round of federal stimulus highway projects.

agenda_items.title: Focus School / Merrick-Moore Memorandum and DATA Transit Board Citizen Appeal Rights
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Discussing a memorandum regarding Focus School and past Merrick-Moore School transit concerns, Council Member Howard Clement III asked whether citizens or schools aggrieved by DATA board decisions have a formal right of appeal. After the City Attorney explained that no formal appellate procedure exists in the ordinance—though Council exerts informal influence via budget control—Clement argued the right to appeal ought to be codified by ordinance, and Council requested a follow-up administrative report from the City Manager.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items and Convention & Visitors Bureau Nomination
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager clarified that Item 17 should proceed through regular channels rather than rule suspension, requested suspending the rules for Item 33 (sale of 601 Eastway Avenue), noted Item 34 (stormwater standards) would return for update, and scheduled Public Works' update on the pedestrian bridge. Council approved the Manager's priority items by voice vote, and the City Clerk presented the Mayor's nominee for the Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau / Tourism Development Authority.

agenda_items.title: Stormwater Development Performance Standards Ordinance Briefing (DPAC Cost Example)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle section, Planning/Stormwater staff explained that the proposed ordinance satisfies Senate Bill 845 (April 1 deadline) and NPDES permit requirements (June 30 deadline) rather than Jordan Lake rules, and presented a DPAC site-plan cost analysis estimating $45,000 for on-site bioretention plus a half-acre off-site donor parcel. Council members discussed urban tier on-site percentages, street standards, Cape Fear vs. Jordan Lake constraints, and ensuring staff nail down clear off-site parcel procedures so developers are not left in uncertainty.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments from Vanessa Alston and Willie Jackson
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vanessa Alston disputed water billing and disconnection records from June 18 after staff explained the difference between a water service cut-off and a stationary leak-indicator dial. Citizen Willie Jackson raised a police matter and was directed to bring the concern through the City Manager's office.

agenda_items.title: NCDOT Response on NC 147 Pedestrian Bridge Demolition and Replacement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works staff reported that NCDOT declined to split demolition and reconstruction of the pedestrian bridge into two contracts because doing so would violate the project's structure, forfeit existing bids, and require months of renegotiation and Board of Transportation approval. Consequently, the city would proceed under a single contract to demolish the existing bridge while completing long-lead shop drawings for the replacement span.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager Priority Items
