meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 2, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council issued a Multiple Sclerosis Awareness Week proclamation, invited Carter Community School students to perform at City Hall, and requested a memorial resolution for Nathaniel Bradshaw White Sr. On the City Manager's priority motion, Council voted 7-0 to refer Item 20 (Stormwater Development Performance Standards Ordinance) back to administration until March 16 for state review. On the Consent Agenda (excluding pulled Item 15 and deferred Item 20), six members—Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, and Farad Ali—voted Aye on all items, while Diane Catotti voted No specifically on Item 19 (Contract Amendment No. 3, Contract ST-227 for 2006 Street Improvements), resulting in a 6-1 approval of Item 19 and 7-0 approval of the remaining Consent items. Council also heard the 2008 Annual Crime Report (noting a under-1% rise in crime rate per 100,000, 191 confiscated weapons, and 1,099 arrests), set an April 6 public hearing on the municipal election process change, and voted 7-0 to approve pulled Consent Item 15 affirming the current monthly plan amendment public hearing process.

agenda_items.title: MS Awareness Week Proclamation and Memorial Resolution for Nathaniel Bradshaw White Sr.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell introduced a proclamation declaring March 2–8, 2009 as Multiple Sclerosis Awareness Week. Council members congratulated Carter Community School on its Walltown history production and Clean Energy Durham on 'Get Unplugged,' and Howard Clement III thanked Congressman Price and NCDOT Secretary Gene Conti while requesting a memorial resolution for Nathaniel Bradshaw White Sr.

agenda_items.title: Deferral of Item 20 (Stormwater Development Performance Standards) to March 16, 2009
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested referring Item 20 (Stormwater Development Performance Standards Ordinance) back to the administration for one cycle until March 16, 2009 so staff could incorporate state review comments and meet with stakeholders on Thursday. Council approved the manager's priority motion unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval and Split Vote on Item 19 (Contract ST-227 Amendment 3)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered the Consent Agenda covering voluntary annexation petitions, police property room audit, Habitat for Humanity subrecipient contract, Rolling Hills budget authority, Greyhound lease at Durham Station, Walltown Park Recreation Center inspections, and street/drainage contracts, with Item 15 pulled and Item 20 deferred. Before the vote, Council Member Diane Catotti announced her intent to vote No on Item 19 (Contract Amendment No. 3, Contract ST-227, 2006 Street Improvements) consistent with her work session position; the Consent Agenda passed 7-0 with Catotti recorded No on Item 19 (6-1).

agenda_items.title: 2008 Annual Crime Report Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police presented the 2008 Annual Crime Report, noting the overall crime rate per 100,000 population rose slightly less than 1%. Targeted enforcement operations utilized $273,000 in overtime funds to serve 2,141 warrants, conduct 13 prostitution operations, confiscate 191 firearms and weapons, make 1,099 custodial arrests, and refer six individuals to a High Point-style Second Chance drug market intervention program.

agenda_items.title: Schedule and Materials for Municipal Election Process Public Hearing (April 6, 2009)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following passage of a resolution setting a public hearing (in the truncated middle section), Council clarified that the public hearing would be held April 6, 2009 so Council could act within the 60-day statutory window rather than waiting until June. Diane Catotti requested that all background materials be posted online and at City Hall, and Howard Clement III—noting his newspaper announcement to seek re-election—requested cost figures given the economic downturn.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Resolution passed prior to timestamp (tally omitted in digest truncation)

agenda_items.title: Plan Amendment Public Hearing Process Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff reported that the Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) reviewed a citizen request to revert from monthly to quarterly plan amendment processing and recommended keeping the current monthly process because quarterly cycles split rezonings from plan amendments and existing rules provide website posting plus mailed notices within 600 feet (property owners) and 1,000 feet (neighborhood associations). A citizen urged broader advance summaries so the electorate can stay informed before decisions, and Council approved Item 15 unanimously.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 19, 2009 City Council Work Session, Mayor Bill Bell presided initially before departing early (with unanimous Council excuse) to attend a White House meeting on the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act stimulus, leaving Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presiding for the remainder of the session. Early actions passed unanimously, including swearing in James C. Henry to the Capital Program Advisory Committee, waiving/suspending rules to appoint three Cultural Master Plan Advisory Board members, approving Manager and Attorney priority items, and excusing absence requests for Friday's budget retreat; Howard Clement III also urged revisiting DATA board governance so City Council has final authority over bus routes. After a truncated middle section, Council debated Center Parking Deck structural repairs—tracing defects back to missing plaza waterproofing from 1989—and roughly $2 million in projected operating costs for new recreation centers, leading staff to recommend halting acquisition of the Trinity Recreation Center and Council unanimously approving the suspended-rules parking/facility item. Council also reviewed updated neighborhood-input rules for the Brighten Our Streets lighting program, heard Northeast Central Durham / Watts Hospital-Hillandale residents, and set the March 2 regular meeting agenda with one unidentified vocal 'no' objection noted during the voice vote.

agenda_items.title: White House Stimulus Invitation, Retreat Absences, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell opened the work session at 1:03 PM and requested an excused early departure and absence from Friday's budget retreat after receiving a White House invitation to meet with the President, Vice President, and cabinet secretaries on the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act. Council unanimously excused Mayor Bell and another member attending a D.C. business roundtable, approved City Manager priority items (including rule suspension on Item 14 with Durham Center Investors and reordering Item 26 greenhouse gas update), and noted a 2:00 PM Board of Elections presentation on changing Council election methods.

agenda_items.title: CPAC Swearing-In, Cultural Master Plan Appointments, and DATA Bus Route Governance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: James C. Henry was sworn in to the Capital Program Advisory Committee, and Council unanimously suspended the rules to appoint three members to the Cultural Master Plan Advisory Board. Council Member Howard Clement III then urged placing the relationship between City Council and the DATA board on a future agenda, arguing Council—not DATA—should be the ultimate arbiter of bus routes, followed by a brief water conservation status update.

agenda_items.title: Parking Deck Structural Repairs and Trinity Recreation Center Budget Constraints
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion, Council discussed Marriott/Center parking deck gate congestion, a new middle-level exit, and structural defects stemming from unaddressed plaza waterproofing since 1989. Staff explained that combined new operating costs for Trinity, Walltown, Holton, and potentially Parkwood recreation centers approached $2 million amid tight budgets, prompting staff to recommend halting Trinity Recreation Center acquisition; Council Member Diane Catotti requested a broader budget discussion of recreation facilities, and Council reluctantly approved the suspended-rules item unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Brighten Our Streets Policy Update and Watts Hospital-Hillandale Neighborhood Concerns
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated Council on the street lighting program (formerly Brighten Our Streets), adding a third leg of formal neighborhood input via Neighborhood Improvement Services alongside Police crime review and Public Works technical review, while keeping a higher threshold for light removals due to Duke Energy financial obligations. Ned Kennington and Steve of the Watts Hospital-Hillandale Neighborhood Association addressed Council after waiting seven months, and Mike Woodard requested a staff response and recommendations before March 2 or the next work session.

agenda_items.title: Setting the March 2, 2009 Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk read the March 2, 2009 Regular Meeting agenda (Consent Items 1–2, 4–13, 15–24; General Business 28 and 34; Public Hearings 29–30). During the voice vote presided over by Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, an unidentified voice answered when she asked if anyone wanted to say no, and she declared the motion carried before adjourning.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (voice vote with one unidentified 'no' exchange)

votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Excused Mayor Bell to attend a White House meeting on the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act stimulus program.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager Priority Items
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously (also re-affirmed at 00:06:12).
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted City Manager's priority items (Item 14 rule suspension, Item 25 at 2:30 PM, Item 26 moved first, Item 32 citizen absence, and water report).

votes.item_title: Excuse Council Member Absence for Friday Budget Retreat
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Excused a Council member attending a Friday business roundtable in Washington, D.C.

votes.discussion_detail: Suspended the rules (00:08:49) and approved appointing three individuals to the Cultural Master Plan Advisory Board.

votes.notes: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden after Mayor Bell's excused departure; voice vote passed without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved suspended-rules item following discussion of Center Parking Deck repair funding and Trinity Recreation Center capital/operating constraints; Council member stated they reluctantly moved the item because 'we don't have a choice.'

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 22, 2009 Durham City Council Work Session opened and presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden (with Mayor Bill Bell delayed at another meeting and Howard Clement III noted absent during later citizen remarks), Council approved the City Manager's priority items and unanimously suspended the rules to waive the one-month advertising rule for Cultural Master Plan Advisory Board appointments. Council reviewed consent items—including supportive housing awards for CASA and Self-Help, police computer leases, and upcoming public hearings on Findlay Glen (Z0800007) and backyard female chickens (TC0800006)—and heard the Capital Program Advisory Committee (CPAC) quarterly report highlighting floodplain impacts on city parks like Northgate Park, waterline leakage, bond-to-shovel timelines, and obtaining DENR approval for Teer Quarry as an offline drought reservoir. Following a truncated middle section, Council engaged in a substantive policy debate over Item 25 (2009 Legislative Program), specifically whether to include a local 'bullet proposal' restricting handgun ammunition purchases: opponents/skeptics raised legislative protocol objections—noting there was no bill sponsor, no drafted legislation, and no backing from North Carolinians Against Gun Violence—and urged focusing on the city's $3–4 million current-year budget shortfall, whereas proponents argued gun violence was an epidemic requiring action to close the gap allowing prohibited handgun buyers to purchase bullets legally; the City Attorney agreed to draft simpler statutory wording for the February 2 meeting. Council concluded by setting the February 2 regular meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Manager Priority Items and Cultural Master Plan Advertising Waiver
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the work session to order with Mayor Bill Bell delayed at another meeting. Council approved the City Manager's priority items (noting absent Citizens' Matters speakers on Items 20–21 and adding Item 25, the 2009 Legislative Program outline) and voted unanimously to suspend the rules and waive the one-month advertising requirement for Cultural Master Plan Advisory Board appointments.

agenda_items.title: Consent & Public Hearing Review and CPAC Quarterly Report (Item 16)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed upcoming consent items (memorial resolutions for James Moses Schooler Sr. and Trevor Devon Spain, CASA and Self-Help housing grants, police computer lease, and state loan execution) and public hearings (Findlay Glen and backyard female chickens). The Capital Program Advisory Committee (CPAC) then delivered its quarterly report urging continued waterline replacement for leakage, DENR approval of Teer Quarry as an offline reservoir, and realistic scheduling of floodplain and administrative approvals between voter bond passage and 'shovel-ready' park construction.

agenda_items.title: 2009 Legislative Program Debate: Handgun Ammunition Purchase Restrictions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle section, Council debated adding a handgun ammunition ('bullet') purchase restriction to the 2009 state legislative agenda. Skeptics cited protocol concerns—no bill sponsor, no drafted text, and lack of endorsement from North Carolinians Against Gun Violence, which prioritized gun-show loopholes and safe storage—and urged focusing on the city's $3–4 million current-year budget shortfall; supporters argued rising gun violence is an epidemic and closing the loophole barring prohibited handgun buyers from buying bullets is the right policy, leading the City Attorney to offer simplified draft language for the February 2 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Courthouse & Correctional Enterprise Revenue Remarks and Setting the February 2 Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A speaker requested that Durham pursue a return of local courthouse revenues and state correctional enterprise revenues ($98 million statewide). Council then approved setting the February 2, 2009 Regular Meeting agenda (Consent Items 1–15 and 25; Public Hearings 17–19).

disagreements.issue: Inclusion of Handgun Ammunition ('Bullet') Purchase Restriction in 2009 Legislative Agenda (Item 25)
disagreements.summary: Council members debated whether to include a proposal restricting handgun ammunition sales in Durham's 2009 state legislative package despite lacking a legislative sponsor, draft bill language, or backing from statewide gun-control advocates.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support including the ammunition purchase restriction in the legislative agenda to close a gap in gun violence prevention.
side_a_arguments: Gun violence in Durham is an epidemic crisis requiring local leadership even if state passage is difficult.
People prohibited from legally buying handguns due to criminal records or mental illness can still walk into stores and buy bullets legally.
Urged Council and the Crime Cabinet (meeting in March) to stand behind tying ammunition eligibility to legal firearm purchase eligibility.
disagreements.side_b_position: Question inclusion based on legislative protocol, missing bill sponsorship, and competing budget priorities.
side_b_arguments: Neither the local legislative delegation nor North Carolinians Against Gun Violence (which is prioritizing safe storage, gun-show loopholes, and anti-bullying bills) supports the proposal, and there is no sponsor or drafted legislation.
State-level gun legislation should not distract Council from focusing 'like a laser beam' on the city's $3–4 million current-year budget shortfall.
disagreements.resolution: Deferred for vote at the February 2, 2009 Regular Meeting, with the City Attorney directed to draft simpler language tying ammunition purchases to legal firearm purchase eligibility (speaker attribution in the digest was largely unnamed except a reference to 'what Farad was saying' and Mayor Bell's view that it is a state issue).

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 21, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting (rescheduled to Wednesday evening) presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven Council members present, the Council focused on federal economic stimulus advocacy, HUD community development needs, and anti-gang grant funding. Council unanimously accepted a City Manager priority item (7-0) and later unanimously adopted Agenda Item 35 (7-0, moved by Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden), a resolution supporting Durham's participation in the federal stimulus package with shovel-ready projects and direct funding to localities rather than routing solely through state government. The Consent Agenda minus Item 19 passed 7-0, covering items such as Crestry Community Council and Self-Help CDC housing agreements, HOME funding reallocation to Durham Community Land Trustees, Fayetteville Road and South Roxboro Street property acquisitions, Northgate Park improvements, Police District 3 substation lease, and Triangle Transit reimbursement. During the FY 2009-2010 Annual Action Plan needs public hearing (Item 26, informational with no vote), Cole-McFadden and Council Member Howard Clement III raised concerns about tracking and implementing the 10-Year Plan to End Homelessness. On pulled Consent Item 19 (FY 2008 Comprehensive Anti-Gang Initiative grant), a public speaker objected to using $60,000 for an Assistant District Attorney position instead of youth intervention programs, but Assistant Police Chief Jim Bearstrom clarified the funding preserves an existing court position previously backed by an expired Byrne grant, and Council passed the item 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the Wednesday evening meeting to order at 7:04 p.m., Council Member Howard Clement III led the Pledge of Allegiance, and the Clerk confirmed all seven Council members were present. Council members reflected on local Martin Luther King Jr. weekend celebrations, the January 20 presidential inauguration of Barack Obama, a Preservation Durham luncheon on historic preservation as an economic development tool, and mayors' meetings with Senators Kay Hagan and Richard Burr on federal stimulus funding.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item: Agenda Item 35 (Federal Stimulus Package Resolution)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager introduced one priority item, Agenda Item 35, a resolution supporting the City of Durham playing a role in the federal economic stimulus package that Mayor Bill Bell had raised during the work session. The City Attorney and City Clerk reported no priority items.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Item 19)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent items including a redesigned citizen water bill, housing subrecipient agreements with Crestry Community Council Inc. and Self-Help CDC, FY08-09 HOME funding reallocation to Durham Community Land Trustees Inc., a COPS reimbursement resolution, property acquisitions for Fayetteville Road widening Phase 2 and South Roxboro Street extension, Northgate Park and Old North Durham Park items, a nine-year lease for Police Substation District 3, controlled substance/asset forfeiture funds, utility extension agreements, and a Triangle Transit Authority Special Transit Advisory Commission reimbursement amendment. Council approved the Consent Agenda with the exception of Item 19.

agenda_items.title: Item 26 Public Hearing: FY 2009-2010 Annual Action Plan Needs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant Director of Community Development Larry Jarvis opened the first of two required HUD public hearings to gather community input on federal funding needs and priorities, noting no formal Council action was required. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden asked how expenditures under the 10-Year Plan to End Homelessness are tracked and voiced concern about implementation, Council Member Howard Clement III echoed concern over the homelessness plan's progress, and Loreisa's Bible of the Durham Affordable Housing Coalition addressed Council.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Item 35: Resolution in Support of Durham's Role in the Federal Stimulus Package
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed a refined list of projects able to enter contracts within 90 days and discussed provisions supporting direct local grants and STP transportation funds rather than state-routed funding, as well as Army Corps of Engineers spending flexibility raised by Council Member Diane Catotti. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved adoption, Council Member Eugene Brown criticized the state's historical shortchanging of major cities, and Council Member Howard Clement III asked for specifics on shovel-ready projects and urged sending the resolution directly to White House officials in addition to Durham's congressional delegation.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 19: FY 2008 Comprehensive Anti-Gang Initiative Grant Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A public speaker objected to allocating $60,000 from the $1.2 million anti-gang initiative grant toward an Assistant District Attorney position rather than youth gang intervention programs, arguing the Durham County courthouse already generated over $16-17 million annually. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden noted the prosecutor is already on board and courts are underfunded, and Assistant Police Chief Jim Bearstrom clarified the position had been funded since 1998 via an Edward Byrne grant that expired, meaning the DA would lose an existing prosecutor without this bridge funding.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager Priority Item (Agenda Item 35: Federal Stimulus Package Resolution)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest; all seven members were confirmed present at roll call and Mayor Bill Bell announced the motion passed 7 to 0.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to add the City Manager's priority item (Agenda Item 35, resolution supporting Durham's role in the federal economic stimulus package) to the meeting agenda.

votes.notes: Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden at [01:26:29]; seconder was not named in the transcript digest. Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Adoption of the resolution advocating for direct federal stimulus funding to local governments, STP transportation routing, and shovel-ready projects in Durham.

votes.item_title: Pulled Consent Item 19: Contract for City of Durham FY 2008 Comprehensive Anti-Gang Initiative Grant
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest; passed 7-0 following public comment and clarification from Assistant Chief Jim Bearstrom.
votes.discussion_detail: Approval of the FY 2008 Comprehensive Anti-Gang Initiative grant contract, including $60,000 to retain an existing Assistant District Attorney position after Edward Byrne grant funds expired.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 5, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven Council members present, the Council opened the new year with a National Mentoring Month proclamation and acted on federal housing stabilization, transit, public safety, and street resurfacing contracts. Council unanimously approved adding priority Agenda Item 28 (7-0) and subsequently approved the Neighborhood Stabilization Program application timeline to hold a January 21 public hearing ahead of the February 3 submission deadline. On pulled Consent Items 12 and 13, Council responded to public questions about using federal asset forfeiture funds for prevention versus law enforcement equipment and sharing JARC/New Freedom transit grants with Chapel Hill, approving Item 12 (7-0) and Item 13 unanimously. On pulled Consent Item 14 (Contract ST-233 for 2009 street repairs and resurfacing with Barnhill Contracting Company), Council members questioned why the $3+ million contract fell short of Durham's 7% M/SDBE and 2% SDBE goals and used a Raleigh trucking subcontractor, and unanimously voted to defer the contract to the Thursday work session for service-area and legal workforce-monitoring review. Council also unanimously excused Council Member Eugene Brown from the Thursday work session and noted an earlier public hearing on backyard chickens/hens.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, National Mentoring Month Proclamation, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the first meeting of 2009 to order at 7:00 p.m., Council Member Howard Clement III led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven members answered roll call. Mayor Bell presented a proclamation declaring January 2009 National Mentoring Month, and Council members offered community tributes and announcements regarding James M. Schooler Sr., Trevor Spain, Sarah Woodard, Eagle Scouts Alexander Catotti and Steve Mihaich's son, and the evening's public hearing on backyard chickens.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item: Agenda Item 28 (Neighborhood Stabilization Program Submittal)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager presented one priority item, Agenda Item 28, requesting to set a January 21, 2009 public hearing on the Neighborhood Stabilization Program (NSP) application submittal. Council accepted the priority item onto the agenda by a 7-0 vote, and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden recognized city employee Beverly Thompson on becoming a Deacon.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Items 12, 13, and 14)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read Consent Agenda Items 1-15, including minutes, Housing Appeals Board and Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority appointments, automated-arm refuse collection vehicles, a 104-foot aerial ladder purchase, street acceptances, the FY 2009-2010 Annual Action Plan public hearing notice, a U.S. Marshals Joint Fugitive Task Force MOU, and a Cary-Durham water and sewer mutual aid agreement. A motion to approve the Consent Agenda excluding Items 12, 13, and 14 (pulled by Ms. Peterson) was moved and seconded, though the vote tally and subsequent middle items (including the backyard chickens public hearing referenced later by Council Member Eugene Brown) were truncated in the digest.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Motion moved and seconded (outcome truncated in digest)

agenda_items.title: Agenda Item 28: Neighborhood Stabilization Program Application Submittal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council confirmed the schedule for the Neighborhood Stabilization Program application, noting the January 21, 2009 public hearing would allow time to incorporate public input and adjust the plan prior to the February 3, 2009 federal submission deadline. Council voted to approve the item.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 12: Controlled Substance Abuse and Federal Asset Forfeiture Funds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speaker Ms. Peterson urged the City to direct drug and asset forfeiture dollars toward prevention and intervention programs rather than solely law enforcement equipment. Police representative Steve Mihaich explained the rules governing federal asset forfeiture funds, and Council Member Howard Clement III clarified whether intervention and interdiction qualify as law enforcement purposes before Council approved the item.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 13: 2007-2008 Job Access Reverse Commute and New Freedom Grant Ordinances
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ms. Peterson questioned how Durham shares federal JARC and New Freedom transportation grant dollars with Chapel Hill. Staff member Mr. Nave responded to the inquiry, and Council approved the grant project ordinances without opposition.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 14: Contract ST-233 2009 Street Repairs and Resurfacing (Barnhill Contracting)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public remarks on local workforce demographics, Council members scrutinized Barnhill Contracting Company's failure to meet the 7% M/SDBE and 2% SDBE goals (achieving 1% and 1.17% on the $3+ million contract) and questioned the use of a Raleigh trucking subcontractor. Council requested staff (Deborah Giles) and Barnhill (John Needle) to clarify the ordinance's service area and asked City Attorney Baker to advise on Thursday regarding legal limits on monitoring contractor workforces, voting unanimously to defer the item to the Thursday work session.

agenda_items.title: Council Business: Excused Absence for Eugene Brown and Meeting Schedule Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted unanimously to excuse Council Member Eugene Brown from the upcoming Thursday work session so he could transport his grandson back to Denver. Brown also praised the dialogue during the earlier public hearing on backyard hens and suggested formatting the upcoming State of the City address to generate similar community engagement on crime reduction, after which Council confirmed upcoming meeting dates and adjourned at 9:01 p.m.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 15, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council recognized Bill of Rights Day, Durham's #10 national ranking for National Night Out, and the Hero Book Project, while Council Member Eugene Brown and colleagues criticized North Carolina's state probation system and urged legislative reform by the General Assembly. Council unanimously approved (7-0) two City Manager priority supplemental street-closing items (Sumter Street and Maxwell Street) and the consent agenda covering fleet and police equipment purchases, building assessments at Five Points, Rock Quarry Park field renovations, and an annexation boundary hearing with Cary. In public hearings, Council unanimously approved (7-0) neighborhood retail incentive contracts with Prestige Automotive Repair and Apogee Fine Foods LLC after community support from PAC 1 and Triangle Citizens Rebuilding Communities, and voted unanimously (7-0) to continue the Sumter Street closing to January 21, 2009. Council also held public hearings on Duke University street-closing requests for Cook Street and Maxwell Street, with Maxwell Street moved and seconded for a two-cycle continuance to January 21, 2009 before adjournment at 8:03 p.m. All recorded votes at the meeting were unanimous with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Ceremonial Recognitions (Bill of Rights Day, National Night Out, Hero Book Project)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. and the Clerk confirmed all seven Council members were present. Mayor Bell presented a proclamation declaring December 15, 2008 as Bill of Rights Day reaffirming non-discrimination and Durham's 2003 policy regarding civil immigration status, and joined Police Chief Jose Lopez to celebrate Durham ranking #10 nationally for National Night Out with local law enforcement, media, and Target partners. Council also recognized students and visual artist Rachel Galper for the 2008 Hero Book Project.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Announcements and State Probation System Critique
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden urged youth mentorship and recounted taking 17 Salvation Army Boys and Girls Club youth to a Charlotte Bobcats game, a resolution honoring late community promoter Jim 'Uncle Bubba' Fields was requested, and Council Member Farad Ali congratulated GlaxoSmithKline's Bill Shaw and County Commissioner Becky Heron on Leadership Triangle's Goodman Awards. Council Member Eugene Brown and a colleague criticized state officials and the General Assembly over failures in North Carolina's probation system—citing Wake and Durham as the worst counties and referencing a slain Duke engineering graduate student—and called for legislative reform.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items and Office of Public Affairs Awards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager introduced two supplemental priority items added to the agenda: Item 18 (Sumter Street closure) and Item 19 (Maxwell Street closure), which Council approved unanimously 7-0. The City Manager also reported national communications awards won by Durham's Office of Public Affairs at the City-County Communications and Marketing Association conference for its 2007 Annual Report and 'City Life' show.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Fleet, Police Equipment, Five Points Assessment, Rock Quarry Park, Cary Annexation Hearing)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed and approved the consent agenda, including three tandem-axle cab-and-chassis trucks, a sole-source Taser purchase, October 2008 bid report, street acceptances, Fire Department janitorial contract amendment, building assessment for city-owned commercial properties at Five Points, Employee Health Services lease amendment, Imagine Durham accountability contract, emergency management agreement amendment, Rock Quarry Park field renovation funding, a Kimley-Horn strategic deployment plan, setting a public hearing on a Cary-Durham annexation boundary agreement, and Contract SR-44 Chapel Hill Street outfall.

agenda_items.title: Item 15: Retail Incentive Grant Contracts (Prestige Automotive Repair Service and Apogee Fine Foods LLC)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mike Keeler of the Office of Economic and Workforce Development presented merchandise-based retail incentive grant contracts with Prestige Automotive Repair Service and Apogee Fine Foods LLC. During the public hearing, Victoria Peterson of Triangle Citizens Rebuilding Communities supported the project and asked the City Manager for an additional $500,000 for the incentive program, and former PAC 1 co-facilitator Gwen Silver stated PAC 1 supported all three businesses. Council closed the hearing and approved the contracts unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Item 16: Street Closing of 75 Linear Feet of Cook Street (SC0800013)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Medlin of the Durham City-County Planning Department presented Duke University's request to permanently close 75 linear feet of Cook Street. After brief discussion in which a Council member noted saving remarks for Item 19, Council opened and closed the vote on the item.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 1, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present following the community opening of the Durham Performing Arts Center (DPAC), Council presented a memorial resolution honoring pioneering African-American photojournalist Alexander M. 'Alex' Rivera, Jr. Council debated a request to hold a public hearing on the planned Adam & Eve retail store at Fayetteville Road and NC 54, with Planning Director Steve Medlin and Mayor Bell explaining that the store was a by-right retail use in the Commercial Neighborhood (CN) zone outside Council's authority to overturn. Council unanimously voted (7-0) to refer Item 29 (downtown nightclubs and bars UDO text amendment) back to the administration, and later in the meeting unanimously approved (7-0) UDO text amendments extending weekend carnival hours to 11 p.m. and allowing registered parties to choose email or paid mail public notices (TC0800008), a technical rezoning for the Poss House at 1514 Pinecrest Road (Z0800030), and the pulled Golden Belt neighborhood revitalization report (Item 8). All votes recorded in the available digest were unanimous (7-0), with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Memorial Resolution for Alexander M. Rivera, Jr.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:08 p.m. after Council attended the community opening of the Durham Performing Arts Center, and the Clerk confirmed all seven members were present. Council presented a resolution memorializing pioneering photojournalist Alexander M. 'Alex' Rivera, Jr., who established the first news bureau at North Carolina College for Negroes in 1939, to family friends Dr. Otis Washington and Robert Lawson.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of Planned Adam & Eve Retail Store at Fayetteville Road and NC 54
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A Council member urged holding a public hearing for over a thousand residents expressing outrage over the planned Adam & Eve project at Fayetteville Road and NC 54. Planning Director Steve Medlin explained the 15,000-square-foot two-building site is zoned Commercial Neighborhood (CN, under the 20,000-square-foot cap) and does not meet the UDO or statutory definition of an adult establishment, and Mayor Bell cautioned against holding a hearing that could raise false expectations since Council cannot legally overturn a by-right retail use.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item (Referral of Item 29) and Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy City Manager requested that Agenda Item 29 (UDO text amendment for downtown nightclubs and bars) be referred back to the administration, which Council approved 7-0. Mayor Bell read the Consent Agenda—including CDBG subrecipient contracts, DPAC naming rights with Scientific Properties, minimum livable wage ordinance amendment, and Holton Center interlocal amendment—with Item 8 (Golden Belt) pulled for separate discussion; the Consent Agenda vote occurred during a section omitted from the transcript digest.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 on Priority Item; Consent vote truncated in digest

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment: Specific Temporary Uses / Weekend Carnival Hours
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a UDO Section 5.2 text amendment allowing carnivals to operate until 11:00 p.m. on Friday and Saturday nights in response to concerns from the Little River Community Complex about early weekend closures limiting fundraising. Following unanimous Planning Commission recommendation and a public hearing with no speakers, Council approved the amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 30: UDO Text Amendment Public Notice (TC0800008)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented TC0800008 revising UDO Section 3.2.5 to let registered organizations and individuals elect free email notice or first-class mail notice ($50 every two years) for development applications and text amendments, addressing a City/County Attorney opinion that email alone did not satisfy prior statutory mailed-notice rules. Although the Planning Commission opposed the $50 fee, the Board of County Commissioners had approved staff's proposal, and Council passed it 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 31: Zoning Map Change — Poss House, 1514 Pinecrest Road (Z0800030)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff and petitioner representative Bill Van Alen presented Barry Poss's request to rezone a 0.69-acre parcel at 1514 Pinecrest Road from University College with a development plan (UC-D) to Residential Suburban 10 (RS-10) to correct a mapping error from the 2003 Duke University rezoning and allow single-family home construction. Council closed the public hearing and approved the rezoning 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 8 (Golden Belt Neighborhood Revitalization) and DPAC Opening Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a point of personal privilege thanking planning staff Julia Mullen and Helen Youngblood for months of work on the Conservation Subdivision amendment, Council heard from Mr. Davis on pulled Item 8 (Golden Belt Neighborhood Revitalization proposal and report) and approved it 7-0. Council Member Howard Clement III and colleagues then praised Capitol Broadcasting, Scientific Properties, Duke University, and the Mayor for the formal opening of the Durham Performing Arts Center earlier that evening.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Item: Referral of Item 29 (UDO Text Amendment — Downtown Nightclubs and Bars)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder not named in transcript digest; passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to refer Agenda Item 29 (downtown nightclubs and bars UDO text amendment) back to the administration per Deputy City Manager request.

votes.item_title: UDO Text Amendment: Section 5.2 Specific Temporary Uses (Weekend Carnival Hours until 11 p.m.)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder not named in transcript digest; passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to adopt UDO text amendment allowing carnivals to operate until 11:00 p.m. on Friday and Saturday nights.

votes.item_title: Item 30: UDO Text Amendment Public Notice (TC0800008)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder not named in transcript digest; passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to adopt UDO Section 3.2.5 text amendment allowing registered recipients to select free email notice or $50 biennial first-class mail notice.

votes.item_title: Item 31: Zoning Map Change — Poss House, 1514 Pinecrest Road (Z0800030)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder not named in transcript digest; passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve rezoning of 0.69 acres at 1514 Pinecrest Road from UC-D to RS-10 for single-family residential construction.

votes.item_title: Item 8: Golden Belt Neighborhood Revitalization Proposal and Report
votes.notes: Mover and seconder not named in transcript digest; passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve pulled Consent Item 8 regarding the Golden Belt neighborhood revitalization proposal and report following remarks by Mr. Davis.

disagreements.issue: Whether to Hold a Public Hearing on Planned Adam & Eve Retail Store at Fayetteville Road and NC 54
disagreements.summary: A Council member requested a public hearing in response to over 1,000 residents objecting to the planned Adam & Eve retail store at Fayetteville Road and NC 54, while Mayor Bill Bell and Planning Director Steve Medlin cautioned that the use was permitted by right under Commercial Neighborhood (CN) zoning and could not be overturned by Council.
disagreements.side_a_position: Hold a public hearing so concerned residents can be heard and have the zoning rules explained publicly.
side_a_arguments: Over a thousand area residents have expressed outrage about the planned store in their neighborhood.
Council owes residents a forum to explain the circumstances surrounding the project.
disagreements.side_b_position: Do not hold a formal public hearing that could mislead residents into expecting Council can block or overturn a permitted retail use.
side_b_arguments: The property is zoned Commercial Neighborhood (CN) and the two buildings total under 15,000 square feet, within the 20,000-square-foot limit.
Staff inspected existing stores and determined the retail sale of goods does not meet the UDO or statutory definition of an adult establishment.
Holding a public hearing would raise false expectations when Council lacks legal authority to overturn the use.
disagreements.resolution: Informational discussion concluded with no formal motion or public hearing scheduled.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 17, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, City Manager Tom Bonfield reported that the Durham Performing Arts Center (DPAC) had been accepted and turned over to operators PFM and Nederlander, and Council unanimously approved (7-0) the consent agenda. On Item 11 (Beer and Wine Privilege License Issuance), Council voted 6-1 to approve the licenses—Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Farad Ali; Nay: Howard Clement III—after Clement objected to the concentration of alcohol vendors in fragile neighborhoods even with four establishments pulled for ABC/quasi-judicial review. Following extensive debate over flood-fringe development and Jordan Lake water quality impacts, Council voted 5-2 to approve the Major Special Use Permit for Southpoint Professional Center Phase II—Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Eugene Brown, and Farad Ali; Nays: Diane Catotti and Mike Woodard—with Catotti and Woodard urging denial so the applicant would seek a rezoning instead. Council also voted 5-2 to approve the companion Southpoint Professional Center Phase II site plan and floodplain development permit—Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Eugene Brown, and Farad Ali; Nays: Diane Catotti and Mike Woodard—and voted unanimously (7-0) to approve Item 31 (historic landmark designation) before adjourning at 10:44 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and City Manager Report (DPAC Turnover)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. and the Clerk confirmed all seven Council members were present. Council heard brief remarks on a taxicab subcommittee workshop, and City Manager Tom Bonfield recognized inspections employee Don and announced that the Durham Performing Arts Center had been accepted and turned over for operation at 6:30 p.m. to PFM and Nederlander.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Police/Fire Vehicles, Cook Street Closing, Erwin Field Park Sale, Rivers Resolution)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the consent agenda covering board applications, police and fire vehicles, sewer cleaner and refuse trucks, Cook Street closing (SC0800013), DHA 2008-2009 CDBG subrecipient contract, Erwin Field Park parcel sales to Duke University, 2008 Target grant award, wastewater sludge removal contract with Synagro Central LLC, a resolution memorializing Alexander M. Rivera, Jr., and rescheduling the January 20, 2009 meeting to January 21, 2009.

agenda_items.title: Item 11: Beer and Wine Privilege License Issuance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney Patrick Baker reported four applicants (Harlem Mini-Mart, El Palenque LLC, Room About 54, and Stop and Go Food Mart) had been pulled for review with the local ABC board for potential quasi-judicial hearings. Council Member Howard Clement III moved the remaining list with the explicit intent of voting no to protest the concentration of beer and wine vendors in fragile neighborhoods, and the item passed 6-1.

agenda_items.title: Item 30: Friends of West Point Park / Black Meadow Ridge Transfer Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Multiple citizens—including Robin Jacobs, Josie McNeil, Melissa Rooney, Avery Henderson, Wayne Poole, and Durham Open Space and Trails (DOST) Chair Dan Kleber—addressed transferring West Point on the Eno Park to the State to enable state acquisition of the adjacent Black Meadow Ridge tract. DOST urged that any transfer be governed by a memorandum of understanding preserving Durham resident access; the remainder of the item fell within a truncated portion of the digest.

agenda_items.title: Southpoint Professional Center Phase II: Major Special Use Permit
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated a Major Special Use Permit in a flood fringe near NC 54 and I-40, with Planning Director Steve Medlin confirming water quality and floodplain rules were met via an enhanced sand filter system exceeding ordinance minimums. Council Members Diane Catotti and Mike Woodard opposed the permit, arguing incremental flood-fringe approvals threaten Jordan Lake water quality and that the applicant should return with a rezoning, while the majority voted 5-2 to grant the permit with staff conditions.

agenda_items.title: Southpoint Professional Center Phase II: Site Plan and Floodplain Development Permit
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Medlin presented the companion site plan for a two-story, 30,000-square-foot office building on 1.5 acres north of NC 54 and I-40 (recommended 6-1 by the Development Review Board) and confirmed the applicant's commitment to fix wall issues would be attached to the final order and site plan. Council approved the site plan and floodplain development permit 5-2.

agenda_items.title: Item 31: Historic Landmark Designation (Continued from October 20)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Sarah Young reported that Assistant City Attorney Karen Sindelar clarified the Historic Preservation Commission—rather than the State Historic Preservation Office—makes the eligibility finding under Durham's ordinance, and that the Commission recommended landmark approval for applicant Wendy Clark's property. Council approved the designation unanimously 7-0 before adjourning at 10:44 p.m.

votes.item_title: Item 11: Beer and Wine Privilege License Issuance
votes.notes: Howard Clement III moved the item while announcing he would vote No to oppose alcohol vendor concentration in fragile neighborhoods; vote re-opened once so Clement could record his No vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve beer and wine privilege licenses after four applicants were pulled for ABC/police review.

votes.item_title: Southpoint Professional Center Phase II: Major Special Use Permit
votes.notes: Diane Catotti and Mike Woodard voted No.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve staff's recommendation granting the Major Special Use Permit with conditions for Southpoint Professional Center Phase II.

votes.item_title: Southpoint Professional Center Phase II: Site Plan and Floodplain Development Permit
votes.notes: Diane Catotti and Mike Woodard voted No.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve the companion site plan and floodplain development permit for a 30,000-square-foot, two-story office building on 1.5 acres north of NC 54 and I-40, with wall repair commitments attached.

votes.item_title: Item 31: Historic Landmark Designation
votes.notes: Mover and seconder not named in transcript digest; passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve historic landmark designation for applicant Wendy Clark's property per Historic Preservation Commission recommendation.

disagreements.issue: Beer and Wine Privilege License Approvals in Fragile Neighborhoods (Item 11)
disagreements.summary: Council Member Howard Clement III opposed issuing beer and wine privilege licenses despite four establishments being pulled for ABC review, arguing too many alcohol vendors operate in fragile neighborhoods.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the remaining privilege license list while staff and the City Attorney review the four flagged businesses with the ABC board for possible quasi-judicial hearings.
side_a_arguments: Four problematic applicants (Harlem Mini-Mart, El Palenque LLC, Room About 54, and Stop and Go Food Mart) were already pulled for review with local ABC officials.
Staff committed to returning with recommendations within two work-session cycles.
disagreements.side_b_position: Vote against privilege license issuance to protest ongoing vendor concentration in fragile neighborhoods.
side_b_arguments: Too many beer and wine vendors remain located in fragile neighborhoods.
A stronger mechanism is needed to remove bad influences from vulnerable communities.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 6-1 with Howard Clement III voting No.

disagreements.issue: Southpoint Professional Center Phase II Major Special Use Permit and Flood-Fringe Development
disagreements.summary: Council divided 5-2 over whether to grant a Major Special Use Permit and companion site plan/floodplain permit for a 30,000-square-foot office building in the NC 54/I-40 flood fringe within the Jordan Lake watershed.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the Major Special Use Permit and companion site plan/floodplain development permit with staff conditions and sand-filter stormwater upgrades.
side_a_arguments: Planning staff confirmed both water quality and floodplain requirements were satisfied with no net adverse impact.
The proposed sand filter system exceeds minimum ordinance standards and equities favored approval.
Wall-repair commitments are incorporated into the final order attached to the site plan.
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny the Major Special Use Permit and require the applicant to return with a rezoning application.
side_b_arguments: Allowing incremental encroachment in flood fringes sets a harmful precedent along Jordan Lake where the city faces $300 million in water quality retrofit obligations.
Repeated negligible impacts accumulate into major environmental and water quality damage.
A rezoning is the more appropriate structural and environmental review mechanism.
disagreements.resolution: Both the Major Special Use Permit and the companion site plan/floodplain development permit passed 5-2 with Diane Catotti and Mike Woodard voting No.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 3, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present on the eve of the general election, Council presented Resolution #9608 memorializing former City Attorney William I. 'Bill' Thornton, Jr., and proclaimed November as Hire a Vet Month while highlighting record early voting exceeding 100,000 Durham residents. Council Member Eugene Brown and Mayor Bell voiced support for the prepared meals/hotel tax ballot referendum, projecting roughly $5 million annually with 40% paid by non-residents. Council unanimously referred Item 20 (Durham Performing Arts Center pre-opening budget amendment) back to the administration, approved a $500,000 Neighborhood Revitalization Fund economic development incentive policy threshold, and unanimously approved (7-0) a $200,000 incentive contract with Apogee Fine Foods LLC for three Angier-Driver corridor buildings creating 14 jobs. On pulled consent items, Council approved Contract SW-22 ramp construction after public comment advocating preservation of the Apex Street bridge, and unanimously approved (7-0) an interlocal amendment with Durham County for Criminal Justice Resource Center offender reentry programming before adjourning around 8:30 p.m.; all recorded votes were unanimous.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Ceremonial Presentations (Bill Thornton Memorial & Veterans Month)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. and the Clerk confirmed all seven Council members were present. Council presented certified Resolution #9608 memorializing former City Attorney William I. 'Bill' Thornton, Jr. to his widow Barbara C. Thornton and daughter, and issued a proclamation with Lindsay Atkins recognizing veterans and announcing the November 12 Veterans Job Fair.

agenda_items.title: Pre-Election Announcements and Prepared Meals Tax Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Diane Catotti congratulated over 100,000 Durham early voters (over half of 180,000 registered voters) and election workers ahead of the November 4 election, while Council confirmed a memorial resolution was being prepared for Alex Rivera, Jr. Council Member Eugene Brown and Mayor Bell spoke in favor of the prepared meals/hotel tax ballot initiative, noting it would raise an estimated $5 million per year with 40% paid by non-Durham residents.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item: Referral of Item 20 (DPAC Pre-Opening Budget Amendment)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield requested that Item 20—amending the Durham Performing Arts Center operating agreement to increase the pre-opening budget—be referred back to the administration, and Council approved the referral.

agenda_items.title: Job Creation, Retention, and Investment Policy Modification ($500,000 NRF Threshold)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chris Dickey of the Office of Economic and Workforce Development presented a policy modification establishing a $500,000 threshold for Neighborhood Revitalization Fund economic development incentives, citing leveraged projects such as Lewis & Clark LLC on Gilbert Street ($177,000 on $1.1 million investment) and Apogee Fine Foods. Speaker Victoria Peterson questioned job-training set-asides and local hiring compliance, and Dickey confirmed contractual workforce development and SBE/SPD plans would be overseen by staff before Council approved the policy.

agenda_items.title: Item 46: Neighborhood Revitalization Fund Incentive Contract — Apogee Fine Foods LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chris Dickey presented an incentive contract reimbursing up to 80% of capital expenditures (capped at $200,000 on ~$456,000 total development cost) for Apogee Fine Foods LLC to renovate three buildings along the Angier-Driver corridor into a neighborhood grocery store, internet cafe, and sandwich shop creating 14 jobs. No members of the public spoke during the hearing, and Council approved the contract 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 15: Contract SW-22 Ramp Construction (Apex Street Bridge)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speaker Ms. Braswell urged City, state, and federal officials to preserve the Apex Street bridge to keep communities connected rather than divided. Following brief confirmation that Council had previously voted to maintain the bridge, Council approved Item 15 unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 17: Durham County Criminal Justice Resource Center (CJRC) Contract Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speaker Victoria Peterson praised City-County collaboration on ex-offender reentry via the Criminal Justice Resource Center—citing roughly 600 daily county jail detainees and 4,000 residents on probation or parole—and urged creating a prevention and intervention task force. Community Development Director Mike Barrows agreed to provide a written response, and Council approved the contract amendment 7-0 before adjourning around 8:30 p.m.

votes.notes: Mover and seconder not named; vote opened and closed before transcript middle truncation with no dissent.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to refer Agenda Item 20 (amendment increasing the Durham Performing Arts Center pre-opening budget) back to the administration.

votes.notes: Mayor Bell announced 'Passes' without dissent; exact numeric tally not read aloud.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to establish a $500,000 threshold for Neighborhood Revitalization Fund economic development incentive projects.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously ('passes seven').
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve an up to $200,000 incentive contract for Apogee Fine Foods LLC along the Angier-Driver corridor.

votes.notes: No dissent recorded; tally transcribed phonetically.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve pulled Consent Item 15 for Contract SW-22 ramp construction following comments on the Apex Street bridge.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 20, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council recognized volunteer board members, referred Item 64 (Bandwidth.com) back to the administration (7-0), and approved the consent agenda (7-0) except Item 20. Council heard public input from Woodcroft residents supporting Item 28 (bicycle lanes on Fayetteville Road between Woodcroft Parkway and Barbee/Buxton Road) alongside American Tobacco Trail usage counts. In a split 6-1 vote on an initial zoning/annexation item in the Falls Lake/Lake Creek watershed—following citizen warnings about erosion, steep slopes, and Clean Water Act violations at Ravenstone—Council approved staff's low-density recommendation with Ayes from Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Farad Ali, and Nay from Mayor Bill Bell. Finally, after voting 7-0 to excuse Mayor Bill Bell from Item 20, the remaining six Council members debated historic preservation versus redevelopment before voting 6-0—Ayes: Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Farad Ali (with Bill Bell recused)—to advance the upset-bid sale of 727 North Mangum Street in Five Points to UDI Community Development Corporation.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Ceremonial Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk called the roll confirming all seven Council members were present, and Mayor Bill Bell thanked volunteers serving on city boards and commissions following a pre-meeting reception. Council members discussed street conditions, condominium sales, the new Durham arts history book 'Brighter Leaves' honoring Dr. Pat Keenan, a visually impaired 'Beep Ball' and wheelchair basketball event, and Mechanics & Farmers Bank's 100th anniversary.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item (Bandwidth.com Referral) and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to remove Item 64 (Bandwidth.com) from the agenda and refer it back to the administration. Council then voted 7-0 to approve the Consent Agenda—with Item 20 pulled for separate action and Item 28 placed on General Business—including minimum livable wage data, City-County Planning interlocal agreement, 2007 and 2008 HIDTA drug-trafficking grants, Solid Waste fee clarifications, the Cary-NC 55 connection contract, and Resolution memorializing William I. Thornton, Jr.

agenda_items.title: Item 28: Bicycle Lanes on Fayetteville Road (Woodcroft Parkway to Buxton/Barbee)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation planner Dale McKeel presented 12-hour manual user counts at Cook Road and the American Tobacco Trail (640 total users: 291 cyclists, 349 pedestrians, plus dogs, strollers, and skaters). A Woodcroft HOA representative from the 2,500-home community presented an HOA resolution supporting bike lanes in the road widening project for commuter safety and health benefits; any subsequent vote fell inside the omitted middle of the digest.

agenda_items.title: Initial Zoning / Annexation Public Hearing (Lick/Lake Creek & Falls Lake Watershed)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A speaker presented aerial photos and EPA/Clean Water Act enforcement records from Ravenstone 1 and 2, warning that steep-slope development by the same developer/engineer threatens Falls Lake with nutrient runoff and algae blooms and urging downsizing. Staff noted the site is limited to low-density development (24% or less impervious surface rather than up to 70% allowed in the protected watershed), Howard Clement III noted the owner had not requested a downzoning, and Council approved staff's recommendation 6-1 with Mayor Bill Bell voting No.

agenda_items.title: Item 20: Proposed Sale of 727 North Mangum Street (Five Points Parcel 104905)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to recuse Mayor Bill Bell from Item 20, then debated selling 727 North Mangum Street in the Five Points redevelopment area to UDI Community Development Corporation (represented by Mr. Stewart) via the upset-bid process with a $30,000 minimum 10% bid increment and a potential future $186,000 economic incentive requiring a public hearing. Preservation advocates urged attaching preservation covenants to prevent demolition, while Mr. Stewart confirmed his proposal commits to restoring the building if a structural engineer deems it sound, and the remaining six Council members approved advancing the sale 6-0.

votes.notes: Mayor Bill Bell voted No.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve staff's initial zoning recommendation limiting the site to low-density development (24% or less impervious surface) in the protected watershed.

votes.notes: Passed 7-0 prior to Item 20 consideration.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to excuse Mayor Bill Bell from participating and voting on Item 20.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Proposed Sale of 727 North Mangum Street (Parcel 104905) to UDI Community Development Corp.
votes.notes: Mayor Bill Bell excused/recused; all six remaining Council members voted Aye.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve administration recommendation initiating the upset-bid sale process for 727 North Mangum Street (Five Points) subject to future project contingencies and public hearing if economic incentives are requested.

disagreements.issue: Initial Zoning and Stormwater Runoff Concerns in Falls Lake Watershed (Lake Creek / Sierra)
disagreements.summary: Council debated whether to approve staff's recommended low-density initial zoning or downzone the property after citizen testimony tied the developer/engineer to prior Clean Water Act erosion violations at Ravenstone draining into Falls Lake.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve staff's recommended initial zoning capping impervious surface at 24% under low-density watershed rules.
side_a_arguments: The property owner had not requested a downzoning.
Although the protected watershed tier could permit up to 70% impervious surface, the proposal voluntarily limits development to low density (24% or less impervious surface).
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose approval / favor downsizing due to steep-slope erosion and Falls Lake water quality concerns.
side_b_arguments: Documented sediment and nutrient runoff from the same developer's nearby Ravenstone 1 and 2 projects had remained unresolved for over 18 months.
Phosphorus and nitrogen runoff via Lake Creek contributes to algae blooms in Falls Lake.
disagreements.resolution: Staff's recommendation passed 6-1 with Mayor Bill Bell voting No.

disagreements.issue: Historic Preservation Covenants vs. Redevelopment Process for 727 North Mangum Street (Item 20)
disagreements.summary: Preservation advocates urged requiring preservation covenants to prevent demolition of a significant Five Points structure before selling 727 North Mangum Street to UDI Community Development Corporation, while Council and staff maintained the current action only initiated the upset-bid process.
disagreements.side_a_position: Advance the upset-bid sale process to UDI CDC now, with community review and a public hearing occurring later before any $186,000 incentive contract is approved.
side_a_arguments: Approval only begins the upset-bid process (requiring a 10% / $30,000 minimum upset bid) and does not finalize a site plan or incentive grant.
UDI CDC's proposal already states it will restore the building if a structural engineer determines it is structurally sound.
Any future $186,000 economic incentive requires three contingencies, community review, and a subsequent Council public hearing.
disagreements.side_b_position: Require binding preservation covenants with the sale so blight is addressed through renovation rather than demolition.
side_b_arguments: Fighting blight is best achieved by rehabilitating significant existing structures rather than tearing them down.
Surrounding empty lots can accommodate new construction without losing historic fabric.
disagreements.resolution: With Mayor Bill Bell excused, Council voted 6-0 to approve the administration's recommendation initiating the upset-bid sale.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 6, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, fire officials reduced chamber occupancy for code compliance before Council proclaimed International Walk to School Day (October 8, 2008) and Disability Awareness Month (October 2008), honored retired 1958 Durham Fire Department pioneers, and recognized Domestic Violence Awareness Month. Council members also highlighted Minority Economic Development Week, an HBCU forum on the $700 billion federal financial bailout, Project Homeless Connect, and Durham's designation by Black Enterprise as the best place to retire. Following a truncated middle section, Council held a public hearing and voted unanimously (7-0) to approve the Meridian Business Park zoning map change rezoning 32 acres along Meridian Parkway from Light Industrial (IL) to Office and Institutional (OI) without a development plan, after Mayor Bell questioned flooding impacts and staff confirmed future floodplain crossings would require Board of Adjustment review. Council also voted unanimously (7-0) to continue Item 41 (Bandwidth.com) to October 20, 2008 and approved pulled Consent Items 8 and 25 (7-0) after speaker Victoria Peterson urged open public bidding for City contracts and local hiring before adjourning at 8:38 p.m.; all recorded votes were unanimous.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Fire Code Occupancy Adjustment, and Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. and asked the Fire Chief to reduce room occupancy to comply with fire capacity limits before roll call. Council issued proclamations for International Walk to School Day (October 8, 2008, with Safe Kids Durham County and FedEx) and Disability Awareness Month (October 2008), honored retired 1958 Durham Fire Department pioneers (John Lyons, Nathaniel Thompson, George King, and Veltan Thompson), and recognized Domestic Violence Awareness Month.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Announcements (HBCU Forum, Project Homeless Connect, Best Place to Retire)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council praised staff support for the World Beer Festival at Durham Bulls Athletic Park, while Farad Ali highlighted Minority Economic Development Week and a Sheraton forum with North Carolina HBCU chancellors on the $700 billion federal bailout. Council members also commended Project Homeless Connect volunteers, breast cancer awareness walkers, Corporal Addison, and Black Enterprise naming Durham the best place to retire.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Meridian Business Park (Light Industrial IL to Office & Institutional OI)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered America's Capital Partners' request (presented by Patrick Byker, with Melissa Rooney also speaking) to rezone 32 acres at Meridian Parkway and Exchange Place in the Northeast Creek floodplain from Light Industrial (IL) to Office and Institutional (OI) without a development plan, supported by the Auburn Homeowners Association and a 7-6 Planning Commission vote. Mayor Bell questioned flooding risks and why no development plan was attached, and staff clarified that OI eliminates intense industrial uses while any future floodplain/stream crossings would require a Minor Special Use Permit before the Board of Adjustment; Council approved the rezoning 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 41: Bandwidth.com Incorporated (Continuance)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a City Manager priority request, Mayor Bell opened the public hearing on Item 41 (Bandwidth.com Incorporated) and Council voted unanimously 7-0 to continue the item to October 20, 2008.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items 8, 19, and 25 (Public Contracting Transparency and Local Hiring)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Items 8 and 25 (noting Item 19 was referred back to the administration), questioning why private economic-development contracts like those with the Chamber of Commerce and Downtown Durham Inc. were not publicly advertised like CDBG grants and urging local hiring for Durham residents and youth. Assistant City Manager Alan DeLyle explained OEWD contracts were approved during the budget process, and Council approved Item 8 and passed Item 25 unanimously 7-0 before adjourning at 8:38 p.m.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 7-0 on Item 25; Item 8 passed without objection

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 15, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council issued a proclamation declaring September 25, 2008 as the National Day of Remembrance for Murder Victims in Durham and heard an announcement supporting the prepared meals tax at the Hayti Heritage Center. Following performance evaluations, Council unanimously approved (7-0) a 3% salary increase for City Attorney Patrick Baker and a 4% salary increase for City Clerk Anne Gray effective January 1, 2009. Council unanimously approved (7-0) the consent agenda covering Downtown Durham Inc., Durham Tech Brownfield job training, citywide compensation and classification implementation, City Hall renovations, hybrid bus capital grants, and NCDOT railroad safety devices. In public hearings, Council unanimously approved (7-0) street closings for Watkins Road (Item 36) and an unnamed alley off East Club Boulevard (Item 37), and voted on the Davis Park West rezoning (Item 38, Z07-S27) for 330 multifamily units, 82,000 square feet of non-residential space, and a 180-room hotel near Hopson Road and Davis Drive before adjourning at 7:35 p.m.; all recorded votes were unanimous with no split or contested votes.

Mayor Bell proclaimed September 25, 2008 as the National Day of Remembrance for Murder Victims in recognition of the Durham chapter of Parents of Murdered Children, youth citizenship guests thanked Council Member Mike Woodard, and an event supporting the prepared meals tax at Hayti Heritage Center was announced.

agenda_items.title: City Attorney and City Clerk Performance Evaluations and Salary Increases

FY09 contract, WIA grant project ordinance #13635, City Hall renovation contingency, Riggsbee Avenue substation funds, citywide compensation classification system implementation, Research Center Streets (ST-233), hybrid bus capital grants, NCDOT railroad crossing warning devices at View and Gilbert Streets, and FY 2011–2017 TIP priorities.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 2, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, Council swore in members of the newly renamed Durham Youth Commission (expanding to accept all high school applicants and adopting Southside Sanctuary Community Center and event recycling ambassadorship) and celebrated 20 years of the Sister Cities partnership with Toyama, Japan. Council unanimously approved (7-0) the consent agenda—including asset forfeiture funding for police training and equipment, Durham Athletic Park agreements, and fleet extensions—and voted 7-0 on General Business Item 6B to refer a proposal regarding NCDOT Transportation Impact Analysis delays to the Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC). In public hearings, Council unanimously approved (7-0) a petitioned sewer improvement on Ed Cook Road (Item 12) and four mini-assessment relief rolls on Azure/Azalea Drive and Chapel Hill Road (Items 13–16). Council also voted unanimously (7-0) on five street and alley closings (Items 17–21) covering portions of Ramsey Street, #28 Alley, East Peabody Street, an unnamed alley, and South Dillard Street to enable construction of the Durham County Human Services complex before adjourning around 7:41 p.m.; all votes were unanimous.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 18, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Mayor Bell administered the ceremonial oath of office to new City Manager Thomas J. 'Tom' Bonfield, and Council unanimously approved (7-0) priority agenda adjustments, the consent agenda (covering the Alston Avenue Durham Freeway pedestrian bridge, American Tobacco Trail Phase Z, and street closings), and a Castle Rock Drive curb-and-gutter assessment roll (Item 23). Following a truncated middle section, Council engaged in sharp debate over supplemental Item 39 regarding the Environmental Affairs Board (EAB) report on the proposed National Bio and Agro-Defense Facility (NBAF): Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved a resolution opposing the facility (amended by Diane Catotti to accept the EAB report and forward its unanswered questions), while Eugene Brown sought to sever the opposition clause for lack of information and Howard Clement III sought to abstain. The floor vote initially tallied 5-1 (Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Mike Woodard, Diane Catotti, Farad Ali; Nay: Eugene Brown; attempted abstention: Howard Clement III), until City Attorney Patrick Baker returned at the end of the meeting and ruled that under applicable law a physically present member without a personal conduct or financial conflict cannot abstain and must be recorded as an affirmative vote—resulting in an official 6-1 passage (Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Mike Woodard, Diane Catotti, Farad Ali, and Howard Clement III; Nay: Eugene Brown). Council also voted unanimously (7-0) to approve supplemental Item 40 supporting a Durham County advisory referendum on a local prepared food tax funding cultural and trail projects before adjourning at 10:35 p.m.
