agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order, the Clerk confirmed all seven members were present, and Mayor Bell administered the ceremonial oath of office to new City Manager Thomas J. Bonfield (who began August 11). Council issued a proclamation for Alcohol and Drug Addiction Recovery Month, recognized Miss Preteen North Carolina, Southern Growth Policies Board YouTube contest runner-up Juquetta Cherry, and anti-smoking youth advocate Sydney Bronson, and observed a moment of silence for city employee Tawana Parker.

agenda_items.title: City Manager and City Attorney Priority Items and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield referred Item 14 (OPEB Fund) and Item 34 (Conservation Subdivisions TC07-19) back to staff and added supplemental Item 39 (EAB NBAF report) and Item 40 (prepared food tax referendum support), while City Attorney Patrick Baker clarified Item 25 was only a public hearing on the proposed Minimum Non-Residential Building Code and re-adoption of May Minimum Housing Code amendments (passed 7-0). Council also approved the consent agenda 7-0, including board appointments, street closings, Alston Avenue pedestrian bridge replacement, and American Tobacco Trail Phase Z design.

agenda_items.title: Item 23: Mini-Assessment Roll Confirmation — Castle Rock Drive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater Manager Ed Venable presented Item 23 confirming the assessment roll for completed curb, gutter, and paving improvements on Castle Rock Drive. No members of the public spoke, and Council adopted the resolution 7-0 (the subsequent Item 24 Dot Nichols annexation hearing fell inside the omitted middle of the digest).

agenda_items.title: Item 39 (Supplemental): Environmental Affairs Board Report and Resolution Opposing Proposed NBAF
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden's motion—amended by Diane Catotti—to accept the Environmental Affairs Board report, forward the EAB's unanswered questions, and adopt a resolution opposing the proposed National Bio and Agro-Defense Facility (NBAF). Eugene Brown requested severing the opposition clause and voted No for lack of information, while Howard Clement III sought to abstain; the floor vote initially read 5-1, after which the City Attorney ruled at 03:31:36 that Clement's non-vote must be recorded as an affirmative vote, making the final tally 6-1.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 6-1 (5-1 on floor with 1 attempted abstention converted to Aye)

agenda_items.title: Item 40 (Supplemental): Resolution Supporting County Advisory Referendum on Local Prepared Food Tax
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant to the City Manager Karmisha Wallace presented a corrected project list (fixing three spelling errors without changing figures) unanimously endorsed by the Joint City-County Committee for funding via a prepared food tax referendum: Durham Armory, Carolina Theatre, Durham Arts Council, Durham Bulls Athletic Park, Durham County Stadium, and numerous greenway/park projects including the American Tobacco Trail Environmental Education Center, West Point on the Eno, Third Fork Creek, and Ellerbe Creek trails. Council approved the resolution 7-0 before hearing the City Attorney's abstention ruling and adjourning at 10:35 p.m.

disagreements.issue: Council Position on Proposed National Bio and Agro-Defense Facility (NBAF) and Abstention Authority (Item 39)
disagreements.summary: Council divided over whether to adopt a formal resolution opposing the proposed NBAF alongside accepting the Environmental Affairs Board's report and forwarding unanswered questions, as well as whether Howard Clement III could abstain.
disagreements.side_a_position: Accept the EAB report, forward its unanswered questions, and adopt a Council resolution opposing the proposed NBAF.
side_a_arguments: The EAB report identified substantial unanswered questions and outstanding environmental and safety concerns.
Passing the opposition resolution reflects the unresolved concerns highlighted in items one and two of the motion.
disagreements.side_b_position: Accept the EAB report and forward questions, but do not vote to oppose the facility without complete facts (with Eugene Brown voting No and Howard Clement III attempting to abstain).
side_b_arguments: Council had been placed in a bind by being asked to approve or disapprove the facility without having all the facts.
The Environmental Affairs Board itself recommended deferring action until additional information was obtained.
Eugene Brown requested severing the motion so he could support accepting the report and sending questions while declining to oppose the facility.
disagreements.resolution: The floor vote tallied 5-1 (Eugene Brown No, Howard Clement III attempting to abstain), and at 03:31:36 City Attorney Patrick Baker ruled Clement could not abstain without a conflict of interest and must be recorded as an affirmative vote, resulting in a 6-1 adoption.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 4, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council highlighted National Night Out and its new asset-forfeiture mobile command vehicle, presented a memorial resolution honoring arts leader Ella Fountain Kessler Pratt, and recognized City Clerk Anne Gray on earning her Master Municipal Clerk designation. Council unanimously approved (7-0) City Manager priority referrals of Boler North Carolina plan amendment A07-14 (Item 52) and Boler Highway 54 rezoning Z07-34 (Item 58), reviewed chamber renovations replacing the old voting machine, and heard a City Attorney item authorizing incoming City Manager Tom Bonfield's August 11 start date. Later in the meeting, Council heard sharp dispute between Gateway Terrace developers and a neighboring protest petitioner demanding an approximately $350,000 land purchase, with Farad Ali questioning whether Council should mediate private real estate negotiations and Diane Catotti suggesting JCCPC review before Council unanimously approved (7-0) the Gateway Terrace rezoning. Council also voted unanimously (7-0) to translate county Residential 20 zoning on an annexed parcel, adopt a UDO text amendment requiring a Special Use Permit and neighborhood meeting for Commercial Neighborhood developments over 5,000 square feet bordering residential districts on two or more sides, and pass the accompanying consistency resolution (Item 71); all recorded votes were unanimous.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, National Night Out, and Ceremonial Recognitions (Ella Fountain Pratt & Anne Gray)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. and the Clerk confirmed all seven Council members were present. Mayor Bell and Police Chief Jose Lopez highlighted National Night Out and a mobile police command vehicle purchased with asset forfeiture funds, presented a memorial resolution for arts leader Ella Fountain Kessler Pratt (passing July 28, 2008) to her son Ray Pratt and Durham Arts Council Executive Director Sherry DeVries, and recognized City Clerk Anne Gray on achieving Master Municipal Clerk (MMC) certification.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Referrals of Items 52 & 58; Council Chambers Renovations) and Bonfield Start Date
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to refer Item 52 (plan amendment A07-14) and Item 58 (rezoning Z07-34) back to the administration, while General Services Director Beverly Thompson reviewed summer Council Chamber renovations including replacement of the legacy voting machine. The City Attorney also introduced a motion authorizing incoming City Manager Tom Bonfield's August 11 start date (remainder of early agenda truncated in digest).

agenda_items.title: Gateway Terrace Rezoning Public Hearing and Protest Petition Dispute
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Developers represented by Bob Zumwalt (John R. McAdams Co.) and Mr. Spalding presented committed elements (including a 100-foot buffer along Watkins Road) for Gateway Terrace, explaining they closed on the land early and rejected a protest petitioner's demand to buy nearly an acre of adjacent residential land. Protest petitioner Mr. Waldridge argued purchasing the end parcel for roughly $350,000 (~1.5–1.7% of the project budget) would eliminate buffering issues and urged a two-restaurant, one-hotel project without Hooters, while Farad Ali questioned mixing private business negotiations into zoning policy and Diane Catotti suggested referring the broader issue to JCCPC before Council approved the rezoning 7-0.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a request to translate Durham County Residential 20 zoning to identical City Residential 20 zoning following annexation, noting Planning Commission approval. No members of the public spoke, and Council approved the zoning 7-0.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment: Commercial Neighborhood (CN) Major Special Use Permit and Consistency Resolution (Item 71)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a UDO text amendment arising from a Board of Adjustment appeal that requires a Special Use Permit and neighborhood meeting for any Commercial Neighborhood (CN) development with over 5,000 square feet of new floor area bordering residential districts on two or more sides (recommended 8-5 by the Planning Commission and already adopted by the Board of County Commissioners). Council approved both the text amendment (7-0) and the accompanying consistency resolution, Item 71 (7-0).

votes.notes: Passed 7-0.

disagreements.issue: Gateway Terrace Rezoning and Protest Petitioner Land-Purchase Demand
disagreements.summary: During the Gateway Terrace rezoning hearing, a neighboring protest petitioner urged Council to withhold approval unless the developer purchased an adjacent ~1-acre residential parcel for roughly $350,000, prompting Council members to question whether private real estate disputes belong in zoning decisions.
disagreements.side_a_position: Make a zoning policy decision on the merits without forcing the applicant to buy adjacent private real estate, while referring broader policy questions to JCCPC.
side_a_arguments: The applicant met ordinance standards, agreed to committed elements including a 100-foot buffer along Watkins Road, and had no project use for the extra acre.
Requiring a land purchase would force a brand-new rezoning application and a 9-to-12-month delay.

Council Member Farad Ali questioned whether Council was being asked to intervene in a private business transaction before deciding zoning policy, and Diane Catotti suggested placing the broader issue on a JCCPC agenda.
disagreements.side_b_position: Hold rezoning support pending a land-purchase settlement (~$350,000) to incorporate the adjacent parcel and remove a 25-foot residential buffer.
side_b_arguments: Buying the end parcel represents roughly 1.5–1.7% of the mid-to-upper-teens million budget and would yield additional usable square footage.
A settlement would address neighborhood concerns over potential tenants such as Hooters.
disagreements.resolution: Council voted 7-0 to approve the Gateway Terrace rezoning.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 16, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven Council members present, the Council presented ceremonial proclamations recognizing GlaxoSmithKline for water conservation leadership during historic droughts and honoring Mrs. Gore for community and police volunteerism, and adopted a memorial resolution honoring former City Council member (1960–1961) and civic leader Southgate Jones Jr., who passed away on June 5, 2008. Youth Employment / Yoderm staff also presented results from the Summer Career Academy, noting 23 participating students achieved an 88 percent rate of maintaining or improving grades and attendance alongside internships and service-learning projects. During priority items, the City Manager moved Item 66 (Durham Athletic Park renovation project construction agreements) to the consent agenda after Council Member Diane Catotti's questions were answered and highlighted supplemental items on voluntary annexation frequency (Item 73) and the Southgate Jones Jr. memorial resolution (Item 74). In the public-hearing portion of the meeting, all six recorded votes passed unanimously 7-0, approving initial zonings for Davis Park West (Item 56, Z07-27), Brightleaf Tract 3 Outparcel (Item 57, Z08-01A), and the Freeman Road/Roberts property (Item 58, Z08-13A), closing an unnamed alley off Chapel Hill Road for Self-Help (Item 53, SC08-01), adopting a compromise UDO text amendment on IL/Compact Height near Old West Durham and Ninth Street (Item 69), and approving University Center (UC) initial zoning for the Duke Lemur Center following a private agreement between Duke University and the West Cornwallis Neighborhood Association (Item 70).

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented Case SC08-01, a request on behalf of Self-Help to close an approximately 150.71 linear-foot unnamed alley off Chapel Hill Road, noting agency review found no issues. meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 2, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present and overflow attendees directed to the personnel briefing room, Council proclaimed June 14–21, 2008 as Juneteenth Celebration Week and voted 7-0 to adopt the City Manager's priority items (referring Item 31, the Quarterly Crime Report, back to the administration for a dedicated public police presentation) and 7-0 to approve the consent agenda excluding pulled Item 22. Following an extended public hearing—where firefighters advocated for pay increases following the Waters Group compensation study, arts advocates supported organizations including Hayti Heritage Center and Youth Noise Network, and taxicab industry speakers including Earl Blue urged added staffing to enforce passenger-for-hire rules against unlicensed vehicles—Council voted 7-0 to accept the public comments for the record. On pulled Consent Item 22 (the Walltown Park Recreation Center CMAR construction services agreement for structural steel detailing, fabrication, and erection), after Walltown Community Association President Audrey Mitchell voiced support while asking for answers on community concerns and timely progress, the Council approved Item 22 by a 6-1 split vote, with Ayes from Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Diane Catotti, and Farad Ali and a Nay from Eugene Brown. Following the vote, the City Manager committed to providing a Walltown Park status report at Thursday's work session, Council Member Clement requested a budget-driver update on taxicab enforcement staffing, and Council Member Brown confirmed the June 9 budget review meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Chamber Capacity Management, Roll Call, and Juneteenth Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell opened the meeting at 7:02 p.m. and arranged for roughly 30 standing attendees to move to an overflow monitor room due to chamber capacity limits. After all seven Council members answered roll call, the Mayor presented a Juneteenth Celebration Week (June 14–21, 2008) proclamation to Phyllis Coley of Spectacular Magazine and Parks and Recreation Director Rhonda Parker.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Quarterly Crime Report Referral and Overflow Logistics)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested referring Item 31 (Quarterly Crime Report) back to the administration so the Police Department could deliver a dedicated public presentation on crime trends, noted a revised script for public hearing Item 44, and coordinated overflow seating in the personnel briefing room. Council approved the priority items 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Item 22)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the consent agenda excluding Item 22 (Walltown Park Recreation Center CMAR construction services agreement) by a 7-0 vote. Covered items included financial and cash compliance audits, minutes, board applications and appointments, Patterson Place Phase 2 and Brightleaf site plans, FY 2007–08 budget amendments, surplus property and sewer easement acquisitions, community recreation agreements, gang investigator training, stormwater replacement fund regulations, water/sewer technical corrections, and an OWASA wastewater agreement.

agenda_items.title: General Business: Durham Arts Council 25-Year Lease Amendment and Budget Public Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council began general business with Item 21 concerning the Durham Arts Council 25-year lease amendment and subrecipient agreement policy parity (such as with St. Joseph's/Hayti), before a truncated middle section led into extensive public comments on fire department pay after the 2007 Waters Group study, arts and youth program funding, and unlicensed for-hire shuttle/taxi enforcement raised by Earl Blue and others. At 05:04:38, Council voted 7-0 to close the public hearing and accept the comments for the record.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 22: Walltown Park Recreation Center CMAR Construction Services Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Audrey Mitchell, President of the Walltown Community Association, thanked Council for funding the project and stated the community did not oppose negotiating structural steel detailing, fabrication, and erection, while asking for answers to community concerns and expedient progress. Council Member Eugene Brown requested that the record reflect his vote against the measure, and Council approved Item 22 by a 6-1 vote with Brown voting No.

agenda_items.title: Work Session Follow-Ups (Walltown Report, Taxicab Staffing, and Budget Schedule)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager committed to providing a Walltown Park status report at Thursday's work session and meeting with Audrey Mitchell. Council Member Howard Clement III asked for a budget-driver response regarding additional taxicab enforcement personnel, and Council Member Eugene Brown confirmed the June 4 meeting with County Commissioners and the June 9 revised-budget meeting at 8:30 a.m.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Items (Referral of Item 31 Quarterly Crime Report)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve the City Manager's priority item referring Item 31 (Quarterly Crime Report) back to the administration for a separate public police presentation.

votes.item_title: Close Public Hearing and Accept Public Comments for the Record
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to close the public hearing and accept public comments regarding fire pay, arts funding, and taxicab enforcement into the record.

votes.item_title: Pulled Consent Item 22: Walltown Park Recreation Center CMAR Construction Services Agreement
votes.notes: Council Member Eugene Brown asked that the record note his vote against the measure; Mayor Bell announced the vote passed 6-1 with Brown voting No.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve the CMAR construction services agreement for structural steel detailing, fabrication, and erection at the Walltown Park Recreation Center.

disagreements.issue: Walltown Park Recreation Center CMAR Construction Services Agreement (Item 22)
disagreements.summary: Council approved the CMAR construction services agreement for Walltown Park Recreation Center structural steel detailing, fabrication, and erection by a 6-1 vote, with Council Member Eugene Brown dissenting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the CMAR construction services agreement to advance the Walltown Park Recreation Center structural steel work while providing a Thursday work-session status report to the community.
side_a_arguments: The Walltown Community Association appreciated the funding and did not oppose negotiating structural steel work so the project could move forward expediently.
The City Manager committed to meeting with Walltown Community Association President Audrey Mitchell and reporting back at the Thursday work session on outstanding community questions.
disagreements.side_b_position: Vote against the CMAR construction services agreement.
side_b_arguments: Council Member Eugene Brown requested that the record note his vote against the measure without elaborating on-mic in the transcript digest.
disagreements.resolution: Item 22 passed 6-1, and the City Manager committed to presenting a status update at the Thursday work session.

In the City Manager's water supply update, staff reported water restrictions had been relaxed to Stage 3 moderate mandatory conservation effective April 2, Teer Quarry was offline, total water reserves stood at 343 days of supply, and the expanded Town of Cary interconnection was nearing completion. meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 5, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council presented proclamations for Drinking Water Week (honoring local and statewide K–8 Water Heroes poster winners and Department of Water Management staff), Older Americans Month, and Children's Mental Health Awareness Day, and recognized The Compassionate Friends designation of Durham as a Compassionate Employer. Council voted 7-0 to adopt the City Manager's priority items reordering Item 40 after Item 43 and referring Items 42 and 52 back to the administration. Following a truncated middle segment, Council engaged in a contested debate over an ordinance containing both code recodification technical corrections and Section 2's phased development/impact fee resolution (affecting projects submitted after July 2008 and July 2009): rejecting arguments to separate or further delay the fees pending development-review reforms, Council passed the full item including the fees by a 4-3 split vote, with Ayes from Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Farad Ali and Nays from Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Howard Clement III. Council then voted 7-0 on three economic development and finance items: amending an economic development corridor design contract with EGG to $299,000 (Item 15), advancing the Northeast Central Durham redevelopment plan division of labor (Item 16), and approving a $26 million maximum debt reimbursement authorization containing a standard 20 percent market-adjustment cushion (Item 17).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Proclamations, Water Heroes Poster Awards, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. with all seven members present. Council presented Drinking Water Week awards to K–8 poster contest winners and Water Management staff, received a Compassionate Employer recognition from The Compassionate Friends, proclaimed Older Americans Month and Children's Mental Health Awareness Day, and heard announcements on Bull Durham's 20th anniversary and the May 1 National Day of Prayer.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Items 40, 42, 43, and 52)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested hearing Item 40 (TW Alexander properties zoning map change) after Item 43 (TW Alexander plan amendment), referring Item 42 (Z07-14A) back to the administration, and referring Item 52 (purchase and contract approval thresholds) back to the administration. Council approved the priority items 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Development / Impact Fee Schedule Resolution and Code Technical Corrections
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a truncated middle portion, Council debated whether to enact the next phase of development/impact fee increases alongside minor recodification technical corrections or postpone Section 2's fee resolution amid NAIOP and development-community concerns over the development review process. Proponents noted the fees were already delayed a year and phased across July 2008 and July 2009 and argued parks, open spaces, and roads should not be held hostage; Council approved the full item including the fees 4-3, with Clement, Cole-McFadden, and Bell voting No.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Corridor Design Contract Amendment with EGG
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Responding to Council Member Farad Ali's questions about raising the EGG contract by $61,098 to $299,000 after negotiations failed with Kimley-Horn on the West Chapel Hill Street corridor, Chris Dickey of the Office of Economic Development explained roughly $300,000 from 2000 bond funds had been budgeted for schematic designs across five corridors. Council approved the amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Northeast Central Durham Redevelopment Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Farad Ali questioned staff on the division of labor for implementing the Northeast Central Durham redevelopment plan, and staff confirmed Kevin Dick and his team would lead implementation. Council approved the item 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Debt Issuance / Expense Reimbursement Authorization ($26 Million Maximum)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Farad Ali asked why the maximum authorization was set at $26 million. Assistant City Manager Allen DeLisle explained that bond counsel advises requesting 20 percent above anticipated project needs to give flexibility for last-minute coupon-to-par adjustments required by banks at pricing, while the city only issues what it actually needs; Council approved the item 7-0.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Items (Order of Items 40/43 and Referrals of Items 42 and 52)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve City Manager priority items scheduling Item 40 after Item 43 and referring Items 42 and 52 back to the administration.

votes.item_title: Development / Impact Fee Schedule Resolution and Code Technical Corrections
votes.notes: Clerk announced the motion passed 4-3 with Council Member Howard Clement III, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, and Mayor Bill Bell voting No; all seven members were present at roll call, establishing the four Ayes.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to adopt the item as presented, including both recodification technical corrections and Section 2's phased development/impact fee resolution.

votes.item_title: Item 15: Economic Development Corridor Design Contract Amendment with EGG ($299,000)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to amend the contract with EGG to $299,000 (an increase of $61,098) for schematic design work across economic development corridors including West Chapel Hill Street.

votes.item_title: Item 16: Northeast Central Durham Redevelopment Plan
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve the Northeast Central Durham redevelopment plan item with implementation led by Kevin Dick's staff.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Debt Issuance and Expense Reimbursement Authorization ($26 Million Maximum)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve reimbursement resolution and $26 million maximum authorization (incorporating a 20% pricing buffer per bond counsel guidance).

disagreements.issue: Phased Development / Impact Fee Increase vs. Development Review Process Delay
disagreements.summary: Council divided 4-3 over passing Section 2's phased development/impact fee schedule alongside technical ordinance corrections versus setting aside or delaying the fee increase until development-review reforms satisfied business groups.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the full ordinance including the phased fee schedule to fund parks, open space, and road infrastructure.
side_a_arguments: Parks, open spaces, and roads should not be held hostage to the development review reform process.

The fee increase had already been delayed a full year and split into two phases (July 2008 and July 2009) to soften the impact, while infrastructure cost studies justified collecting the full amount earlier.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose adopting the fee resolution as presented rather than decoupling or postponing Section 2.
side_b_arguments: Critics and business/NAIOP stakeholders argued the city's development review system remained inconsistent and had made backward steps alongside partial improvements.
disagreements.resolution: Council adopted the full item including Section 2's fee resolution by a 4-3 vote.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 21, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council presented a Safe Kids Durham County childhood injury-prevention proclamation, recognized Victims' Awareness Week and the Annual March Against Violence, and voted 7-0 to adopt both the City Manager's priority items (referring Item 16 on minimum housing code/undergrowth and Item 22 on conservation water rates back to the administration) and the consent agenda. Police Chief Jose Lopez presented the 2007 end-of-year Police Department report (Item 39), highlighting recruitment and retention pressures caused by Durham having the lowest base starting pay among 11 peer agencies, an approximately 20-year span to reach top pay, officer departures to neighboring departments, and 18 civilian vacancies out of 118 positions, alongside modest property crime growth. Following a truncated middle segment, all remaining recorded land-use and street-closing votes passed unanimously 7-0, including the landmark Tuscaloosa-Lakewood Neighborhood Protection Overlay (Item 24 and its companion item)—Durham's first NPO under the Unified Development Ordinance—along with a Residential Compact multifamily rezoning on 10 parcels near Morning Glory Avenue (Item 26) and two street and right-of-way closings on Rustica Drive (Item 28, SC07-11) and Martin Luther King Jr. Parkway (Item 29, SC07-12).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Safe Kids Proclamation, and Victims' Awareness Week Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell opened the meeting at 7:02 p.m. with all seven members present and presented a Safe Kids Durham County proclamation to Duke University Hospital Emergency Department representative Ms. Fromond emphasizing booster seat and helmet safety. Council also commended the Durham Police Department Victim Services Unit for its work during Victims' Awareness Week and the Annual March Against Violence.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Referrals of Items 16 and 22; Scheduling Item 39)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested referring Item 16 (minimum housing code and removal of trash/undergrowth) and Item 22 (conservation water rates) back to the administration for further work-session discussion, and moving Item 39 (Police Department 2007 end-of-year report) right after the consent agenda. meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 7, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council presented proclamations for Jazz Appreciation Month, Public Safety Communications Officers Week, and Earth Day (April 19), and honored the memories of pioneering physician Dr. Robert Dawson and a prominent 99-year-old Durham businessman. On the business agenda, every recorded vote passed unanimously 7-0: Council approved the City Manager's priority items (referring Item 22 on East Deck facade treatment back to administration, moving Item 37 on City Code recodification to public hearing, and adding supplemental Items 39 and 40), adopted the consent agenda (including the 2008 short-session legislative program, water treatment and East Durham outfall contracts, and a sustainability interlocal agreement with Durham County), and approved all general business and public hearing items. Specifically, Council awarded $252,000 in HOME funds to Housing for New Hope Inc. for William Square Apartments Phase 1 (Item 14), approved special-needs housing funding for Housing for New Hope and CASA (Item 19), adopted UDO sidewalk flexibility and ADA compliance amendments (Item 35, TC07-20), recodified the City Code and fee schedule (Item 37), reinstated Durham Workforce Development Board members (Item 39), and approved the joint Durham–Raleigh Long Range Transportation Plan revenue element grant project ordinance (Item 40).

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m., confirmed all seven members present, and presented proclamations for Jazz Appreciation Month (joined by NCCU Jazz Studies Director Artie Wiggins), Public Safety Communications Officers Week, and Earth Day (April 19, 2008). Council members also recognized promoted Durham Police officers and memorialized pioneering physician Dr. Robert Dawson and a prominent 99-year-old Durham businessman.

agenda_items.title: City Manager and City Attorney Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager referred Item 22 (East Deck facade treatment) back to administration, moved Item 37 (City Code recodification and fee schedule) to public hearing, and introduced supplemental Items 39 (Workforce Development Board) and 40 (Durham–Raleigh Long Range Transportation Plan revenue element), prompting Council Member Howard Clement III to caution that DATA transit funding must not be jeopardized. Council approved the manager's priority items 7-0, and the City Attorney briefed Council on raising the recommended local auto license tax addition to $10 and opposing NC Senate Bill 1180 in Item 1.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members requested Thursday work-session updates on drought-stage enforcement, uniform Triangle drought standards, the water-saving toilet program, and youth dropout prevention. Council then voted 7-0 to adopt the consent agenda, including the 2008 legislative program (Item 1), Operations Breakthrough weatherization (Item 16), the FY 2008–09 Annual Action Plan hearing schedule (Item 20), taxicab permit revocation appeals (Item 30), water treatment reliability improvements (Item 31), East Durham Outfalls Phase 3 (Item 32), and the county sustainability interlocal agreement (Item 38).

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented TC07-20, requested by Public Works Engineering to revise UDO Section 12.4 so the Public Works Director can grant sidewalk requirement variations for safe pedestrian walkways and federal ADA compliance, noting an 11-0 Planning Commission recommendation on February 12. No public speakers appeared, and Council approved the amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Recodifying the City Code and Adopting the Fee Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant City Attorney Richard Whelhouse presented the City Code recodification and fee schedule public hearing. With no members of the public wishing to speak, Council closed the hearing and approved the ordinance 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Reinstatement of Durham Workforce Development Board Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained that Item 39 corrected a reporting error affecting Durham Workforce Development Board members. Council approved the reinstatement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: City of Durham and City of Raleigh Long Range Transportation Plan Revenue Element Grant Project Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Just before adjournment, Council took up supplemental Item 40—the joint Durham–Raleigh Long Range Transportation Plan revenue element grant project ordinance—and passed it 7-0.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 17, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council presented proclamations for Black Marriage Day (March 30) and the annual Senator Jeanne Hopkins Lucas Day (March 17), commended Police Chief Jose Lopez and homicide detectives for recent arrests, and discussed violent-crime bond levels and criminal-justice coordination ahead of an April 8 courthouse briefing on the Atwater/Lovette homicide investigation. After the City Manager referred Item 15 (City Code recodification/fee booklet) back to administration and a truncated middle portion, Council divided 4-3 on adopting the first phase of development/impact fee increases: proponents argued the phase-in was a reasonable compromise keeping Durham competitive with Raleigh and Cary while funding infrastructure, whereas Mayor Bill Bell opposed acting that night before demonstrating development-review improvements to the public. The first-phase fee motion passed 4-3, with Ayes from Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Farad Ali and Nays from Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Howard Clement III. Council then voted 7-0 on four items: approving zoning map change Z07-46 to align design guidelines with an approved development plan (Item 33), adopting UDO Technical Change 4 TC07-13 (Item 34), approving the Equal Business Opportunity Program consent item after public comment from Victoria Peterson (Item 18), and accepting a Walmart crime-fighting donation while referring Peterson's research request to staff (Item 24); the Clerk also reported that Anna Brannley received 4 ballot votes for the DPAC Oversight Committee (individual ballot votes were not read aloud).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Proclamations, and Homicide / Criminal Justice Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell convened the meeting at 7:03 p.m. with all seven members present and presented proclamations for Black Marriage Day (accepted by Paula Norman-Sherman of Union Baptist Church) and Senator Jeanne Hopkins Lucas Day. Police Chief Jose Lopez praised investigators on recent homicide cases, and Mayor Bell and Council Member Howard Clement III discussed raising Superior Court second-degree murder bond guidelines from $100,000 to $600,000, juvenile-to-adult justice communication gaps, and an April 8 courthouse report by NC Department of Correction leadership on the Atwater/Lovette case.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested referring Item 15 (City Code recodification and fee booklet) back to the administration while staff continued working with the City Attorney, and began a water supply update noting significant recent watershed rainfall before middle transcript truncation.

agenda_items.title: Debate and Vote on First-Phase Development / Impact Fee Increase
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated adopting the first phase of development/impact fee increases after staff dialogue with homebuilders and comparison showing most Durham fees remained below Raleigh and Cary (with Cary also raising fees in July 2008). Council Member Eugene Brown signaled support as a cost of doing business, whereas Mayor Bill Bell argued for waiting two to three weeks until staff could publicly demonstrate substantial development-review reforms; the motion passed 4-3 with Clement, Cole-McFadden, and Bell voting No.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Design Guideline Revisions (Z07-46)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Scott Whiteman presented Z07-46 to revise design guidelines so they match the height and densities already permitted by the approved development plan, noting a 9-2 Planning Commission recommendation on February 12. agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson spoke for two minutes on the Equal Business Opportunity Program ordinance. The City Attorney advised that civil rights attorneys had drafted Durham's ordinance as strongly as legally permissible, though management was considering a future study; Council approved Item 18 by a 7-0 vote.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson urged using corporate crime-fighting donations to fund research into why young African American men repeatedly enter the criminal justice system. Mayor Bell referred the research question to the City Manager and City Attorney, and Council approved accepting the Walmart donation 7-0.

disagreements.issue: First-Phase Development / Impact Fee Increase Timing and Development Review Reform
disagreements.summary: Council split 4-3 over whether to enact the first phase of development/impact fee increases immediately after staff consultations with homebuilders or wait two to three weeks until development-review reforms could be demonstrated to the public.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the first phase of fee increases now as a reasonable compromise aligned with neighboring jurisdictions.
side_a_arguments: Staff engaged in extensive dialogue with the development community and structured a two-phase compromise.
Fee comparisons showed most Durham fees remained lower than Raleigh and Cary (with Cary also increasing fees in July 2008), representing a normal cost of doing business.
disagreements.side_b_position: Delay imposing the fee increase until substantial improvements in the development review process are completed and shown to the public.
side_b_arguments: Mayor Bill Bell argued it was not legally critical to adopt the fees that night rather than two or three weeks later.
Imposing higher fees before publicly demonstrating meaningful development-review improvements created poor public relations and risked unresolved business-community concerns.
disagreements.resolution: Council passed the first-phase fee motion 4-3, with Howard Clement III, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Bill Bell voting No.

disagreements.issue: Flag-Lot Layout Policy in Zoning Map Change Z07-44 (Item 26)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 5-2 over approving zoning map change Z07-44 after Council Member Mike Woodard criticized the applicant's intended flag-lot layout off Hickory Nut Drive.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the straight rezoning request based on comprehensive plan consistency and UDO standards.
side_a_arguments: Planning staff recommended approval as consistent with the comprehensive plan and noted no subdivision plan was yet before Council.
Staff explained flag-lotting is an existing alternate lotting provision under the UDO for limited frontage situations.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the rezoning because it facilitates an undesirable flag-lot configuration.
side_b_arguments: Council Member Mike Woodard argued a flag lot with a house facing away from the street along the flagpole portion is bad policy and made the rezoning request untenable.
Without converting the 30-foot corridor to an approved public or private street, legal frontage remained constrained to Hickory Nut Drive.
disagreements.resolution: Item 26 passed 5-2, with Eugene Brown explicitly recorded voting No and the second Nay voter's name garbled in the automated transcript following Mike Woodard's opposition.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 18, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council presented proclamations honoring incoming NCCU Chancellor Charlie Nelms, HIV/AIDS awareness, and the 50th anniversary of the Durham Human Relations Commission (originating in 1958), and heard results of the 2007 employee Seven Stars campaign. In the City Manager's water supply update, staff reported a 30-day average draw of 19.06 million gallons per day (21.47 MGD excluding Cary interconnections), prompting Council discussion of drought-resistant city policies and rain barrel programs ahead of a Thursday work session. Following a truncated middle section and continuation of Item 33 (Time Warner public access cable agreement, including debate over keeping public access on the lower tier versus funding $400,000+ in annual production operations after state franchising changes), all five recorded votes passed unanimously 7-0: Council directed staff to bring land-development and construction drought-response ordinance amendments to Thursday's work session (Item 31), approved initial zonings for Glenview Station (Item 22, Z07-30A), Jordan at Southpoint (Item 23, Z06-51A), and Steel Blue / JT Properties (Item 24, Z07-33A), and adopted pulled Consent Item 11 before adjourning.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 4, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council recognized the Bull City Gymnastics competitive team and Teens Against Alcohol Consumption, welcomed the interim City Attorney, and heard a water supply update showing Lake Michie and Little River had recovered to 33 percent capacity (up from 11 percent in December 2007) alongside an 11.3 percent year-over-year water-use reduction in January 2008. All four recorded votes passed unanimously 7-0: Council approved the consent agenda excluding pulled Item 15 (Time Warner Road Runner Internet Service), approved the 25-acre Washington Terrace rezoning along NC-55 at Riddle Road after neighbor Charles Gooch conditionally supported it based on a second driveway access route (Z07-03), adopted a UDO conservation subdivision technical text amendment aligning open-space standards with state law (Item 20, TC07-16), and voted to hold pulled Consent Item 15 at least through Thursday's work session amid Council frustration with Time Warner's handling of local public-access church programming and a 5.9 percent rate increase. During the FY 2008–2009 budget public hearing (Item 18), Victoria Peterson also raised questions regarding city building leases and work-session attendance.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Ceremonial Recognitions, and Water Supply Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell convened the meeting at 7:01 p.m. with all seven members present and welcomed the interim City Attorney. Council Member Diane Catotti and Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden recognized the Bull City Gymnastics team and Teens Against Alcohol Consumption, and the City Manager reported Lake Michie and Little River had reached 33% capacity with an 11.3% January conservation reduction while advancing Cary water interconnections.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Item 15)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to approve the consent agenda excluding Item 15 (Time Warner Road Runner Internet Service), covering a TW Alexander annexation technical correction, minutes, 2007 election results, DPAC Oversight Committee re-advertisement, HOME consortium extension, streetscape design services, regional urban search-and-rescue MOA amendment, domestic violence community court contract, Driver Street railroad crossing gates, and water compliance engineering.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Fiscal Year 2008–2009 Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Budget Director Johnson opened the public hearing on the proposed FY 2008–2009 budget. Victoria Peterson criticized city building-lease costs and Council attendance at work sessions (prompting a response from Council Member Howard Clement III), and asked when Holton School would be ready, before a brief truncated segment.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change — Washington Terrace (Z07-03)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Planning Director Steve Medlin presented Case Z07-03 by Dearly Investments LLC to rezone two parcels (~25 acres) on NC-55 south of Riddle Road from IP and RU-5 to Light Industrial (IL) with a Northeast Creek greenway trail easement, noting a 9-3 Planning Commission recommendation. Resident Charles Gooch and proponent George Stancil spoke, with Gooch stating he withdrew opposition after securing agreement for a second driveway access; Council approved the rezoning 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment — Conservation Subdivision Technical Change (TC07-16)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Planning Director Steve Medlin presented TC07-16 amending UDO Section 6.2.4 so purpose and primary/secondary conservation open-space considerations are explicitly designated as evaluation standards as required by recent state law, following a 12-0 Planning Commission recommendation. No public speakers appeared, and Council approved the amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 15: Time Warner Road Runner Internet Service
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Robin James-Foley supported approving the Road Runner internet bid over a cost-prohibitive satellite alternative while raising concerns about state cable franchising and Time Warner's treatment of public-access church broadcasts. Council members and the City Manager expressed frustration over Time Warner continuing disputed channel actions and raising rates an average of 5.9%, and Council voted 7-0 to hold Item 15 at least through Thursday's work session.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 22, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, the Council voted 6-0 to excuse Council Member Farad Ali, leaving six seated members present throughout the session. Mayor Bell delivered the annual State of the City address—broadcast for the first time with closed captioning—highlighting downtown revitalization and the Durham Performing Arts Center (scheduled to open November 2008), Durham Housing Authority HOPE VI construction, inner-city neighborhood revitalization, stricter pre-trial bond policies for gun offenses and nuisance property accountability, and urgent drought response measures including 193 days of water supply, Teer Quarry and Cary water interconnections, a proposed July 1, 2008 tiered water rate structure, and referral of the Planning Commission's Water Resources Resolution to the February 21 work session. Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, Council unanimously approved (6-0) a neighborhood revitalization public hearing item, approved (6-0) Zoning Map Change 2K07-25 (Finsbury Phase II) after the applicant proffered a 50-foot right-of-way reservation for the future Triangle Parkway, and unanimously adopted (6-0) companion East Durham street renamings (Items 26 and 27) aligning Conover Road and Windham Drive. No split or contested votes occurred during the meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Excusal of Council Member Farad Ali
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order, led a moment of silent meditation, and asked Council Member Howard Clement III to lead the Pledge of Allegiance. The City Clerk called the roll, confirming six members present (Mayor Bell, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, and Council Members Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Howard Clement III, and Mike Woodard) and noting that Council Member Farad Ali requested to be excused. Council voted 6-0 to excuse Council Member Ali.

agenda_items.title: Mayor's State of the City Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell delivered the State of the City address—highlighting the debut of closed captioning on Durham Government TV and the City website—and reviewed downtown public-private partnerships, the Durham Performing Arts Center topping-out milestone, and Durham Housing Authority HOPE VI multifamily and homeownership construction. He emphasized drought mitigation with 193 days of water supply remaining, expediting Teer Quarry storage, Jordan Lake intake options, a second Cary interconnection, aging pipe repairs, moving toward a tiered water rate structure by July 1, 2008, and reviewing the Planning Commission's January 8, 2008 Water Resources Resolution at the February 21 work session. Mayor Bell also recognized second-grade students for water conservation pledges, prioritized revitalization in Northeast and Southwest Central Durham, and called for tougher pre-trial bond restrictions on gun-crime defendants and stronger nuisance-property enforcement, followed by Council discussion of water supply projections.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Downtown-Bordering Neighborhood Revitalization and Rehabilitation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, a speaker concluded public comment linking neighborhood revitalization in downtown-bordering neighborhoods to public and private downtown investment. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden thanked speakers and highlighted involving local youth in housing rehabilitation efforts alongside outside volunteer groups such as World Changers. After closing the public hearing, Council voted 6-0 to approve the item.

agenda_items.title: Item 25: Zoning Map Change — Finsbury (2K07-25)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Department staff member Steve Medlin presented TMC Associates, LLC's request to rezone 7.08 undeveloped acres on the north side of Hobson Road, west of Davis Drive and east of the future Triangle Parkway, from Science Research Park (SRP) to Residential Compact with a development plan (RCD) for medium-density residential use (6–12 dwelling units per acre). Applicant representative Craig noted the site had been de-annexed from Research Triangle Park by the Board of County Commissioners in February 2007 for Finsbury Phase II, and in response to Council concern over future taxpayer right-of-way acquisition costs, proffered a committed element reserving up to 50 feet of additional right-of-way for the North Carolina Turnpike Authority at the applicant's cost. Council voted 6-0 to approve the rezoning.

agenda_items.title: Item 26: Street Renaming — Conover Road to Windham Drive (070003)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a request submitted by Horvath Associates on behalf of Sharon Road Ventures LLC to rename an approximately 307-foot segment of Conover Road extending from Bookman Street in East Durham (part of the Ravenstone development) to Windham Drive to eliminate duplicate street names caused by prior street dedications and removals. Staff noted all reviewing city and public service agencies found no issues and recommended approval. No members of the public spoke, and Council voted 6-0 to approve the renaming.

agenda_items.title: Item 27: Street Renaming — Windham Drive to Conover Road (0704)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the companion request from Sharon Road Ventures LLC to rename a portion of Windham Drive to Conover Road so the continuous linear roadway segment carries a single consistent street name. Reviewing staff and service agencies reported no issues or adverse impacts and recommended approval. With no public speakers, Council voted 6-0 to approve the street renaming before adjourning at 8:42 p.m.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 7, 2008 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council focused heavily on severe drought water supply contingencies and Workforce Investment Act (WIA) contracting. The City Manager reported a 40 percent demand reduction and 182 days of available water supply while keeping Durham in Stage 4 mandatory conservation, and the Council voted unanimously (7-0) to add and approve Supplemental Item 31, amending the Water and Wastewater Capital Improvement Project ordinance by $3 million and authorizing a design contract up to $500,000 with Hazen and Sawyer for a second Cary interconnection to access Jordan Lake water. Council also voted 7-0 to contract with Mercer Group Inc. (up to $34,400) for executive search services for the City Manager position and approved (7-0) a City/County zoning designation item following a public hearing. On pulled Consent Items 10, 11, and 12—covering WIA amendments with General Management Solutions, Inc., Community Partnerships, Inc., and the 2007–2009 Employment and Training Grant Project Ordinance—speaker Ms. Peterson criticized Workforce Development Board quorum rates, non-competitive awards, and youth employment/GED outcomes, but Council unanimously approved all three items (7-0) after staff clarified youth GED progression targets and improved state monitoring results. No split or contested Council votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, National Mentoring Month Proclamation, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order, led a moment of silent meditation, and had Council Member Howard Clement III lead the Pledge of Allegiance before the Clerk confirmed all seven members were present. Mayor Bell presented a National Mentoring Month proclamation to Durham Companions, and Council remarks congratulated a News & Observer Tar Heel of the Year honoree and thanked Gayle and Ernie Mills for their Christmas Eve luncheon at the Rescue Mission.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item: Supplemental Item 31 Placement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager introduced Supplemental Agenda Item 31 (Cary Interconnection Engineering Design Services), explaining that bringing a second interconnection with Cary online by early to mid-summer would add roughly 4.5 million gallons per day of water supply for Durham. Council voted 7-0 to accept the City Manager's priority item onto the agenda for immediate consideration.

agenda_items.title: Water Supply Status and Drought Conservation Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager reported that mandatory water restrictions enacted in September had achieved a 40 percent reduction in demand and that total available supply stood at 182 days—including 1.2 billion gallons (64 days) of treatable water below the Little River and Lake Michie intakes—while keeping Stage 4 severe mandatory conservation in place because reservoirs remained several feet below full. He noted ongoing expansion of the existing Cary interconnection from 2 million gallons per day toward 7 million gallons per day from Jordan Lake allocation and indicated staff would address Council billing structure and debt service questions at Thursday's work session.

agenda_items.title: Legislative Town Hall Announcement and City Manager Executive Search Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On Item 1 (2008 Legislative Program Short Session), Mayor Bell announced a January 29, 2008 town hall at 4:00 p.m. in City Hall's second-floor committee room with Senators Marc Basnight and Floyd McKissick, and noted an earlier closed session would continue to January 16 at 5:00 p.m. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved to contract with Mercer Group Inc. for executive search services for the City Manager position in an amount not to exceed $34,400, which passed 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Overview (Items 2–12; Items 10, 11, and 12 Pulled)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent agenda items including Council minutes (Item 2), the FY 2008–2009 Annual Action Plan public hearing (Item 3), a major site plan for a parking lot (D05-572, Item 4), petition improvement public hearings (Item 5), street exceptions (Item 6), a mortgage buyback agreement with Durham County Habitat for Humanity (Item 8), and a Durham Crisis Response Center subrecipient amendment (Item 9). Items 10, 11, and 12 (Workforce Investment Act and Employment and Training grant amendments) were pulled for separate consideration; remaining bulk consent votes occurred within the truncated portion of the transcript.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: City/County Zoning Designations Item

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 17, 2007 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council presented a Bill of Rights Day resolution and received a severe drought update from the City Manager. Staff reported a 36 percent demand reduction since September mandatory restrictions and approximately 59 days of remaining supply in Little River and Lake Michie, with temporary pumping from Teer Quarry starting within 10 days alongside efforts to expand Cary and OWASA interconnections to access Durham's Jordan Lake allocation. The Council unanimously referred a two-thirds bond reimbursement resolution (Item 13) and historic landmark designations (Items 26-35) back to the administration (7-0) and unanimously approved a South Durham conservation subdivision annexation item (7-0) after staff confirmed substantial compliance with proposed UDO specimen-tree amendments. Following questions from Council Member Farad Ali on project budget and lender payment assignments, the Council also unanimously approved the Durham City Center parking deck redevelopment agreement (Item 43, 7-0) and passed three pulled consent items (Items 12, 15, and 47, 7-0). No split or contested votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Ceremonial Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m., Council Member Howard Clement III led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven seated Council members were recorded present. Mayor Bell presented a Bill of Rights Day resolution to Joan Walsh and members of the Bill of Rights Committee reaffirming Durham's 2003 Bill of Rights and immigrant rights resolutions, as well as a proclamation recognizing Honey Baked Ham's fifth anniversary in Durham.

agenda_items.title: City Manager's Priority Items (Referral of Item 13 and Items 26-35)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested referring Agenda Item 13 (two-thirds bond reimbursement resolution, to return Thursday with a request to suspend rules) and Agenda Items 26-35 (historic landmark designations) back to the administration to resolve outstanding issues. Council unanimously approved the manager's priority referrals.

agenda_items.title: Weekly Drought and Water Supply Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager reported that the central Piedmont remained in exceptional drought, with water demand down 36 percent from September 21 levels and 10 percent below December 2006 usage. With 1.2 billion gallons below intake (~59 days supply) at Little River and Lake Michie, Durham planned to begin drawing from Teer Quarry within 10 days using a permanent tap, pursue water purchases from OWASA, expand the Cary interconnection from 2 to 4 million gallons per day by late January, add a second interconnection by early summer for 7 million gallons per day, and review potential Stage 5 restrictions in January.

agenda_items.title: South Durham Conservation Subdivision Annexation Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff clarified that the annexation financial analysis had mistakenly used a standard 'rezoning' heading when comparing baseline density to the proposed conservation subdivision density. Resident Melissa Rennie urged denial or deferral until UDO conservation subdivision amendments were adopted, objecting to power line easements counting toward 40 percent open space and clear-cutting in the Jordan Lake watershed. After staff confirmed to Council Member Diane Catotti that the project complied substantially with proposed specimen-tree protections, Council voted unanimously to approve the item.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Agenda Items 12, 15, and 47
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Three consent agenda items (Items 12, 15, and 47) that had been pulled earlier were brought forward. Because the person who pulled those items was no longer present, Council moved, seconded, and approved all three items together unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Item 43: Durham City Center Parking Deck Redevelopment Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Farad Ali questioned staff on the management fee (~$53,000), the gap between the $3,844,300 construction budget and the $4.2 million allocation, and Section 11.25 lender assignment rights. Deputy Manager Wanda Page, Assistant City Manager Alan DeLisle, and project representatives clarified that the ~$368,000 difference covered design and structural engineering visits and that Section 11.25 assigned only city cash-flow payments upon developer default rather than property collateral. Council then approved the contract unanimously.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 3, 2007 organizational and regular City Council meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Durham County Board of Elections Director Michael Ash presented the certified results of the November 6, 2007 municipal election, outgoing Council Member Thomas Stith III was recognized for his 1999-2007 service, and the newly elected Council was sworn in. The Council unanimously re-appointed Cora Cole-McFadden as Mayor Pro Tempore (7-0) and approved Mayor Bell's Council committee appointments (7-0). Later in the meeting, Council debated Item 12 (utility extension agreement) and Item 33g (annexation public hearing) amid concerns raised by Council Member Eugene Brown and others about committing water and sewer extensions during Durham's severe drought. On a split vote, Council Member Diane Catotti's substitute-to-the-substitute motion to defer both items until the January 24, 2008 work session failed 3-4, with Howard Clement III, Eugene Brown, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Bill Bell voting Nay and Diane Catotti, Mike Woodard, and Farad Ali voting Aye. The Council subsequently adopted the substitute motion deferring Item 12 to December 17 and voted unanimously (7-0) to continue the Item 33g public hearing to December 17 without additional advertising.

agenda_items.title: Certification of November 6, 2007 Municipal Election, Outgoing Recognition, and Swearing-In
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Board of Elections Director Michael Ash presented certified abstracts and election certificates from the October 9 primary and November 6, 2007 general election. Outgoing Council Member Thomas Stith III was recognized for serving from December 6, 1999 through December 3, 2007, and incoming and re-elected Council members were sworn into office, delivering remarks on gang accountability, Northeast Central Durham revitalization, and the water supply crisis.

agenda_items.title: Re-Appointment of Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell recommended re-appointing Cora Cole-McFadden as Mayor Pro Tempore, praising her dedication to Durham residents and city staff. Council approved the appointment unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Approval of City Council Committee Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented the slate of Council committee appointments and liaisons, noting an update on page three regarding the Passenger Vehicle for Hire Committee assignment. Council unanimously approved the appointments before taking a brief recess.

agenda_items.title: Items 12 & 33g: Utility Extension Agreement and Annexation Public Hearing Deferral
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members questioned whether approving a utility extension agreement and annexation could legally obligate the city to provide water and sewer service amid the ongoing drought. After Mike Woodard initially sought an open-ended deferral and the City Attorney advised coupling both items to a date certain, a substitute motion was made to defer to December 17. Diane Catotti offered a substitute-to-the-substitute motion to defer until January 24 to avoid overworking staff over the holidays, which failed 3-4; Council then approved the December 17 deferral and voted 7-0 to continue the Item 33g public hearing to December 17.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Substitute-to-substitute failed 3-4; Dec 17 deferral passed; hearing continued 7-0

disagreements.issue: Timeline for Deferring Utility Extension Agreement (Item 12) and Annexation (Item 33g) Amid Drought Review
disagreements.summary: Following concerns about whether approving annexation and utility extension agreements would obligate Durham to supply water during the drought, Council split 3-4 over whether to defer Items 12 and 33g until late January 2008 or only until December 17, 2007.
disagreements.side_a_position: Defer Items 12 and 33g until January 24, 2008 (second meeting in January)
side_a_arguments: Pressing staff to complete legal and water-obligation review by December 17 places an unnecessary burden on staff over the holidays.
A longer deferral gives staff and Council adequate time to thoroughly research drought and utility obligations.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer Items 12 and 33g only until December 17, 2007
side_b_arguments: Further delay past December 17 imposes additional financial costs on the applicant, who specifically offered December 17 to try to preserve a December 31 effective date for tax assessment.
Staff and the City Attorney indicated December 17 was achievable and the item could be deferred again then if review remained incomplete.
disagreements.resolution: The January 24 deferral substitute-to-the-substitute motion failed 3-4, after which Council adopted the December 17 deferral and voted 7-0 to continue the Item 33g public hearing to December 17.
